tools.name: start_google_auth
tools.description:
Manually initiate Google OAuth authentication flow.

NOTE: This tool should typically NOT be called directly. The authentication system
automatically handles credential checks and prompts for authentication when needed.
Only use this tool if:
1. You need to re-authenticate with different credentials
2. You want to proactively authenticate before using other tools
3. The automatic authentication flow failed and you need to retry

In most cases, simply try calling the Google Workspace tool you need - it will
automatically handle authentication if required.

Args:
    service_name: Name of the Google service (default: "Gmail")
    user_google_email: Optional user's Google email address. If not provided,
                      the user will be prompted to provide it after authentication.

Returns:
    A formatted message with authentication instructions and URL.

tools.name: start_gmail_auth
tools.description: Start OAuth flow for Gmail scopes.

tools.name: exchange_gmail_connector_code
tools.description:
Exchange and store a Gmail OAuth code from the Phoenix PC local callback.

This tool is used when Gmail authorization redirects to the PC local gateway
instead of the MCP public callback. The MCP server performs the code exchange
and persists credentials in the same store used by normal Google callbacks.

tools.name: start_google_calendar_auth
tools.description:
Initiate OAuth authorization for Google Calendar via Pipedream Connect.

**When to call:**
Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Google Calendar account
through Pipedream, enabling calendar event listing, creation, updating, and
other Calendar operations via the Pipedream API Proxy.

**Parameters:**
None. The tool automatically identifies the current user (accio_id).

**Returns:**
A JSON string with:
  - authUrl: The authorization URL to present to the user. The user must
    open this link in a browser to complete Google Calendar authorization.
  - expiresAt: ISO 8601 timestamp when the authorization link expires
    (typically 4 hours).

**Usage:**
Present the authUrl to the user as a clickable Markdown link. Example:
  "Please click [here](authUrl) to authorize Google Calendar access."
After the user completes authorization, the account credentials are
automatically stored and available for subsequent Google Calendar operations.

tools.name: start_google_drive_auth
tools.description:
Initiate OAuth authorization for Google Drive via Pipedream Connect.

**When to call:**
Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Google Drive account
through Pipedream, enabling file listing, reading, uploading, and other
Drive operations via the Pipedream API Proxy.

**Parameters:**
None. The tool automatically identifies the current user (accio_id).

**Returns:**
A JSON string with:
  - authUrl: The authorization URL to present to the user. The user must
    open this link in a browser to complete Google Drive authorization.
  - expiresAt: ISO 8601 timestamp when the authorization link expires
    (typically 4 hours).

**Usage:**
Present the authUrl to the user as a clickable Markdown link. Example:
  "Please click [here](authUrl) to authorize Google Drive access."
After the user completes authorization, the account credentials are
automatically stored and available for subsequent Google Drive operations.

tools.name: start_twitter_auth
tools.description:
Authorize a user's X (Twitter) account for the current workspace.

Each workspace (accio_id) can bind exactly one X account. After authorization,
Twitter tools in this workspace will run as that X account.

**WHEN TO CALL**

Only call this tool in these cases:
  1. First time the user wants to use Twitter tools and this workspace has no
     X credential yet.
  2. A Twitter tool **explicitly** returned `unauthorized` / `token_invalid` /
     a `401 Unauthorized` HTTP error AND the user agreed to re-authorize.
  3. The user explicitly asked to switch to a different X account
     (re-authorization).

**WHEN NOT TO CALL — IMPORTANT**

Do NOT call this tool when a Twitter tool returns `403 Forbidden`.
`403 from Twitter ≠ token expired`. A 403 means the action needs a permission
or X plan you don't have (e.g. liking, following, posting from a free-tier
project). Re-authorizing **will not fix it** — the new token will have the
same scope and the next call will 403 again, creating a frustrating loop for
the user. Instead, tell the user the action is restricted and stop.

**IDEMPOTENT**

If the workspace already has a healthy X credential, this tool will detect
that and return an `already connected` message *without* generating a new
OAuth link, so accidentally calling it does not force the user to re-authorize.

Returns:
    Either a markdown message containing the authorization link to share
    with the user, or a markdown message saying the workspace is already
    connected (so you can proceed directly with other Twitter tools).

tools.name: list_all_authorizations

tools.name: start_github_auth
tools.description: Start GitHub OAuth authorization flow.

tools.name: exchange_github_connector_code
tools.description:
Exchange and store a GitHub OAuth code from the Phoenix PC local callback.

This tool is used when GitHub authorization redirects to the PC local gateway

tools.name: manage_github_org_access
tools.description:
Manage GitHub organization access for the connected OAuth App.

Use this tool when:
- The user recently joined a new GitHub organization and needs to grant
  the OAuth App access to it.
- An org-scoped operation (list org repos, create repo under org, fork
  to org) returns 403 because the OAuth App has not been granted access
  to that organization.
- The user wants to review or revoke organization-level access.

Re-running start_github_auth does NOT help here — GitHub skips the
organization selection screen when the user has already authorized the
app. This tool returns a direct link to the GitHub settings page where
the user can grant or revoke per-organization access.

tools.name: start_linkedin_auth
tools.description: Start LinkedIn OAuth authorization flow.

tools.name: start_notion_auth
tools.description:
发起 Notion OAuth 2.0 授权流程。

Returns:
    包含授权链接的指引消息。

tools.name: set_notion_token
tools.description:
Set or update Notion Integration Token for a user.

This tool stores the Notion Integration Token for a specific user,
allowing them to access their Notion workspace through the MCP server.

To get a Notion Integration Token:
1. Visit https://www.notion.so/my-integrations
2. Create a new integration or use an existing one
3. Copy the "Internal Integration Token" (usually starts with "secret_" or "ntn_")
4. Share the pages/databases you want to access with the integration

Args:
    user_id: User identifier (email or custom ID)
    token: Notion Integration Token (must start with "secret_" or "ntn_")
    
Returns:
    Success or error message
    
Example:
    set_notion_token(
        user_id="user@example.com",
        token="ntn_1234567890abcdef..."
    )

tools.name: check_notion_token
tools.description:
Check the status of a user's Notion Integration Token.

This tool checks if a token exists for the user and verifies its validity.
It does NOT expose the actual token value.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier (email or custom ID)
    
Returns:
    Token status information
    
Example:
    check_notion_token(user_id="user@example.com")

tools.name: delete_notion_token
tools.description:
Delete a user's Notion Integration Token.

This tool removes the stored token for a user. After deletion,
the user will need to set a new token to use Notion tools.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier (email or custom ID)
    
Returns:
    Success or error message
    
Example:
    delete_notion_token(user_id="user@example.com")

tools.name: list_notion_token_users
tools.description:
List all users with stored Notion Integration Tokens.

This tool shows which users have configured Notion tokens.
It does NOT expose the actual token values.

Returns:
    List of user IDs with tokens
    
Example:
    list_notion_token_users()

tools.name: search_notion_workspace
tools.description:
Search pages and databases in the user's Notion workspace.

**When to call**: The user wants to find a specific page, database, or
keyword inside their Notion workspace.  Also useful as a first step to
discover page/database IDs for subsequent operations.

Args:
    query:    Free-text search term.  Empty string returns recent items.
    filter_type: ``"page"`` or ``"database"`` to narrow results.
                 Omit to search both.
    page_size: Number of results to return (1–100, default 10).
    start_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous response's
                  ``next_cursor`` field.

Returns:
    **Success** — human-readable summary + JSON list of matching objects
    with ``id``, ``title``, ``url``, ``object`` (page/database).

    **Failure** — single-line error reason + actionable guidance.

Example:
    search_notion_workspace(query="Q3 OKR")
    search_notion_workspace(filter_type="database")

tools.name: get_notion_page_content
tools.description:
Retrieve a Notion page's properties and (optionally) its content blocks.

**When to call**: The user wants to read a specific page — its title,
properties, and body content.  Use after ``search_notion_workspace`` to
inspect a page found by search.

Args:
    page_id:  (required) The Notion page ID (UUID, with or without dashes).
    include_children: Whether to also fetch the page's block children
                      (default ``True``).  Set to ``False`` if you only
                      need the page metadata/properties.
    children_page_size: Max number of child blocks to return (1–100,
                        default 50).

Returns:
    **Success** — page properties + child blocks in JSON.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    get_notion_page_content(page_id="abc123...")

tools.name: create_notion_page
tools.description:
Create a new page (note) in the user's Notion workspace.

**When to call**: The user wants to create a new note, page, or document
in Notion.  Supports creating a page under an existing page or inside a
database.

Args:
    title:   Page title (required).
    parent_page_id: ID of a parent page.  The new page will be created
                    as a sub-page.  Mutually exclusive with
                    ``parent_database_id``.  If neither is provided, the
                    page is created at the **workspace top level**.
    parent_database_id: ID of a database to add a new entry to.
                        Mutually exclusive with ``parent_page_id``.
    content:  Plain text content for the page body.  Automatically
              converted to paragraph blocks.  Ignored when ``children``
              is provided.
    children: Raw Notion block objects for the page body.  Overrides
              ``content`` when both are provided.

Returns:
    **Success** — summary + JSON with ``page_id``, ``title``, ``url``.

    **Failure** — error reason + actionable guidance.

Example:
    create_notion_page(title="Meeting Notes")
    create_notion_page(
        title="Sprint Review",
        content="Key takeaways from today's sprint review."
    )
    create_notion_page(
        title="Sub Page",
        parent_page_id="abc123...",
    )

tools.name: update_notion_page_properties
tools.description:
Update properties of an existing Notion page.

**When to call**: The user wants to change a page's title, status,
assignee, date, or any other property.  Also use ``archived=True``
to soft-delete a page.

Args:
    page_id:    (required) Notion page ID to update.
    properties: (required) A dict mapping property names to their new
                values, following the Notion API property-value schema.

                Example — change title:
                ```json
                {
                  "Name": {
                    "title": [{"text": {"content": "New Title"}}]
                  }
                }
                ```

                Example — set a select property:
                ```json
                {
                  "Status": {"select": {"name": "Done"}}
                }
                ```
    archived:   Set to ``True`` to archive (soft-delete) the page, or
                ``False`` to un-archive.  Omit to leave unchanged.

Returns:
    **Success** — confirmation + updated page JSON.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    update_notion_page_properties(
        page_id="abc123...",
        properties={"Status": {"select": {"name": "In Progress"}}}
    )

tools.name: append_notion_blocks
delete_notion_block
tools.description:
Delete (archive) a block from a Notion page.

**When to call**: The user wants to remove a specific block (paragraph,
heading, to-do, etc.) from a page.  The block is soft-deleted (archived)
and can be recovered via the Notion UI.

Use ``get_notion_page_content`` first to discover block IDs.

Args:
    block_id: (required) The Notion block ID to delete.

Returns:
    **Success** — confirmation with the deleted block ID.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    delete_notion_block(block_id="block-uuid-here")

tools.name: get_notion_database
tools.description:
Retrieve a Notion database's schema (title, properties and their types).

**When to call**: The user wants to understand the structure of a database
before querying it — e.g. what columns/properties exist, their types,
and available select/status options.  This is the recommended first step
before calling ``query_notion_database``.

Args:
    database_id: (required) The Notion database ID (UUID).

Returns:
    **Success** — database title, property schema, and URL in JSON.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    get_notion_database(database_id="abc123...")

tools.name: query_notion_database
tools.description:
Query a Notion database with optional filters and sorts.

**When to call**: The user wants to list, filter, or sort entries in a
Notion database (e.g. "show me all tasks assigned to me", "list open
bugs sorted by priority").  Use ``get_notion_database`` first to
discover the available properties and their types.

Args:
    database_id: (required) The Notion database ID (UUID).
    filter_obj:  Notion filter object following the
                 `Notion filter API schema <https://developers.notion.com/reference/post-database-query-filter>`_.

                 Example — filter by status:
                 ```json
                 {
                   "property": "Status",
                   "status": {"equals": "In Progress"}
                 }
                 ```
    sorts:       List of sort objects.

                 Example — sort by created time descending:
                 ```json
                 [{"timestamp": "created_time", "direction": "descending"}]
                 ```
    page_size:   Number of results (1–100, default 20).
    start_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous ``next_cursor``.

Returns:
    **Success** — summary + JSON list of database entries with their
    properties.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    query_notion_database(database_id="abc123...")
    query_notion_database(
        database_id="abc123...",
        filter_obj={"property": "Status", "status": {"equals": "Done"}},
        sorts=[{"property": "Due Date", "direction": "ascending"}],
    )

tools.name: add_notion_comment
tools.description:
Add a comment to a Notion page and optionally read existing comments.

**When to call**: The user wants to leave a comment/note on a page,
or wants to see what comments already exist before adding one.
Set ``read_existing=True`` to fetch the comment thread first.

Args:
    page_id:       (required) Notion page ID to comment on.
    comment_text:  (required) Plain-text content of the new comment.
    read_existing: If ``True``, retrieve existing comments *before*
                   posting the new one (default ``False``).
    read_page_size: Number of existing comments to fetch (1–100,
                    default 20).  Only used when ``read_existing=True``.

Returns:
    **Success** — confirmation of the posted comment (+ existing
    comments if ``read_existing`` was ``True``).

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    add_notion_comment(
        page_id="abc...",
        comment_text="Looks good — approved!",
        read_existing=True,
    )

tools.name: get_notion_comments
tools.description:
Retrieve all comments on a Notion page.

**When to call**: The user wants to read existing comments/discussion
on a page without adding a new comment.  Use this for reviewing
feedback, audit trails, or conversation history on a page.

Args:
    page_id:      (required) The Notion page ID whose comments to read.
    page_size:    Number of comments to return (1–100, default 50).
    start_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous ``next_cursor``.

Returns:
    **Success** — summary + JSON list of comments with ``id``,
    ``created_time``, ``text``, and ``created_by``.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    get_notion_comments(page_id="abc123...")
    get_notion_comments(page_id="abc123...", page_size=10)

tools.name: list_notion_users
tools.description:
List users in the Notion workspace.

**When to call**: The user wants to see who has access to the workspace,
look up a person's user ID for assigning tasks or filtering by "People"
properties, or verify integration bot identity.

Args:
    page_size:    Number of users to return (1–100, default 50).
    start_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous ``next_cursor``.

Returns:
    **Success** — summary + JSON list of users with ``id``, ``name``,
    ``type`` (person/bot), and ``avatar_url``.

    **Failure** — error reason + guidance.

Example:
    list_notion_users()
    list_notion_users(page_size=10)

tools.name: start_vercel_auth
tools.description:
Start Vercel OAuth authorization flow.

NOTE: This tool should typically NOT be called directly. The authentication
system automatically prompts the user when a Vercel tool is invoked without
valid credentials. Only use this tool when the user explicitly asks to (re)connect
a Vercel account, or when the automatic flow has failed and we need to retry.

Returns:
    A human-readable message containing the Vercel authorize URL. The link
    must be opened in a browser by the end user to complete authorization.

tools.name: exchange_vercel_connector_code
tools.description:
Exchange and store a Vercel OAuth code from the Phoenix PC local callback.

Used when Vercel authorization redirects to the PC local gateway
(``http://127.0.0.1:4097/mcp/vercel/callback``) instead of the MCP public
callback. The MCP server performs the code exchange and persists credentials
in the same store used by normal Vercel callbacks.

Args:
    code: ``code`` query param returned by Vercel.
    state: ``state`` query param returned by Vercel; must be the value we issued.
    redirect_uri: optional override; defaults to PC local gateway URL.
    team_id: optional, only present in Vercel Integration mode.
    configuration_id: optional, only present in Vercel Integration mode.

Returns:
    JSON string with ``ok`` flag plus credential summary or failure detail.

tools.name: get_vercel_user_profile
tools.description:
Return the connected Vercel account profile (id, email, name, username).

Use this tool to verify the OAuth connection works, or when the user asks
"which Vercel account am I connected to?".

Args: none.

Returns:
    Human-readable text plus a JSON snippet containing
    ``{ user_id, user_email, user_name, username, team_id }``.
    On failure: a single line beginning with ``❌`` and a remediation hint.

tools.name: list_vercel_projects
tools.description:
List Vercel projects accessible by the connected account.

Call this when the user wants to see what projects exist on their Vercel
account, or before deeper actions like inspecting a deployment.

Args:
    limit: page size (Vercel max 100). Default 20.
    search: optional case-insensitive substring filter on project name.
    team_id: optional Vercel team id; defaults to the team bound at OAuth time.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet ``{ "count": N, "projects": [{id,name,framework,updatedAt,...}] }``.
    Failure: single ``❌`` line with hint.

tools.name: get_vercel_project
tools.description:
Get full Vercel project detail (env count, framework, latest deployment summary).

Call this when the user asks "show me details of project X" or after
``list_vercel_projects`` to drill into a single project.

Args:
    project_id_or_name: Vercel project ``id`` (``prj_xxx``) or human-readable ``name``.
    team_id: optional team id override.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet with the full project object (trimmed).
    Failure: single ``❌`` line with hint.

tools.name: list_vercel_deployments
tools.description:
List recent Vercel deployments (filterable by project / state / target).

Use this when the user asks "show me recent deployments" or "did my last
deployment succeed". Pair with ``get_vercel_deployment`` for details.

Args:
    project_id: optional Vercel ``project_id`` (``prj_xxx``); empty lists across all projects.
    limit: page size (Vercel max 100). Default 20.
    state: optional filter, one of ``BUILDING|ERROR|INITIALIZING|QUEUED|READY|CANCELED``.
    target: optional filter, one of ``production|preview``.
    team_id: optional team id override.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet
    ``{ "count": N, "deployments": [{uid,url,state,target,createdAt,projectId,creator,...}] }``.
    Failure: single ``❌`` line with hint.

tools.name: get_vercel_deployment
tools.description:
Get a single Vercel deployment's full detail (state, build duration, alias, error info).

Use this after ``list_vercel_deployments`` when the user wants to dig into
a specific deployment, e.g. to confirm whether a build succeeded.

Args:
    deployment_id_or_url: Vercel ``deployment id`` (``dpl_xxx``) or deployment URL
        (e.g. ``my-app-xxxx.vercel.app``).
    team_id: optional team id override.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet with the trimmed deployment object.
    Failure: single ``❌`` line with hint.

tools.name: get_vercel_deployment_logs
tools.description:
Fetch build/runtime log events for a Vercel deployment.

Use this when the user asks "why did my deployment fail" or "show the build
logs". Returns a normalized snapshot — for live tailing, call again.

Args:
    deployment_id: Vercel deployment id (``dpl_xxx``). Required.
    limit: max number of events to return (Vercel max 1000). Default 100.
    direction: ``backward`` (newest first, default) or ``forward``.
    team_id: optional team id override.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet
    ``{ "count": N, "events": [{type,created,text,level,...}] }``.
    Failure: single ``❌`` line with hint.

tools.name: start_netlify_auth
tools.description:
Start Netlify OAuth authorization flow.

Returns a human-readable message containing the Netlify authorize URL.

tools.name: exchange_netlify_connector_code

instead of the MCP public callback.

tools.name: get_netlify_user_profile

"which Netlify account am I connected to?".

tools.name: list_netlify_sites
tools.description:
List Netlify sites (projects) accessible by the connected account.

Call this when the user wants to see what sites exist on their Netlify
account, or before deeper actions like inspecting deployments.

Args:

    page: page number starting at 1.
    filter: optional filter value. Use "all" to list all sites including
        team sites, or leave empty for sites owned by the user.

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet with sites list.
    Failure: single error line with hint.

tools.name: get_netlify_site
tools.description:
Get full Netlify site detail (domains, build settings, deploy info).

Call this when the user asks "show me details of site X" or after
``list_netlify_sites`` to drill into a single site.

tools.name: list_netlify_deploys

Returns:
    Success: text + JSON snippet with deploys list.
    Failure: single error line with hint.

tools.name: get_netlify_deploy
tools.description:
Get a single Netlify deploy's full detail (state, error info, timing).

Use this after ``list_netlify_deploys`` when the user wants to dig into
a specific deploy.

Args:

tools.name: set_higgsfield_credentials

tools.name: generate_higgsfield_image
tools.description:
Generate an image using the Higgsfield AI API.

Submit an image generation request and optionally wait for the result.
Higgsfield uses an asynchronous queue — the request is queued and processed in background.

Supported models:
- "higgsfield-ai/soul/standard" — Flagship text-to-image model (default)
- "flux-pro/kontext/max/text-to-image" — FLUX.2 Pro (supports seed, negative_prompt)
- "bytedance/seedream/v4/text-to-image" — ByteDance Seedream v4 (supports 2K resolution)

Args:
    prompt: Natural language description of the image to generate.
    model_id: Model to use. Different models support different parameters.
    aspect_ratio: Image aspect ratio. Options: "1:1", "16:9", "9:16", "4:3", "3:4", "21:9", "9:21".
    resolution: Resolution. Options: "480p", "720p", "1080p", "2K", "4K".
    negative_prompt: Things to avoid in the image (if supported by model).
    seed: Random seed for reproducible results (if supported by model).
    n: Number of images to generate (if supported by model, 1-6).
    style: Reserved for future use.
    user_id: User identifier for credential lookup. Defaults to accio_id.
    wait_for_completion: If True, poll until generation completes (up to poll_timeout seconds).
                         If False, return immediately with request_id for manual polling.
    poll_interval: Seconds between status polls (when waiting).
    poll_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for completion.

Returns:
    JSON with generation result including status, request_id, and image URLs (if completed).

Example:
    # Soul model (default)
    generate_higgsfield_image(
        prompt="A futuristic city at sunset with flying cars",
        aspect_ratio="16:9",
        resolution="1080p"
    )

    # FLUX Pro model
    generate_higgsfield_image(
        prompt="A serene mountain landscape",
        model_id="flux-pro/kontext/max/text-to-image",
        aspect_ratio="16:9",
        seed=42,
        negative_prompt="blurry, low quality"
    )

tools.name: generate_higgsfield_video
tools.description:
Generate a video using the Higgsfield AI API.

Submit a video generation request and optionally wait for the result.
Video generation typically takes longer than image generation.

**Supported models** (all are image-to-video, require image):

Higgsfield DoP:
- "higgsfield-ai/dop/standard" — DoP image animation (5s/10s)
- "higgsfield-ai/dop/turbo" — DoP fast generation with priority queue
- "higgsfield-ai/dop/lite" — DoP entry-level (5s/10s)

Third-Party Models:
- "kling-video/v2.1/pro/image-to-video" — Kling 2.1 cinematic animations (5s/10s)
- "bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video" — ByteDance Seedance Pro (3-10s)

Args:
    prompt: Natural language description of the video to generate.
    image_url: URL of the source image (for single-image models).
    image_urls: List of image URLs (for multi-image models).
    model_id: Video model. Defaults to "higgsfield-ai/dop/standard".
    duration_seconds: Video duration in seconds (varies by model).
    negative_prompt: Things to avoid in the generation (if supported).
    aspect_ratio: Video aspect ratio (if supported). Options: "16:9", "9:16", "1:1", "4:3".
    resolution: Video resolution (if supported). Options: "360p", "480p", "720p", "1080p".
    quality: Video quality (if supported). Options: "basic", "medium", "high", "standard".
    camera_fixed: Lock camera, animate only subject (Seedance models).
    motion: Reserved for motion presets (not yet enabled).
    effect_name: Reserved for video effects (not yet enabled).
    user_id: User identifier for credential lookup. Defaults to accio_id.
    wait_for_completion: If True, poll until generation completes.
    poll_interval: Seconds between status polls.
    poll_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait (default 10 minutes for video).

Returns:
    JSON with generation result including status, request_id, and video URLs (if completed).

Example:
    # DoP standard
    generate_higgsfield_video(
        prompt="A stylish woman walks down a Tokyo street",
        image_url="https://example.com/photo.jpg",
        model_id="higgsfield-ai/dop/standard",
        duration_seconds=5
    )

    # DoP Turbo (faster generation)
    generate_higgsfield_video(
        prompt="Cinematic drone shot over ocean",
        image_url="https://example.com/beach.jpg",
        model_id="higgsfield-ai/dop/turbo",
        duration_seconds=10
    )

    # Kling video
    generate_higgsfield_video(
        prompt="Cinematic pan across landscape",
        image_url="https://example.com/landscape.jpg",
        model_id="kling-video/v2.1/pro/image-to-video",
        duration_seconds=10,
        quality="high"
    )

    # Seedance Pro
    generate_higgsfield_video(
        prompt="Character walks forward",
        image_url="https://example.com/portrait.jpg",
        model_id="bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video",
        duration_seconds=5,
        camera_fixed=True
    )

tools.name: get_higgsfield_generation_status
tools.description:
Get the status of a Higgsfield generation request.

Use this to check the status of a generation that was submitted with
wait_for_completion=False, or to check a previously submitted request.

Args:
    request_id: The request_id returned from a generation call.
    user_id: User identifier for credential lookup. Defaults to accio_id.

Returns:
    JSON with current status and media URLs (if completed).
    Status values: queued, in_progress, completed, failed, nsfw

Example:
    get_higgsfield_generation_status(request_id="d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff")

tools.name: cancel_higgsfield_generation
tools.description:
Cancel a queued Higgsfield generation request.

Only requests that are still in the "queued" status can be canceled.
Once processing has started ("in_progress"), cancellation is no longer possible.

Args:
    request_id: The request_id of the generation to cancel.
    user_id: User identifier for credential lookup. Defaults to accio_id.

Returns:
    JSON with cancellation result.

Example:
    cancel_higgsfield_generation(request_id="d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff")

tools.name: set_instantly_credentials
tools.description:
Set, update, or disconnect Instantly API Key for the current user.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Instantly workspace,
or when an Instantly tool returns ``INSTANTLY_MISSING_CREDENTIAL`` /
``INSTANTLY_AUTH_FAILED`` indicating credentials are missing or expired.

**How to obtain an API key:**
1. Log in to https://app.instantly.ai
2. Go to Settings → Integrations → API Keys → Create API Key.
3. Recommended scope (production): ``campaigns:all`` + ``lead_lists:all``
   + ``leads:all``. For full access (dev / power-users): ``all:all``.
4. Copy the displayed key. **The key is shown only once** — if lost it
   must be revoked and recreated.

**Disconnect:**
Pass an empty string for ``api_key`` to disconnect. The stored credential
is removed idempotently and no Instantly API verification is performed.

**Verification:**
Before storing, the credential is verified against
``GET /api/v2/workspaces/current``. On success the returned workspace
identity (id / name / owner / plan_id) is persisted with the key so
``/auth/authorizations`` can show a real workspace name.

Args:
    api_key: Instantly API key (base64 of ``<uuid>:<secret>``, ~60 chars,
        no fixed prefix). Pass empty string to disconnect.

Returns:
    - On success: a message containing "connected" along with workspace
      name and plan id.
    - On empty key: a message containing "disconnected".
    - On failure: a structured JSON error with code and message.

Example:
    set_instantly_credentials(api_key="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx==")
    set_instantly_credentials(api_key="")  # disconnect

tools.name: check_instantly_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the current user's Instantly credentials.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user asks whether Instantly is connected, or
before performing an Instantly operation to confirm auth status.

This tool checks if credentials exist and re-verifies them against
Instantly. It does NOT expose the actual API key value.

Returns:
    Credential status including validity, workspace, plan, and creation
    time.

Example:
    check_instantly_credentials()

tools.name: delete_instantly_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Instantly credentials.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to disconnect their Instantly
workspace or revoke access.

After deletion, the user will need to set new credentials to use
Instantly tools again.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_instantly_credentials()

tools.name: list_instantly_campaigns
tools.description:
List Instantly cold-outreach campaigns in the current workspace.

Args:
    limit: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 10.
    starting_after: Cursor returned as ``next_starting_after`` from the
        previous page. Omit on the first call.
    search: Case-insensitive substring match against the campaign name.

Returns:
    Markdown table of campaigns (id, name, status, created), plus a
    cursor hint when more pages are available.

tools.name: create_instantly_campaign
tools.description:
Create a new Instantly campaign.

Args:
    name: Display name of the campaign (required).
    campaign_schedule: Sending schedule object. Must contain a
        ``schedules`` array; each schedule has ``name``, ``timing``
        (``from``/``to`` HH:MM), ``days`` (mapping ``"1"``–``"7"`` →
        bool, Mon=1), and ``timezone`` (e.g. ``"Etc/GMT+0"``).
    sequences: Optional list of step objects (``[{steps: [...]}]``);
        each step contains email variants. Omit to create an empty
        campaign and add sequences later.
    email_gap: Optional integer — minutes between consecutive sends.
    text_only: Optional bool — disable HTML rendering.

Returns:
    Success line plus a JSON snapshot of the created campaign (id, name,
    status). Errors are returned as JSON payloads with stable codes.

tools.name: get_instantly_campaign
tools.description:
Fetch the full details of a single Instantly campaign.

Args:
    campaign_id: UUID of the campaign.

Returns:
    Pretty-printed JSON of the campaign object (schedule, sequences,
    status, counters, …). Errors are returned as JSON payloads.

tools.name: activate_instantly_campaign
tools.description:
Activate (start or resume) an Instantly campaign.

Args:
    campaign_id: UUID of the campaign.

Returns:
    Confirmation line including the campaign name and new status.

tools.name: pause_instantly_campaign
tools.description:
Pause an Instantly campaign (stops sending until re-activated).

Args:
    campaign_id: UUID of the campaign.

Returns:
    Confirmation line including the campaign name and new status.

tools.name: delete_instantly_campaign
tools.description:
Delete an Instantly campaign. **Destructive — irreversible.**

🚨 Two-step deletion protocol — the calling agent MUST follow:

1. FIRST CALL: always with ``confirm=False`` (the default). The tool
   returns a ⚠️ warning string and does NOT touch the Instantly API.
   Surface this warning to the user verbatim and ask them to confirm
   in their own words.
2. SECOND CALL: only after the user has explicitly confirmed having
   seen the warning, re-call this tool with ``confirm=True`` to
   actually issue the DELETE.

🚫 DO NOT pass ``confirm=True`` on the first call, even if the user's
original request is unambiguous (e.g. "删了", "delete it", "直接删，
别问我"). A single user instruction must always become two tool
calls.

🚫 Anti-pattern — user insistence ≠ user having seen the warning.
"I'm sure, just do it", "stop asking, delete it now", "trust me"
are NOT substitutes for the user having read the ⚠️ warning string
that this tool emits on its first call. The warning is generated by
THIS tool — you cannot fabricate or summarize it. If you have not
called this tool with ``confirm=False`` for ``campaign_id`` in the
current turn and shown the response to the user, you have NOT
obtained valid confirmation and MUST NOT call with ``confirm=True``.

🚫 DO NOT bypass this tool by issuing ``DELETE`` to the Instantly
REST API via bash / curl / requests / any HTTP client. The whole
point of this guard is the two-step protocol — bypassing it is a
security incident, not a workaround.

Args:
    campaign_id: UUID of the campaign to delete.
    confirm: Must remain ``False`` on the first call; only set to
        ``True`` on the second call after explicit user confirmation.

Returns:
    - First call (``confirm=False``): the ⚠️ warning prompt — show to
      user, wait for explicit confirmation, then call again.
    - Second call (``confirm=True``): success line with the deleted
      campaign's name.

tools.name: list_instantly_lead_lists
tools.description:
List Instantly lead lists (static prospect groupings) in the current workspace.

Args:
    limit: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 10.
    starting_after: Cursor returned as ``next_starting_after`` from the
        previous page. Omit on the first call.

Returns:
    Markdown table of lead lists (id, name, has_enrichment_task,
    created), plus a cursor hint when more pages are available.

tools.name: create_instantly_lead_list
tools.description:
Create a new Instantly lead list.

Args:
    name: Display name of the lead list (required).
    has_enrichment_task: Optional — when ``True``, Instantly will run
        its enrichment pipeline on leads added to this list.
    owned_by: Optional workspace user id to assign ownership.

Returns:
    Success line plus a JSON snapshot of the created lead list (id,
    name). Errors are returned as JSON payloads with stable codes.

tools.name: list_instantly_leads
tools.description:
List Instantly leads (prospects) with rich filtering.

Internally uses ``POST /api/v2/leads/list`` (not GET; the GET variant
returns 404). Callers don't need to know this — just call the tool.

Args:
    limit: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 10.
    starting_after: Cursor from a previous response's
        ``next_starting_after``.
    search: Case-insensitive substring match against name/email.
    filter: Status enum, e.g. ``FILTER_VAL_REPLIED``,
        ``FILTER_VAL_CONTACTED``, ``FILTER_VAL_BOUNCED``,
        ``FILTER_VAL_NOT_CONTACTED`` (≈30 values; see Instantly docs).
    campaign: Restrict to leads in this campaign id.
    list_id: Restrict to leads in this lead list id.
    in_campaign: ``True`` → only leads that belong to any campaign;
        ``False`` → only orphan-from-campaign leads.
    in_list: Same semantics as ``in_campaign`` but for lead lists.

Returns:
    Markdown table of leads (id, email, name, status, campaign, list),
    plus a cursor hint when more pages are available.

tools.name: add_instantly_leads
tools.description:
Bulk-add 1–1000 leads to either a campaign OR a lead list.

Instantly does not accept orphan leads — exactly one of
``campaign_id`` or ``list_id`` must be provided.

Args:
    leads: List of lead dicts (1–1000). Each dict must contain at
        least one of ``email``, ``first_name``, or ``last_name``;
        other common fields include ``company_name``, ``website``,
        ``personalization``, and arbitrary custom variables.
    campaign_id: UUID of the campaign to add leads under (XOR with
        ``list_id``).
    list_id: UUID of the lead list to add leads under (XOR with
        ``campaign_id``).

Returns:
    Success line with the count added and a JSON snapshot of the
    response. Errors are returned as JSON payloads with stable codes.
    For more than 1000 leads, split the call client-side and invoke
    the tool multiple times.

tools.name: start_sentry_auth
tools.description:
Initiate Sentry OAuth authorization flow.

Use this tool when the user wants to connect their Sentry account via OAuth.
This generates an authorization URL that the user must visit to grant access.
After authorization, Sentry redirects to the configured callback URL and
credentials are stored automatically.

Trigger scenarios:
- User says "connect Sentry", "link Sentry account", "authorize Sentry"
- A Sentry tool returns an authentication-required error

Returns:
    Markdown message containing the Sentry authorization URL for the user to click.

tools.name: set_sentry_credentials
tools.description:
Set Sentry API credentials by providing an auth token directly.

Use this tool when the user already has a Sentry auth token (e.g., from an
Internal Integration or personal token) and wants to connect without OAuth.
The token is validated against the Sentry API before being stored.

Trigger scenarios:
- User provides a Sentry auth token directly
- User prefers not to use the OAuth flow
- User is connecting a self-hosted Sentry instance

Args:
    auth_token: Sentry authentication token (Bearer token).
    organization_slug: Optional. The Sentry organization slug to associate.

Returns:
    Success message containing "connected" if valid, or error message.

tools.name: check_sentry_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of stored Sentry credentials.

This tool checks if credentials exist and reports their validity.
It does NOT expose the actual token value.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "is my Sentry connected?" or "check Sentry status"
- Before running Sentry tools, to confirm auth is still valid

Returns:
    Credential status information.

tools.name: delete_sentry_credentials
tools.description:
Delete stored Sentry credentials for the current workspace.

Use this tool when the user wants to revoke Sentry access or switch accounts.
After deletion, the user will need to re-authorize to use Sentry tools.

Trigger scenarios:
- User says "disconnect Sentry", "remove Sentry", "unlink Sentry"
- User wants to switch to a different Sentry organization

Returns:
    Success or error message.

tools.name: list_sentry_organizations
tools.description:
List Sentry organizations accessible to the connected account.

Use this tool to discover which organizations are available, or to verify
the connection is active. Returns organization slugs needed for other tools.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "what Sentry organizations do I have?"
- Need to find the org slug before querying projects or issues
- Verify Sentry connection is working

Args:
    organization_slug: Optional. If provided, uses this org's credential.

Returns:
    JSON array of organizations with slug, name, and id.

tools.name: list_sentry_projects
tools.description:
List all projects in a Sentry organization.

Returns project slugs, names, and platforms. Project slugs are needed
to filter issues by project.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "what projects are in Sentry?"
- Need to find a project slug before querying issues
- Overview of monitored applications

Args:
    organization_slug: The Sentry organization slug. If empty, uses the
        default from stored credentials.

Returns:
    JSON array of projects with slug, name, platform, and creation date.

tools.name: get_sentry_project_stats
tools.description:
Get error/transaction statistics for a Sentry organization or project.

Returns event counts grouped by outcome (accepted, filtered, rate_limited)
over the specified time period.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "how many errors in the last 24 hours?"
- Overview of error volume trends
- Check if error rate is spiking

Args:
    organization_slug: The Sentry organization slug.
    project_slug: Optional. Filter stats to a specific project.
    stat_period: Time period: "1h", "24h", "7d", "30d". Default "24h".

Returns:
    JSON with event statistics grouped by outcome.

tools.name: list_sentry_releases
tools.description:
List recent releases for a Sentry organization or project.

Returns release versions, creation dates, and new issue counts.
Useful for checking which release introduced new errors.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "what releases happened recently?"
- Investigating which version introduced a bug
- Checking release health

Args:
    organization_slug: The Sentry organization slug.
    project_slug: Optional. Filter releases to a specific project.
    limit: Maximum number of releases to return (default 10).

Returns:
    JSON array of releases with version, date, and new issue count.

tools.name: list_sentry_issues
tools.description:
List unresolved Sentry issues, sorted by last seen (most recent first).

Returns a summary of each issue including title, error count, affected
users, and when it was last seen.

Trigger scenarios:
- User asks "what errors are happening?" or "show me Sentry issues"
- Starting a bug investigation
- Daily error triage

Args:
    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.
    project_slug: Optional. Filter to a specific project.
    limit: Max issues to return (default 25, max 100).

Returns:
    JSON array of issues with id, title, count, userCount, lastSeen.

tools.name: search_sentry_issues
tools.description:
Search Sentry issues using Sentry's query syntax.

Supports Sentry search operators like:
- is:unresolved / is:resolved / is:ignored
- assigned:me / assigned:user@email.com
- level:error / level:fatal
- firstSeen:>2024-01-01
- tag key/value: browser:Chrome, os:Windows
- Free text search in issue title

Trigger scenarios:
- User wants to filter issues by specific criteria
- Looking for issues assigned to someone
- Searching for a specific error message

Args:
    query: Sentry search query string (e.g., "is:unresolved level:error TypeError").
    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.
    project_slug: Optional project filter.
    limit: Max issues to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON array of matching issues.

tools.name: get_sentry_issue_detail
tools.description:
Get full details of a Sentry issue including the latest event's stack trace.

Returns the issue metadata plus the most recent event with exception frames,
breadcrumbs, tags, and user context. This is the primary tool for debugging.

Trigger scenarios:
- User wants to see the stack trace for an issue
- Investigating root cause of an error
- Need to see breadcrumbs leading up to the error

Args:
    issue_id: The Sentry issue ID (numeric string, e.g., "12345").
    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.

Returns:
    JSON with issue details and the latest event's exception + breadcrumbs.

tools.name: get_sentry_issue_tags
tools.description:
Get tag distribution for a Sentry issue.

Shows how an issue breaks down by browser, OS, URL, device, etc.
Useful for identifying if an error is specific to certain environments.

Trigger scenarios:
- "Which browsers are affected by this error?"
- "Is this issue only on mobile?"
- Understanding the impact scope of an issue

Args:
    issue_id: The Sentry issue ID.
    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.

Returns:
    JSON array of tags with their top values and counts.

tools.name: update_sentry_issue
tools.description:
Update a Sentry issue's status or assignment.

Can resolve, ignore, unresolve an issue, or assign it to a team member.

Trigger scenarios:
- "Resolve this issue" / "Mark as fixed"
- "Ignore this issue" / "Mute this issue"
- "Assign this to user@company.com"
- "Reopen this issue"

Args:
    issue_id: The Sentry issue ID.
    status: New status: "resolved", "ignored", "unresolved". Leave empty to skip.
    assigned_to: Email or username to assign to. Use "" to unassign. Leave empty to skip.
    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.

Returns:
    JSON with updated issue state.

tools.name: bulk_update_sentry_issues
tools.description:
Bulk update multiple Sentry issues at once.

Applies the same status change to multiple issues simultaneously.
More efficient than calling update_sentry_issue repeatedly.

Trigger scenarios:
- "Resolve all these issues"
- "Ignore all TypeError issues"
- Batch triage of similar issues

Args:

    organization_slug: Sentry organization slug. Auto-resolved if empty.

Returns:
    JSON confirmation of the bulk update.

tools.name: list_neon_projects

List Neon projects in the current organization.

Create a new Neon project.

database (neondb), role, and read-write endpoint.

Args:

               "aws-eu-central-1", "aws-ap-southeast-1" (Singapore, default).
    pg_version: PostgreSQL major version (default 17). Options: 14, 15, 16, 17.

Get detailed information about a Neon project.

Returns:

tools.name: delete_neon_project
tools.description:
Delete a Neon project. THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE.

🚨 MANDATORY TWO-STEP CALL — DO NOT BYPASS:
  Step 1: Call WITHOUT confirm (or confirm=False) → returns a warning preview.
          You MUST show the returned warning text to the user verbatim
          and ask "Are you sure you want to delete?".
  Step 2: ONLY AFTER the user explicitly confirms (e.g., "yes", "confirm",
          "确认", "继续删除"), call again with confirm=True to actually delete.

DO NOT pass confirm=True on the first call, even if the user's request
sounds urgent or definitive (e.g., "delete it now", "立即删除"). A confident
tone from the user is NOT a substitute for seeing the warning preview.

Deleting a project removes ALL its branches, databases, endpoints, and data.

Args:
    project_id: The Neon project ID to delete.
    confirm: Safety flag. MUST be False on the first call (to get the
             warning preview). MUST be True only on the second call,
             after the user has seen the warning and explicitly confirmed.

Returns:
    Warning preview when confirm=False; deletion confirmation when confirm=True.

Example:
    # Step 1 (preview, REQUIRED):
    delete_neon_project(project_id="old-project-12345")
    # → returns warning; show it to user, ask for confirmation
    # Step 2 (only after user confirms):
    delete_neon_project(project_id="old-project-12345", confirm=True)

tools.name: list_neon_branches
tools.description:
List branches for a Neon project.

Branches are copy-on-write forks of data. Every project has at least one
default branch (usually named "production" or "main").

Args:
    project_id: The Neon project ID (e.g. "morning-flower-39811501").
    cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous response.
    limit: Max number of branches to return (1-100, default 10).

Returns:
    Markdown table of branches with IDs, parent info, and creation dates.

Example:
    list_neon_branches(project_id="morning-flower-39811501")

tools.name: create_neon_branch
tools.description:
Create a new branch in a Neon project.

Branches use copy-on-write, so creating a branch is instant and costs no
additional storage until data diverges. This is recommended before any
write operations (create tables, insert data, schema migrations).

Supports point-in-time recovery (PITR):
- parent_lsn: Fork from a specific WAL Log Sequence Number
- parent_timestamp: Fork from a specific point in time (ISO 8601)

Args:
    project_id: The Neon project ID.
    name: Branch name (optional, e.g. "dev", "feature-xyz"). Auto-generated if omitted.
    parent_id: Branch ID to fork from. Defaults to the project's default branch.
    parent_lsn: Fork from this LSN (e.g. "0/1E45A30"). Mutually exclusive with parent_timestamp.
    parent_timestamp: Fork from this timestamp (e.g. "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z").
                      Mutually exclusive with parent_lsn.

Returns:
    Created branch details including endpoints and connection URIs.

Example:
    # Simple fork from default branch
    create_neon_branch(project_id="morning-flower-39811501", name="dev")

    # PITR: fork from a specific timestamp
    create_neon_branch(
        project_id="morning-flower-39811501",
        name="recovery-point",
        parent_timestamp="2024-06-01T08:00:00Z"
    )

tools.name: describe_neon_branch
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a Neon branch.

Returns branch metadata including parent info, logical size, state, and timestamps.

Args:
    project_id: The Neon project ID.
    branch_id: The branch ID (e.g. "br-weathered-star-aoqqo91t").
               Get this from list_neon_branches.

Returns:
    Detailed branch information in markdown format.

Example:
    describe_neon_branch(
        project_id="morning-flower-39811501",
        branch_id="br-weathered-star-aoqqo91t"
    )

tools.name: delete_neon_branch
tools.description:
Delete a Neon branch. THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE.

🚨 MANDATORY TWO-STEP CALL — DO NOT BYPASS:
  Step 1: Call WITHOUT confirm (or confirm=False) → returns a warning preview.
          You MUST show the returned warning text to the user verbatim
          and ask "Are you sure you want to delete?".
  Step 2: ONLY AFTER the user explicitly confirms (e.g., "yes", "confirm",
          "确认", "继续删除"), call again with confirm=True to actually delete.

DO NOT pass confirm=True on the first call, even if the user's request
sounds urgent or definitive. A confident tone from the user is NOT a
substitute for seeing the warning preview.

Cannot delete the default (production) branch. Deleting a branch removes
its data, endpoints, and all child branches that depend on it.

Args:
    project_id: The Neon project ID.
    branch_id: The branch ID to delete.
    confirm: Safety flag. MUST be False on the first call (to get the
             warning preview). MUST be True only on the second call,
             after the user has seen the warning and explicitly confirmed.

Returns:
    Warning preview when confirm=False; deletion confirmation when confirm=True.

Example:
    # Step 1 (preview, REQUIRED):
    delete_neon_branch(project_id="proj-xxx", branch_id="br-xxx")
    # → returns warning; show it to user, ask for confirmation
    # Step 2 (only after user confirms):
    delete_neon_branch(project_id="proj-xxx", branch_id="br-xxx", confirm=True)

tools.name: list_granola_notes
tools.description:
List Granola meeting notes (only those with AI summary AND transcript ready).

**Critical constraint**: Granola only returns notes whose AI summary AND
transcript are BOTH ready. Notes in pending / processing / never-summarized
state are silently excluded. If the returned count is lower than the user
expects, advise them to open the Granola desktop app and verify that the
AI summary has been generated for the missing meetings.

**When to call**: Use for queries like "list my recent meeting notes",
"找昨天的会议记录", "show notes from last week", "filter by folder X".

Args:
    cursor: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous response.
    page_size: 1-30, default 10.
    created_before / created_after / updated_after: ISO 8601 datetime
        filters (e.g. "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z").
    folder_id: Filter by folder membership (``fol_xxxxxxxxxxxxxx``).

Returns:
    Markdown table of notes, or the GRANOLA_NOTE_NOT_READY hint when empty.

Example:
    list_granola_notes()
    list_granola_notes(page_size=5, created_after="2026-05-01T00:00:00Z")
    list_granola_notes(folder_id="fol_xxxxxxxxxxxxxx")

tools.name: get_granola_note
tools.description:
Get a single Granola meeting note (optionally with full transcript).

**Use `include_transcript=True`** when the user asks for verbatim quotes,
transcript, "原话 / 引述 / quote / 他说了什么 / what did X say".

Behavior of `include_transcript` (实测沉淀):
  - The `transcript` key is ALWAYS present in the Granola response;
    without `include=transcript` it is an empty array, with it it is
    populated with per-segment objects.
  - Body size grows roughly +20% on a typical 30-min meeting
    (~6.3KB → ~7.5KB on the smoke-test sample); for long meetings the
    delta can dominate. Only opt in when the user explicitly asks for
    verbatim content.

**404 handling**: A 404 has TWO causes:
  (a) the note_id truly does not exist, OR
  (b) the note exists but its AI summary / transcript is not yet ready.
The tool always communicates BOTH possibilities in the error payload —
do NOT just say "not found"; advise the user to check the Granola
desktop app for processing status.

Args:
    note_id: ``not_xxxxxxxxxxxxxx`` (14-char base62 suffix).
    include_transcript: Pass True to include the per-segment transcript.

Returns:
    Markdown with note metadata + AI summary (+ transcript if requested),
    or an error JSON payload with hint when the note is not ready.

Example:
    get_granola_note(note_id="not_abc123def456GH")
    get_granola_note(note_id="not_abc123def456GH", include_transcript=True)

tools.name: list_granola_folders
tools.description:
List Granola folders visible to the current API key.

**When to call**: Use for queries like "list my Granola folders",
"看看我的 Granola 文件夹", "show folder list", or when the user wants a
`folder_id` to feed into `list_granola_notes(folder_id=...)`.

**Scope reminder**: A folder appears here only if the API key's scope
grants access to it. If the user expects more folders than returned,
ask them to verify the key's scope (Personal / Public) in Granola
Desktop → Settings → Connectors → API keys.

**Empty list is normal**: Granola does not require folders — many users
keep notes flat. An empty list here is NOT the same as the
GRANOLA_NOTE_NOT_READY constraint that affects `list_granola_notes`.

Args:
    cursor: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous response.
    page_size: 1-30, default 10.

Returns:
    Markdown table of folders, or a friendly "no folders" message when
    the result set is empty.

Example:
    list_granola_folders()
    list_granola_folders(page_size=30)

tools.name: set_mailchimp_credentials
tools.description:
Set, update, or disconnect Mailchimp API credentials for the current user.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Mailchimp account, or
when a Mailchimp API call returns 401 indicating the API key is missing or
has been revoked.

**How to obtain an API Key:**
The user should visit https://us1.admin.mailchimp.com/account/api/ to
generate an API key. The key has the format ``<random>-<data_center>``
(e.g. ``abc...-us17``). The data center suffix (``us17``) is extracted
automatically and used as the API base host.

**Disconnect:**
Passing an empty string for ``api_key`` is the connector-level disconnect
contract. The stored credential is removed idempotently and no Mailchimp
API verification is performed.

**Verification:**
Before storing, the API key is verified against the Mailchimp API root
endpoint. If verification fails, the key is NOT stored and a structured
error payload is returned.

Args:
    api_key: Mailchimp API Key (format: ``<random>-<data_center>``).
        Empty string means disconnect.

Returns:
    - On success: a message containing the Mailchimp account name.
    - On empty api_key: a message containing "disconnected".
    - On failure: a structured JSON error with code and message.

Example:
    set_mailchimp_credentials(api_key="abc1234567890abcdef-us17")
    set_mailchimp_credentials(api_key="")

tools.name: check_mailchimp_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the current user's Mailchimp API credentials.

This tool checks whether credentials exist and re-verifies them against
the Mailchimp API. It does NOT expose the actual API key value.

Returns:
    Credential status information.

Example:
    check_mailchimp_credentials()

tools.name: delete_mailchimp_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Mailchimp API credentials.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to disconnect their Mailchimp account
or revoke access.

After deletion, the user will need to set new credentials before using
Mailchimp tools.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_mailchimp_credentials()

tools.name: get_mailchimp_account_info
tools.description:
Get Mailchimp account information including plan details, contact limits,
and usage statistics.

Returns:
    JSON string of the authenticated Mailchimp account profile.

Example:
    get_mailchimp_account_info()

tools.name: list_mailchimp_audiences
tools.description:
List all audiences (mailing lists) in your Mailchimp account.

Args:
    count: Maximum number of audiences to return (1-1000, default 10).
    offset: Zero-based pagination offset (default 0).

Returns:
    JSON string with the audience list and pagination metadata.

Example:

tools.name: get_mailchimp_audience
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific audience including member statistics.

List members (subscribers) in a specific audience list.

Example:
    list_mailchimp_members(list_id="abc123def4", count=50, status="subscribed")

tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific list member by email address.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    email_address: Member email address. Mailchimp identifies members by
        the lowercase MD5 hash of this address.

Returns:
    JSON string with member details.

Example:
    get_mailchimp_member(list_id="abc123def4", email_address="user@example.com")

tools.name: add_or_update_mailchimp_member
tools.description:
Add a new member or update an existing member in an audience list.

Uses Mailchimp's PUT (upsert) semantics — if the member exists, it is
updated; otherwise a new subscriber is created.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    email_address: Subscriber email address.
    status: Subscriber status. One of "subscribed", "unsubscribed",
        "cleaned", "pending", "transactional". Defaults to "subscribed".
    merge_fields: Optional JSON-encoded object of merge fields, e.g.
        '{"FNAME": "Ada", "LNAME": "Lovelace"}'.
    tags: Optional JSON-encoded array of tag names to assign on create,
        e.g. '["VIP", "Newsletter"]'. (Use manage_mailchimp_member_tags
        to add/remove tags from existing members.)

Returns:
    JSON string with the created/updated member resource.

Example:
    add_or_update_mailchimp_member(
        list_id="abc123def4",
        email_address="user@example.com",
        status="subscribed",
        merge_fields='{"FNAME": "Ada"}',
        tags='["VIP"]'
    )

tools.name: delete_mailchimp_member
tools.description:
Remove (archive) a member from an audience list.

Mailchimp archives the subscriber rather than permanently deleting them.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    email_address: Subscriber email address.

Returns:
    JSON string indicating success.

Example:
    delete_mailchimp_member(list_id="abc123def4", email_address="user@example.com")

tools.name: manage_mailchimp_member_tags
tools.description:
Add or remove tags for a specific list member.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    email_address: Subscriber email address.
    tags: JSON-encoded array of tag operations. Each item should be an
        object with "name" (the tag name) and "status" ("active" to add,
        "inactive" to remove).
        Example: '[{"name": "VIP", "status": "active"},
                   {"name": "Cold", "status": "inactive"}]'.

Returns:
    JSON string indicating success.

Example:
    manage_mailchimp_member_tags(
        list_id="abc123def4",
        email_address="user@example.com",
        tags='[{"name": "VIP", "status": "active"}]'
    )

tools.name: list_mailchimp_campaigns
tools.description:
List email campaigns in your Mailchimp account.

Args:
    count: Maximum number of campaigns to return (default 10).
    offset: Zero-based pagination offset (default 0).
    status: Optional campaign status filter. One of:
        "save", "paused", "schedule", "sending", "sent".

Returns:
    JSON string with the campaign list and metadata.

Example:
    list_mailchimp_campaigns(count=20, status="sent")

tools.name: create_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Create a new email marketing campaign.

Args:
    list_id: Audience (list) ID to send the campaign to.
    subject_line: Subject line shown in recipients' inboxes.
    title: Internal campaign title (used in the Mailchimp dashboard).
    from_name: Display name shown as the sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    campaign_type: Campaign type. One of "regular", "plaintext",
        "absplit", "rss", "variate". Defaults to "regular".

Returns:
    JSON string with the created campaign resource (including its id).

Example:
    create_mailchimp_campaign(
        list_id="abc123def4",
        subject_line="Spring Sale Inside!",
        title="2026 Spring Sale",
        from_name="Acme Store",
        reply_to="hello@acme.example"
    )

tools.name: update_mailchimp_campaign_content
tools.description:
Set or update the **email body** (HTML / plain-text) of an existing campaign. Scope: ONLY the message content. Use ``update_mailchimp_campaign`` to change campaign metadata (subject_line, from_name, reply_to, title, preview_text) or the recipient audience (list_id, segment_opts). Endpoint: ``PUT /campaigns/{id}/content``. Provide HTML, plain text, or both. At least one must be supplied. Args: campaign_id: ID of the campaign to update. html: HTML body of the campaign email. plain_text: Plain-text alternative body. Returns: JSON string with the updated campaign content resource. Example: update_mailchimp_campaign_content( campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5", html="

Hello!

Thanks for subscribing.

", plain_text="Hello! Thanks for subscribing." )

tools.name: update_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Update **campaign metadata** (settings + recipient audience) of an
existing campaign. The email body is NOT touched here.

Scope: subject_line, title, from_name, reply_to, preview_text, folder_id,
recipients (list_id / segment_opts). Use
``update_mailchimp_campaign_content`` to change the HTML / plain-text
body.

Endpoint: ``PATCH /campaigns/{id}``.

Only supplied (non-null) fields are sent to Mailchimp; omitted fields
are left unchanged. At least one settable field must be provided.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the campaign to update.
    subject_line: New subject line shown in recipients' inboxes.
    title: New internal campaign title (Mailchimp dashboard).
    from_name: New display name shown as the sender.
    reply_to: New reply-to email address.
    preview_text: Optional preview text shown after the subject line.
    folder_id: Optional campaign folder ID.
    list_id: New audience (list) ID, to redirect the campaign to a
        different audience.
    segment_opts: Optional JSON-encoded segment options object, e.g.
        '{"saved_segment_id": 12345}' or
        '{"match": "all", "conditions": [...]}'.

Returns:
    JSON string with the updated campaign resource.

Example:
    update_mailchimp_campaign(
        campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5",
        subject_line="Updated Subject",
        from_name="Acme Store"
    )

tools.name: send_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Send an email campaign immediately to all recipients.

The campaign must already have content set and be in a sendable state.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the campaign to send.

Returns:
    JSON string indicating success.

Example:
    send_mailchimp_campaign(campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5")

tools.name: schedule_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Schedule a campaign to be sent at a specific UTC time.

The campaign must already have content set and be in a sendable state.
Use ``unschedule_mailchimp_campaign`` to cancel a scheduled send before
it dispatches.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the campaign to schedule.
    schedule_time: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp aligned to a quarter-hour
        (e.g. "2026-06-01T13:00:00+00:00" or "2026-06-01T13:00:00Z").
        Minutes must be 00, 15, 30 or 45. Must be in the future.
    timewarp: If True, send to each recipient at the given local time in
        their own timezone (Timewarp requires a date ≥ 1 day ahead).

Returns:
    JSON string ``{"success": true, "campaign_id": ..., "schedule_time": ...}``.

Example:
    schedule_mailchimp_campaign(
        campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5",
        schedule_time="2026-06-01T13:00:00+00:00"
    )

tools.name: unschedule_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Cancel the scheduled send of a campaign.

The campaign goes back to a draft ("save") status and can be re-scheduled
or sent later.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the scheduled campaign to unschedule.

Returns:
    JSON string ``{"success": true, "campaign_id": ...}``.

Example:
    unschedule_mailchimp_campaign(campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5")

tools.name: get_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Fetch full details of a single campaign (read-only).

Use this to inspect a campaign's current ``status`` (save / schedule /
paused / sending / sent / canceled), ``send_time``, ``settings``
(subject_line, from_name, reply_to, preview_text, title) and
``recipients`` (list_id, segment_opts) before performing further actions
such as ``update_mailchimp_campaign``, ``schedule_mailchimp_campaign``,
``send_mailchimp_campaign`` or ``delete_mailchimp_campaign``.

Endpoint: ``GET /campaigns/{id}``.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the campaign to fetch.

Returns:
    JSON string with the full campaign resource.

Example:
    get_mailchimp_campaign(campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5")

tools.name: delete_mailchimp_campaign
tools.description:
Permanently delete a campaign.

⚠️ WARNING: This operation is **irreversible**. The campaign and its
associated content/report data are removed from Mailchimp.

Allowed only for campaigns in ``save`` / ``paused`` / ``schedule`` /
``canceled`` status. Mailchimp returns HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed)
for already-sent campaigns; sent campaigns can only be archived via
the dashboard. Always inspect the campaign with ``get_mailchimp_campaign``
or ``list_mailchimp_campaigns`` first to confirm its status, and
obtain explicit user confirmation before calling this tool.

Endpoint: ``DELETE /campaigns/{id}``.

Args:
    campaign_id: ID of the campaign to delete.

Returns:
    JSON string ``{"success": true, "campaign_id": ...}``.

Example:
    delete_mailchimp_campaign(campaign_id="b1a2c3d4e5")

tools.name: send_mailchimp_test_email
tools.description:
Send a test email for a campaign to specified email addresses.

Args:

Returns:

Example:

        test_emails='["qa@example.com"]',
        send_type="html"
    )

Returns:

Example:

tools.name: get_mailchimp_campaign_open_details
tools.description:
Get detailed list of subscribers who opened a specific campaign, including

Args:

Get detailed list of links clicked in a campaign and which subscribers

Args:

Get list of subscribers who unsubscribed from a specific campaign.

Returns:

Hi *|FNAME|*

List all segments in a specific audience list.

tools.name: create_mailchimp_segment
tools.description:
Create a new segment in an audience list. Use static_segment (JSON array of

tools.description:
List all merge fields (custom fields) defined for an audience list.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.

Returns:

Example:

tools.name: add_mailchimp_merge_field
tools.description:
Add a new merge field (custom contact property) to an audience list.
field_type options: text, number, address, phone, date, url, imageurl,
radio, dropdown, birthday, zip.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    name: Merge field display name (e.g. "Birthday").
    field_type: One of text, number, address, phone, date, url, imageurl,
        radio, dropdown, birthday, zip.
    required: Whether the field is required (default False).
    default_value: Optional default value for the field.
    choices: Optional JSON array of strings, used by radio/dropdown fields,
        e.g. '["Option A", "Option B"]'.

Returns:
    JSON string with the created merge field resource.

Example:
    add_mailchimp_merge_field(
        list_id="abc123def4",
        name="Plan",
        field_type="dropdown",
        choices='["Free", "Pro"]'
    )

tools.name: delete_mailchimp_merge_field
tools.description:
Delete a merge field (custom contact property) from an audience list.

WARNING: Deleting a merge field permanently removes it from the audience
and from every contact in that audience. Data stored in this field cannot
be recovered. Built-in fields (e.g. EMAIL) cannot be removed. Avoid
deleting fields you did not create yourself, as they may be used by other
integrations.

Args:
    list_id: Mailchimp audience (list) ID.
    merge_id: The merge field's numeric ID (the ``merge_id`` returned by
        ``list_mailchimp_merge_fields`` / ``add_mailchimp_merge_field``).
        Note this is NOT the merge tag (e.g. "COMPANY").

Returns:
    JSON string ``{"success": true, "list_id": ..., "merge_id": ...}``
    on success.

Example:
    delete_mailchimp_merge_field(list_id="abc123def4", merge_id="5")

Add multiple members to an audience list in a single operation. members is

merge_fields.

Args:
