    members: JSON array of member objects, e.g.
        '[{"email_address": "a@b.com", "status": "subscribed",
           "merge_fields": {"FNAME": "Alice"}}]'.
    update_existing: Whether to update existing members (default True).

Returns:
    JSON string with the batch result, including new_members,
    updated_members and any errors.

Example:
    batch_add_mailchimp_members(
        list_id="abc123def4",
        members='[{"email_address": "a@b.com", "status": "subscribed"}]'
    )

tools.name: set_klaviyo_credentials
tools.description:
Set, update, or disconnect the Klaviyo API key for the current workspace.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when the user wants to
connect their Klaviyo account, rotate the key, or disconnect Klaviyo. It
should also be called when any Klaviyo marketing tool returns an
authentication error indicating the credential is missing or invalid.

**Single-credential contract**: each workspace (accio_id) can bind at most
ONE Klaviyo API key. Setting a new key replaces the previous one.

**Disconnect contract**: passing an empty string for ``api_key`` disconnects
the current Klaviyo binding idempotently and skips Klaviyo API verification.

The tool verifies the API key against the Klaviyo Accounts API before
persisting it. If verification fails, no credential is stored and a
human-readable error is returned.

**Supported permission scopes** (must be enabled on the Klaviyo private key):
Profiles, Lists, Campaigns, Flows, Templates, Events, Metrics, Segments,
Catalogs, Coupons, Webhooks, Accounts.

To create a private API key, visit:
https://www.klaviyo.com/settings/account/api-keys

Args:
    api_key: Klaviyo private API key (starts with "pk_"). Empty string means disconnect.

Returns:
    On success: a message containing "connected" with the verified account info.
    On disconnect: a message containing "disconnected".
    On failure: a human-readable error message.

Example:
    set_klaviyo_credentials(api_key="pk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx")
    set_klaviyo_credentials(api_key="")

tools.name: check_klaviyo_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the Klaviyo API credential for the current workspace.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when the user asks
whether Klaviyo is connected, or before executing a Klaviyo marketing
operation to confirm the credential is still valid.

The tool re-verifies the stored credential against the Klaviyo API.
It does NOT expose the actual API key value.

Returns:
    Credential status information including validity, account id,
    and creation time.

Example:
    check_klaviyo_credentials()

tools.name: delete_klaviyo_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current workspace's Klaviyo API credential.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when the user wants to
disconnect their Klaviyo account or revoke access.

Each workspace (accio_id) binds at most one Klaviyo API key, so this
tool takes no parameters — it deletes whatever credential is currently
stored for the calling workspace. The operation is idempotent.

After deletion, the user will need to call ``set_klaviyo_credentials``
again to reconnect.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_klaviyo_credentials()

tools.name: klaviyo_get_accounts
tools.description:
Retrieve all Klaviyo accounts accessible with the current API key.

**When to call:**
- The user asks about their Klaviyo account details (ID, email, timezone).
- You need the account ID for downstream operations.

Args:
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account. Use `check_klaviyo_credentials` to list
        connected accounts.

Returns:
    On success — account summary plus JSON array.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_tracking_settings
tools.description:
Retrieve Klaviyo tracking settings for the account.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to check or audit their tracking configuration
  (open tracking, click tracking, etc.).

Args:
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — tracking settings summary plus JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_account
tools.description:
Retrieve a single Klaviyo account by ID.

**When to call:**
- The user wants details about a specific Klaviyo account.

Args:
    klaviyo_account_id: The Klaviyo account ID to retrieve (required).
    account_id: Optional credential account ID for multi-account support.

Returns:
    On success — account details plus JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_update_tracking_setting
tools.description:
Update a Klaviyo tracking setting.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to enable or disable automatic UTM parameter tracking.

Args:
    setting_id: Tracking setting ID (required). Get it from ``klaviyo_get_tracking_settings``.
    auto_add_parameters: Enable/disable automatic UTM parameter injection into links.
    utm_source_flow: Static value for utm_source in flow emails (e.g. "Klaviyo").
    utm_source_campaign: Static value for utm_source in campaign emails.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation plus updated JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_profiles
tools.description:
List Klaviyo profiles (contacts) with optional email filter.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to search or browse their contact list.
- You need to find a specific profile by email before updating it.

Args:
    filter_email: Filter by exact email address. Example: "john@example.com".
    page_size: Number of profiles per page (1-100, default 20).
    page_cursor: Cursor for pagination; pass the value from a previous
        response's ``links.next`` to get the next page.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — human-readable list plus JSON array of profiles.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_create_or_update_profile
tools.description:
Create or update a Klaviyo profile (contact). Uses upsert semantics — if a
profile with the given email already exists it will be updated.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to add a new contact to Klaviyo.
- The user wants to update an existing contact's attributes.

Args:
    email: Contact email address (required). Example: "alice@example.com".
    first_name: First name. Example: "Alice".
    last_name: Last name. Example: "Smith".
    phone_number: Phone in E.164 format. Example: "+15551234567".
    title: Job title.
    organization: Company name.
    city: City name.
    country: Country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Example: "US".
    properties: JSON string of custom properties.
        Example: '{"plan": "premium", "signup_source": "website"}'.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text plus profile JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_lists
tools.description:
List all Klaviyo lists.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to see all mailing lists.
- You need a list ID before adding/removing profiles.

Args:
    page_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous response.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — list names with IDs plus JSON array.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_create_list
tools.description:
Create a new Klaviyo list.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to create a new mailing list for segmentation or campaigns.

Args:
    name: List name (required). Example: "VIP Customers".
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation plus list JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_add_profiles_to_list
tools.description:
Add one or more profiles to a Klaviyo list by profile ID.

**Prerequisites — you MUST do these steps before calling this tool:**
1. Use ``klaviyo_get_profiles`` (with ``filter_email``) to look up existing
   profiles and obtain their IDs.
2. If a profile does not exist yet, use ``klaviyo_create_or_update_profile``

**When to call:**
- The user wants to add contacts to a specific list.
- You already have the Klaviyo profile IDs from the steps above.

Args:
    list_id: The Klaviyo list ID (required). Get it from ``klaviyo_get_lists``.
    profile_ids: Comma-separated Klaviyo profile IDs.
        Example: "01ABC123,01DEF456".
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_segments
tools.description:
List all Klaviyo segments.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to view audience segments.
- You need a segment ID for campaign targeting or analytics.

Args:
    page_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous response.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — segment names with IDs plus JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_subscribe_profiles

Subscribe one or more profiles to a Klaviyo list (with double opt-in

    emails: Comma-separated email addresses.
        Example: "alice@example.com,bob@example.com".
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_unsubscribe_profiles
tools.description:
Unsubscribe one or more profiles from a Klaviyo list.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to unsubscribe contacts from marketing emails for a list.

Args:
    list_id: Target list ID (required). Get it from ``klaviyo_get_lists``.
    emails: Comma-separated email addresses.
        Example: "alice@example.com,bob@example.com".
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_get_tags
tools.description:
List all Klaviyo tags.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to see or manage organizational tags.

Args:

tools.name: klaviyo_create_segment
tools.description:
Create a new Klaviyo segment.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to create a dynamic audience segment.

Args:
    name: Segment name (required). Example: "High-value Customers".
    condition_group_json: Optional JSON string defining segment conditions.
        If omitted, creates an empty segment that can be configured in Klaviyo UI.

        **Top-level shape (V3 strict):** the JSON MUST be wrapped in
        ``condition_groups``. Do NOT put ``conditions`` at the root — the
        API will reject ``'condition_groups' is a required field``.
        Layout: ``{"condition_groups": [{"conditions": [ ... ]}]}``.
        Multiple groups are OR'd; conditions inside a group are AND'd.

        **type ↔ field-name pairing (required, easy to mix up):**
        - Custom or event-derived properties:
          ``{"type": "profile-property", "property": "<name>", ...}``
        - Built-in profile attributes (email, first_name, last_name, city,
          country, region, zip, phone_number, organization, ...):
          ``{"type": "profile-attribute", "field": "<name>", ...}``
        - Behavioural metrics (Placed Order, Active on Site, ...):
          ``{"type": "profile-metric", "metric_name": "<name>",
          "measurement": "count"|"sum_value"|"unique", "operator": ...,
          "value": ...}``

        **Email-not-empty pitfall:** the generic ``"operator": "is-set"``
        on the built-in ``email`` field returns
        ``An invalid field type was passed in`` on V3. Use
        ``{"type": "profile-attribute", "field": "email",
        "operator": "contains", "value": "@"}`` instead — every valid
        email contains ``@`` and this passes V3 validation.

        **Examples (copy-paste ready):**
        - Customers who placed at least one order:
          ``{"condition_groups":[{"conditions":[{"type":"profile-metric",
          "metric_name":"Placed Order","measurement":"count",
          "operator":"greater-than","value":0}]}]}``
        - US contacts with a non-empty email (AND):
          ``{"condition_groups":[{"conditions":[
          {"type":"profile-attribute","field":"email","operator":"contains","value":"@"},
          {"type":"profile-attribute","field":"country","operator":"equals","value":"US"}]}]}``

        **When in doubt:** call ``klaviyo_get_segment`` on an existing
        segment and reuse its ``attributes.definition`` as a template.
        The payload here is forwarded as-is, so the caller is responsible
        for using the wrapped ``condition_groups`` form.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation plus segment JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_schedule_campaign
tools.description:
Schedule an existing Draft campaign to be sent at a future time.

Performs Klaviyo's two-step scheduling workflow atomically:
  1. ``PATCH /api/campaigns/{id}/`` — set ``send_strategy``
     (``static`` / ``throttled``, with the chosen ``send_datetime``).
  2. ``POST /api/campaign-send-jobs/`` — submit the campaign to Klaviyo's
     scheduler so its status leaves ``Draft``.
Klaviyo's server-side scheduler then triggers the actual send at the
specified time — no client-side polling needed.

**Pre-requisites (Klaviyo hard constraints):**
- **Status must be Draft.** ``send_strategy`` is only writable in Draft.
  To re-schedule a campaign already in ``Scheduled`` / ``Queued`` /
  ``Queued without Recipients``, first call
  ``klaviyo_cancel_campaign_send(campaign_id, action='revert')`` to bring
  it back to Draft, then call this tool again.
- **Campaign-message must have a template assigned.** A campaign created
  with inline content alone will be rejected with
  ``"message does not have a template"``. Attach a template via
  ``klaviyo_assign_template_to_campaign_message`` first.

**Post-call behaviour (status machine is asynchronous):**
- The HTTP 200 returned here only acknowledges that Klaviyo accepted the
  schedule — the campaign's ``status`` field flips a moment later (usually
  <2s, occasionally up to ~10s) once the backend scheduler ingests the job.
- Terminal post-submit status depends on recipient population:
    * ``Scheduled``                  — has eligible recipients, awaiting send time.
    * ``Queued``                     — in scheduler queue, recipients still being resolved.
    * ``Queued without Recipients``  — list/segment currently has no eligible
      recipients (common for test lists); the schedule is accepted but
      will not deliver until recipients become available.
  All three values mean "the schedule was accepted and the campaign is no
  longer in Draft".
- If you must verify the new status, poll ``klaviyo_get_campaign`` and
  accept any of the three values above.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to send a campaign at a specific time instead of immediately.
- The user wants to switch an immediate-send campaign to a scheduled one.

Args:
    campaign_id: The campaign ID (required). Get it from ``klaviyo_get_campaigns``.
    send_datetime: ISO-8601 send time (required).
        Example: ``"2026-06-01T09:00:00+00:00"``.
    is_local: When ``True``, send in each recipient's local timezone instead of
        absolute UTC. Defaults to ``False`` (everyone receives at the same UTC moment).
    send_past_recipients_immediately: Only meaningful when ``is_local=True``.
        When ``True``, recipients whose local time has already passed receive the
        message immediately instead of being skipped.
    throttle_percentage: Optional 1-100. When provided, uses ``throttled`` strategy:
        sends to this percentage of recipients per batch starting at ``send_datetime``.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation that the campaign is scheduled.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_update_flow_action
tools.description:
Update a Klaviyo flow action's ``definition`` (PATCH /api/flow-actions/{id}/).

This is the only stable v3 API path for editing a flow message's content,
sender, subject line, time-delay value, conditional-split logic, etc.
Klaviyo no longer exposes a direct PATCH on ``/api/flow-messages/{id}/``.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to edit an automation's email/SMS/push content (subject,
  preview text, from address, etc.) or any other action attribute.
- Always fetch the current definition first via
  ``klaviyo_get_flow_action(action_id, include_definition=True)`` and modify
  that payload — ``definition`` must conform to one of Klaviyo's
  action-definition schemas (``SendEmailAction``, ``SendSmsAction``,
  ``TimeDelayAction``, etc.) and is replaced as a whole.

Args:
    action_id: The flow action ID (required). Find it via
        ``klaviyo_get_flow_messages_for_action`` or by inspecting the
        ``relationships.flow-action`` field on a flow-message resource.
    definition_json: JSON string of the **full** ``definition`` object to
        replace the existing one. Klaviyo replaces the field as a whole —
        partial payloads omit required fields and trigger HTTP 422
        (``invalid attribute`` / ``required field is missing``).

        **Mandatory workflow:**
        1. Fetch the current definition via
           ``klaviyo_get_flow_action(action_id, include_definition=True)``.
        2. Mutate only the fields you need on the returned
           ``attributes.definition`` object.
        3. Pass the mutated object back here as ``definition_json``.

        The schema depends on the action ``type`` (one of
        ``SendEmailAction``, ``SendSmsAction``, ``SendPushAction``,
        ``TimeDelayAction``, ``ConditionalSplitAction``,
        ``UpdateProfilePropertyAction``, ``WebhookAction``, ...).

        **SendEmailAction minimal-but-complete shape:**
        ``{"type":"SendEmailAction","message":{"type":"flow-message",
        "id":"<message_id>","subject_line":"...","preview_text":"...",
        "from_email":"sender@brand.com","from_label":"Brand",
        "reply_to_email":"reply@brand.com","cc_email":null,
        "bcc_email":null,"template_id":"<template_id>",
        "smart_sending_enabled":true,"transactional":false}}``
        Always start from the GET response — do NOT hand-craft this
        payload from scratch.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation plus the updated flow action JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_cancel_campaign_send
tools.description:
Cancel or revert a scheduled / sending campaign send job.

Wraps Klaviyo's ``PATCH /api/campaign-send-jobs/{id}/`` endpoint, which accepts
two mutually exclusive actions:

- ``cancel`` (default) — terminate the send job. Campaign status moves to
  ``Cancelled`` and **cannot** be resumed or re-edited.
- ``revert`` — abort the send job and move the campaign back to ``Draft`` so it
  can be edited or rescheduled (use this to *unschedule* a Scheduled campaign).

**When to call:**
- User wants to abort a campaign currently in ``Sending`` / ``Queued`` /
  ``Queued without Recipients`` / ``Scheduled`` status.
- For unscheduling so the campaign can be edited again, pass ``action='revert'``.
- For permanent cancellation, use the default ``action='cancel'``.
- **Mandatory pre-step for re-scheduling**: Klaviyo only accepts a new
  ``send_strategy`` while the campaign is in ``Draft``. To change a
  Scheduled/Queued campaign's send time, call this with ``action='revert'``
  first, then call ``klaviyo_schedule_campaign`` with the new datetime.

**Post-call behaviour (asynchronous):**
- HTTP 204 only acknowledges the request — the campaign's ``status`` field
  flips a moment later (usually <2s). After ``revert`` the status returns
  to ``Draft`` and ``send_strategy`` becomes writable again.

Args:
    campaign_id: The campaign ID (required). Get from ``klaviyo_get_campaigns``.
    action: Either ``"cancel"`` (default, permanent) or ``"revert"``
        (unschedule → back to Draft).
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_create_event
tools.description:
Track a custom event in Klaviyo.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to log a custom event (e.g. purchase, page view) for a profile.

**Profile identifier (V3 contract):**
Klaviyo V3 ``POST /api/events/`` requires at least ONE of the following
profile identifiers; multiple may be supplied to help Klaviyo merge or
create the profile.  Recommended priority when choosing one:
``external_id`` > ``email`` > ``phone_number`` > ``anonymous_id``.
If none is provided this tool returns a structured error instead of
calling the API.

Args:
    metric_name: Event / metric name (required). Example: "Placed Order".
    profile_email: Email of the profile (e.g. ``a@b.com``).
    profile_external_id: Your system's stable user id (e.g. ``user_42``).
        Preferred for B2B/e-commerce integrations where PII (email) is not
        available or must be avoided.
    profile_phone_number: E.164 formatted phone (e.g. ``+15551234567``).
        Klaviyo strictly validates this format.
    profile_anonymous_id: Klaviyo anonymous id captured from the web/mobile
        SDK (cookie ``__kla_id``).  Use for pre-auth tracking.
    properties: JSON string of event properties.
        Example: '{"product_name": "T-Shirt", "quantity": 2}'.
    value: Numeric value for the event (e.g. order total).
    unique_id: Idempotency key to prevent duplicate events.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID. When provided, uses the credential
        for that specific account.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text including the identifier actually used.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_bulk_create_events
tools.description:
Bulk create events in Klaviyo.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to import multiple events at once.

**Profile identifier per event (V3 contract):**
Each event object MUST include at least one profile identifier among
``profile_email`` / ``profile_external_id`` / ``profile_phone_number`` /
``profile_anonymous_id``.  Events sharing the SAME identifier tuple are
grouped under one bulk-create entry; events with different identifiers
are split into separate entries automatically.  Recommended priority
when choosing one: ``external_id`` > ``email`` > ``phone_number`` >
``anonymous_id``.  Multiple identifiers per event are allowed.

Args:
    events_json: JSON array of event objects. Each object must have:
        - metric_name (str): Event name.
        - At least one of: profile_email, profile_external_id,
          profile_phone_number, profile_anonymous_id.
        - properties (dict, optional): Event properties.
        - value (number, optional): Numeric event value.
        Example with mixed identifiers:
          '[{"metric_name": "Placed Order", "profile_email": "a@b.com",
             "properties": {"order_id": 123}, "value": 50},
            {"metric_name": "Page View", "profile_external_id": "u_42"}]'
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation text.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_query_metric_aggregates
tools.description:
Query aggregated metric data from Klaviyo.

**When to call:**
- The user wants analytical data about a specific metric (counts, sums, etc.).

Args:
    metric_id: The metric ID (required). Get it from ``klaviyo_get_metrics``.
    measurements: Comma-separated aggregation types. Options: "count", "sum_value", "unique".
        Default: "count".
    interval: Time interval — "hour", "day", "week", "month". Default: "day".
    page_size: Number of data points (max 500). Default: 500.
    filter_str: Optional Klaviyo filter expression. The endpoint REQUIRES a
        ``datetime`` window; if omitted, this tool auto-injects the last 30
        days. When you DO supply ``filter_str``, the auto-window is dropped,
        so you must include both lower and upper bounds yourself.
        Datetime values must be ISO-8601 with timezone offset (date-only
        strings are rejected). Operators include ``equals``, ``greater-or-equal``,
        ``less-than``, ``contains``, ``any``.
        Example (single bound, the upper bound still defaults to ``now``
        because the API itself enforces a window — prefer passing both):
        ``greater-or-equal(datetime,2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00)``.
        Note: internally this is wrapped as a single-element list and
        sent as ``filter`` to the API.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — aggregated metric data plus JSON.
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

tools.name: klaviyo_create_custom_object_record
tools.description:
Ingest a data source record so Klaviyo can derive a custom object record.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to write external business data into Klaviyo
  (e.g. an order, a subscription, a loyalty event).
- **The user wants to UPDATE an existing custom object record.**
  Klaviyo has no PATCH endpoint for custom object records; updates are
  performed by calling this tool again with the SAME data source and a
  payload whose ``id_path`` field value matches the existing record —
  Klaviyo will overwrite the existing record. IMPORTANT: include the
  **entire** record because any omitted properties become null.

How it works:
    Klaviyo doesn't expose a direct "create object record" endpoint.
    Instead, you ingest a record into a **data source** and the source
    mapping/schema turns it into one or more object records.
    This tool calls
    ``POST /api/data-source-record-create-jobs`` (revision ``2026-04-15``).
    Re-ingesting with a matching ``id_path`` value performs an
    "overwrite by re-ingest" update.

Args:
    custom_object_api_name: The data source's ``namespace`` or its ULID.
        Example: "orders" or ``01J7C23V8XWMRG13FMD7VZN6GW``.
    properties_json: JSON string used as the data source record payload.
        Example: '{"order_id": "O-1001", "total": 99.5, "currency": "USD"}'.
        Field names must match the data source record shape expected by
        your source mapping (typically a flat object).
    profile_id: Deprecated/ignored. Profile linkage is configured by the
        source mapping (via ``email`` / ``external-id`` / ``klaviyo-id`` /
        ``phone`` extracted from the record), not by this parameter.
    account_id: Optional Klaviyo account ID.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation plus job JSON (the job id can be used to
    poll Klaviyo if needed).
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

       Shippo Dashboard → Settings → Carrier Accounts. Do NOT search the filesystem,
       environment variables, or source code.

Args:
    object_id: Carrier account object_id (optional; if provided, fetches that single account)
    carrier: Filter by carrier code, e.g., "usps", "ups", "fedex", "dhl_express",
        "canada_post", "dpd_de", "hermes_uk" (optional)
    active_only: Only return carriers with active=True (default True)
    fetch_all_pages: Auto-paginate to retrieve ALL carriers across pages (default True).
        Set False only if you explicitly want a single page (rare).

Returns:
    Single carrier account dict (when object_id given), or
    {"results": [...], "count": N} aggregated across pages.

tools.name: create_shippo_customs_item
tools.description:
Create a customs item for international shipping declarations.

Args:
    description: Description of the item
    quantity: Quantity of items
    net_weight: Net weight per item
    mass_unit: Weight unit ("g", "oz", "lb", "kg")
    value_amount: Value per item (e.g., "25.00")
    value_currency: Currency code (e.g., "USD")
    origin_country: ISO 2-letter country of manufacture
    tariff_number: HS/tariff code (optional)
    sku_code: SKU code (optional)
    eccn_ear99: Export control classification (optional)
    metadata: Custom metadata (optional)

Returns:
    Created customs item with object_id

tools.name: get_shippo_customs_items
tools.description:
Get a single customs item by ID or list all customs items.

Args:
    object_id: Customs item object_id (optional; if omitted, lists all)

Returns:
    Single customs item or paginated list

tools.name: create_shippo_customs_declaration
tools.description:
Create a customs declaration for international shipments (海关申报 / customs form).

PREREQUISITE: You must first create customs items via create_shippo_customs_item, then
pass their object_ids in the `items` parameter.

WORKFLOW for international shipping:
1. Call create_shippo_customs_item for each product in the package
2. Call this tool with those item IDs to create the declaration
3. Pass the declaration object_id to create_shippo_shipment's customs_declaration param

Args:
    contents_type: Type of contents ("DOCUMENTS", "GIFT", "SAMPLE", "MERCHANDISE", "HUMANITARIAN_DONATION", "RETURN_MERCHANDISE", "OTHER")
    non_delivery_option: Action if undeliverable ("ABANDON" = dispose, "RETURN" = return to sender)
    certify: Must be True — certifies the declaration is accurate
    certify_signer: Full name of person certifying (e.g., the user's name)
    items: List of customs item object_ids (from create_shippo_customs_item)
    contents_explanation: Required when contents_type is "OTHER" (optional otherwise)
    exporter_reference: Exporter reference (optional)
    importer_reference: Importer reference (optional)
    invoice: Invoice number (optional)
    eel_pfc: EEL/PFC code for US exports over $2500 (e.g., "NOEEI_30_37_a") (optional)
    incoterm: Incoterm — "DDU" (buyer pays duties) or "DDP" (seller pays duties) (optional)
    metadata: Custom metadata (optional)

Returns:
    Created customs declaration with object_id — pass this to create_shippo_shipment

tools.name: get_shippo_customs_declarations
tools.description:
Get a single customs declaration by ID or list all declarations.

Args:
    object_id: Declaration object_id (optional; if omitted, lists all)

Returns:
    Single declaration or paginated list

tools.name: create_shippo_shipment
tools.description:
Create a shipment and get available shipping rates from multiple carriers.

IMPORTANT: Pass address dicts inline (with name, street1, city, state, zip, country fields).
Only pass an object_id string if the address was already created in a previous step
and you have its ID available.

Args:
    address_from: Sender address as a dict with keys: name, street1, city, state, zip, country.
        Alternatively, pass a Shippo address object_id string if one already exists.
    address_to: Recipient address dict with the same keys, or an existing object_id string.
    parcels: List of parcel dicts with keys: length, width, height, distance_unit, weight, mass_unit.
        Alternatively, pass parcel object_id strings if parcels were previously created.
    customs_declaration: Customs declaration object_id for international shipments (optional)
    extra: Extra shipment options like signature_confirmation, insurance, etc. (optional)
    metadata: Custom metadata (optional)

Returns:
    Shipment object with shipment_id and rates array containing rate_id, amount, currency, provider, servicelevel, estimated_days

tools.name: get_shippo_shipments
tools.description:
Retrieve shipment records — the shipping requests you created (with sender/recipient addresses, parcels, and available rates).

This is NOT for labels or tracking. Use get_shippo_transactions for purchased label records,
or track_shippo_shipment for package tracking status.

Args:
    object_id: Shipment object_id (optional; if omitted, lists all shipments)

Returns:
    Single shipment object (with addresses, parcels, rates) or paginated list

tools.name: get_shippo_rates
tools.description:
Retrieve rate quotes for an existing shipment. Rates are generated when you create a shipment
via create_shippo_shipment — use this to re-fetch them later.

Args:
    shipment_id: Shipment object_id to get rates for (optional)
    rate_id: Specific rate object_id to retrieve (optional)

Returns:
    Rate object or list of rates for the shipment

tools.name: purchase_shippo_label
tools.description:
Purchase a shipping label (transaction) using a selected rate.

Args:
    rate_id: Rate object_id from create_shippo_shipment results
    label_file_type: Label format — "PDF", "PDF_4x6", "PNG", "ZPL" (default "PDF")
    metadata: Custom metadata (optional)

Returns:
    Transaction object with transaction_id, label_url, tracking_number, tracking_url_provider, eta

tools.name: get_shippo_transactions
tools.description:
Retrieve purchased shipping label records (transactions). Each transaction represents
a label you bought via purchase_shippo_label, containing the label PDF URL and tracking number.

This is NOT for listing shipments/quotes — use get_shippo_shipments for that.

Common workflow for "today's USPS labels":
    get_shippo_transactions(carrier="usps", object_status="SUCCESS",
                            created_after="2026-05-26T00:00:00Z")

Args:
    object_id: Transaction object_id (optional; if provided, fetches single transaction)
    object_status: Filter by status: "SUCCESS", "ERROR", "QUEUED", "WAITING" (optional)
    tracking_status: Filter by tracking: "UNKNOWN", "PRE_TRANSIT", "TRANSIT", "DELIVERED" (optional)
    carrier: Filter by carrier name, e.g., "usps", "ups", "fedex" (optional, client-side filter)
    created_after: Only include transactions created on/after this ISO 8601 timestamp,
        e.g., "2026-05-26T00:00:00Z" for today's labels (optional, client-side filter)
    fetch_all_pages: Auto-paginate to retrieve all transactions (default True)

Returns:
    Single transaction (when object_id given), or {"results": [...], "count": N}

tools.name: track_shippo_shipment
tools.description:
Look up current tracking status and history for a package (one-time query).

Use this when a user asks "where is my package" or "check tracking status".

Args:
    carrier: Carrier token (e.g., "usps", "ups", "fedex", "dhl_express").
        In test mode, use "shippo" as the carrier with test tracking numbers like SHIPPO_TRANSIT or SHIPPO_DELIVERED.
    tracking_number: Carrier-specific tracking number

Returns:
    Tracking object with tracking_status (current status), tracking_history array, eta, and carrier details

tools.name: create_shippo_manifest
tools.description:
Create a manifest (SCAN form / 当日交单清单) — a carrier end-of-day closeout document
bundling multiple labels submitted to USPS/DHL after all labels are purchased for the day.

PREREQUISITE WORKFLOW:
    1. Call get_shippo_carrier_accounts(carrier="usps") to find the USPS carrier_account.
    2. If results is empty, STOP and tell the user:
       "您的 Shippo 账户里没有 active 的 USPS 承运商，请先在 Shippo Dashboard
       → Settings → Carrier Accounts 添加 USPS。"
       Do NOT search filesystem, environment variables, source code, or SQLite databases
       for carrier IDs — they are ONLY available via get_shippo_carrier_accounts.
    3. Pass results[0].object_id as carrier_account.

PARAMETERS YOU DO NOT NEED TO PRE-COMPUTE:
    - You do NOT need to list transactions manually. If the user says "include all today's
      transactions", simply omit the transactions parameter — Shippo will automatically
      include all eligible (unmanifested, SUCCESS-status) transactions for the carrier.
    - Just construct the address dict directly from the user's input
      (street1/city/state/zip/country fields).

Args:
    carrier_account: Carrier account object_id (32-char hex from get_shippo_carrier_accounts)
    shipment_date: ISO format, e.g., "2026-05-26T00:00:00Z"
    address_from: Origin address dict, e.g.,
        {"street1": "215 Clayton St", "city": "San Francisco", "state": "CA",
         "zip": "94117", "country": "US"}
    transactions: Specific transaction object_ids (optional; omit to auto-include all eligible)

Returns:
    Manifest object with status and documents. Note: status may be PENDING initially —
    poll get_shippo_manifests(object_id) until status=SUCCESS to get the final PDF URL.

tools.name: get_shippo_manifests
tools.description:
Get a single manifest by ID or list all manifests.

Args:
    object_id: Manifest object_id (optional; if omitted, lists all)

Returns:
    Single manifest or paginated list

tools.name: create_shippo_pickup
tools.description:
Schedule a USPS/DHL Express carrier pickup (预约上门取件).
The carrier driver will come to your address at the requested time window to collect
the packages whose labels you've already purchased today.

PREREQUISITE WORKFLOW (must be done in order):
    1. get_shippo_carrier_accounts(carrier="usps") → find USPS carrier_account.
       If empty, STOP and tell user to add USPS in Shippo Dashboard.
    2. get_shippo_transactions(object_status="SUCCESS",
                               created_after=<today_iso>)
       → collect transaction object_ids for today's labels.
       If empty, STOP and tell user: "您今天还没有购买任何运单，无法预约取件。
       请先用 purchase_shippo_label 购买标签。"
    3. Call this tool with the gathered IDs.

Do NOT search filesystem/env vars/source code for any of these IDs.

LOCATION DICT STRUCTURE (Shippo's required nested format):
    {
        "building_location_type": "Front Door",
        "building_type": "apartment",
        "address": {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "street1": "215 Clayton St",
            "city": "San Francisco",
            "state": "CA",
            "zip": "94117",
            "country": "US"
        }
    }
    building_location_type: "Front Door", "Knock on Door", "In/At Mailbox", "Reception", etc.
    building_type: "apartment", "building", "department", "floor", "room", "suite"

USPS BUSINESS RULE: Only ONE pickup per account/address per day.
    Do NOT call this twice for the same address on the same day.
    If already scheduled today, tell the user: "您今天已经预约过 USPS 取件了，
    把后续包裹放在同一位置即可，司机会一并带走，无需重复预约。"

WARNING: is_test=False will schedule a REAL carrier pickup.
    Always pass is_test=True in evaluation/testing contexts.

Args:
    carrier_account: Carrier account object_id from get_shippo_carrier_accounts
    location: Pickup location dict with "building_location_type", "building_type", and "address" (see above)
    transactions: List of transaction object_ids (REQUIRED — pickup must be tied to labels)
    requested_start_time: Earliest pickup time, ISO 8601 (e.g., "2026-05-27T14:00:00Z")
    requested_end_time: Latest pickup time, ISO 8601 (e.g., "2026-05-27T17:00:00Z")
    is_test: Set True for testing (default False — production behavior)

Returns:
    Pickup confirmation with confirmation_code, location, and status

tools.name: create_shippo_refund
tools.description:
Request a refund/void for a purchased shipping label (退款 / 作废面单 / cancel label).

Use this when a user wants to cancel a label they already bought. The label must not
have been used (scanned by carrier). Refund processing typically takes 5-14 days.

WORKFLOW: If the user says "refund my last label" or "cancel that shipment":
1. Call get_shippo_transactions to find the transaction object_id
2. Call this tool with that transaction ID

Args:
    transaction: Transaction object_id to refund (from get_shippo_transactions or purchase_shippo_label result)

Returns:
    Refund object with status (QUEUED/PENDING/SUCCESS/ERROR)

tools.name: get_shippo_refunds
tools.description:
Get a single refund by ID or list all refunds.

Args:
    object_id: Refund object_id (optional; if omitted, lists all)

Returns:
    Single refund or paginated list

tools.name: set_twilio_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Twilio credentials.

The credentials are stored securely and used for all Twilio communication tools.
To get your credentials, log into https://console.twilio.com/ and copy the
Account SID and Auth Token from the Account Info card.

tools.name: check_twilio_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of Twilio credentials.

This tool checks if credentials exist and verifies their validity against the

tools.name: delete_twilio_credentials

Delete Twilio credentials for the current account.

After deletion, you will need to set new credentials to use Twilio tools.

Returns:
