tools.name: send_twilio_sms
tools.description:
Send an SMS or MMS message via Twilio Programmable Messaging.

Either ``from_`` (a Twilio phone number you own, in E.164 format) OR
``messaging_service_sid`` (a Messaging Service SID, starts with ``MG``)
must be provided. ``media_url`` turns the message into an MMS.

Args:
    to: Destination phone number in E.164 format (e.g., "+14155552671").
    body: Message text (up to 1600 characters).
    from_: Twilio phone number to send from (E.164). Optional if
        ``messaging_service_sid`` is provided.
    messaging_service_sid: Twilio Messaging Service SID (starts with "MG").
        Optional if ``from_`` is provided.
    media_url: Optional list of public HTTPS URLs to attach as MMS media.
    status_callback: Optional public HTTPS URL Twilio will POST delivery
        status to.

Returns:
    The Twilio Message resource (sid, status, to, from, body, ...).

tools.name: send_twilio_whatsapp_message
tools.description:
Send a WhatsApp message via Twilio.

The Programmable Messaging endpoint is reused — ``to``/``from_`` are
automatically prefixed with ``whatsapp:`` if not already.

Args:
    to: Destination phone number in E.164 format (e.g., "+14155552671").
        ``whatsapp:`` prefix is added automatically if missing.
    body: Free-form WhatsApp message text. Required for free-form sessions
        (within the 24-hour customer service window). For template
        messages, use ``content_sid`` instead.
    from_: Twilio WhatsApp-enabled sender (E.164). Optional if
        ``messaging_service_sid`` is provided. ``whatsapp:`` prefix is
        added automatically.
    content_sid: Twilio Content Template SID (starts with ``HX``) for
        sending an approved template message.
    content_variables: JSON string mapping template variable indices to
        values, e.g., ``'{"1":"John","2":"12345"}'``.
    messaging_service_sid: Optional Twilio Messaging Service SID.

Returns:
    The Twilio Message resource.

tools.name: list_twilio_messages
tools.description:
List Twilio messages (sent and received), optionally filtered by participants
and time range.

Args:
    to: Filter messages sent to this E.164 phone number.
    from_: Filter messages sent from this E.164 phone number.
    date_sent_after: Only return messages sent after this UTC ISO-8601
        datetime (e.g. ``"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"``). Mapped to Twilio's
        ``DateSent>=`` query parameter.
    date_sent_before: Only return messages sent before this UTC ISO-8601
        datetime. Mapped to Twilio's ``DateSent<=`` query parameter.
    page_size: Number of records per page (1-1000). Defaults to 20.

Returns:
    The Twilio Messages list resource (``messages`` array + paging info).

tools.name: get_twilio_message
tools.description:
Fetch a single Twilio message by its SID.

Args:
    message_sid: Twilio Message SID (starts with "SM" for SMS or "MM" for MMS).

Returns:
    The Twilio Message resource.

tools.name: make_twilio_call
tools.description:
Initiate an outbound Twilio voice call.

Either ``url`` (a public URL returning TwiML) or ``twiml`` (an inline
TwiML XML string) must be provided. ``url`` is preferred for dynamic
call flows.

Args:
    to: Destination phone number in E.164 format (e.g., "+14155552671").
    from_: Twilio voice-enabled phone number to call from (E.164).
    url: Public URL Twilio fetches when the call connects. Must return
        valid TwiML. One of ``url`` / ``twiml`` is required.
    twiml: Inline TwiML XML string. One of ``url`` / ``twiml`` is required.
    method: HTTP method Twilio uses to fetch ``url`` ("GET" or "POST").
        Defaults to "POST".
    status_callback: Public URL Twilio POSTs call status events to.
    record: Whether to record the call. Defaults to False.
    timeout: Number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer
        before giving up (5-600). Defaults to 60.

Returns:
    The Twilio Call resource (sid, status, to, from, ...).

tools.name: list_twilio_calls
tools.description:
List Twilio voice calls, optionally filtered by participants and time range.

Args:
    to: Filter calls placed to this E.164 phone number.
    from_: Filter calls placed from this E.164 phone number.
    status: Filter by call status, e.g., ``"queued" | "ringing" |
        "in-progress" | "completed" | "busy" | "failed" | "no-answer" |
        "canceled"``.
    start_time_after: Only return calls started after this UTC ISO-8601
        datetime. Mapped to ``StartTime>=``.
    start_time_before: Only return calls started before this UTC ISO-8601
        datetime. Mapped to ``StartTime<=``.
    page_size: Number of records per page (1-1000). Defaults to 20.

Returns:
    The Twilio Calls list resource.

tools.name: get_twilio_call
tools.description:
Fetch a single Twilio call by its SID.

Args:
    call_sid: Twilio Call SID (starts with "CA").

Returns:
    The Twilio Call resource.

tools.name: list_twilio_phone_numbers
tools.description:
List the phone numbers owned by the connected Twilio account
(incoming/provisioned numbers).

Args:
    phone_number: Optional filter — only return numbers matching this
        partial or full phone number string.
    friendly_name: Optional filter — only return numbers whose
        friendly name matches this string.
    page_size: Number of records per page (1-1000). Defaults to 50.

Returns:
    The Twilio IncomingPhoneNumbers list resource.

tools.name: search_twilio_available_numbers
tools.description:
Search Twilio's inventory of available local phone numbers in a country.

Args:
    iso_country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., "US", "GB").
    area_code: Optional filter by area code (typically NANP countries).
    contains: Optional digit pattern the phone number must contain.
        ``*`` is a wildcard (e.g., ``"510***1234"``).
    sms_enabled: If True, only return SMS-capable numbers.
    voice_enabled: If True, only return voice-capable numbers.
    mms_enabled: If True, only return MMS-capable numbers.
    page_size: Number of records per page (1-1000). Defaults to 20.

Returns:
    The Twilio AvailablePhoneNumbers (Local) list resource.

tools.name: send_twilio_verification
tools.description:
Send a verification code (OTP) via Twilio Verify v2.

Args:
    service_sid: Twilio Verify Service SID (starts with "VA"). Created in
        Twilio Console under Verify → Services.
    to: Destination — typically an E.164 phone number for sms/call/whatsapp,
        or an email address for the email channel.
    channel: Verification channel: ``"sms" | "call" | "whatsapp" | "email"``.
    locale: Optional language locale for the message (e.g., "en", "zh").
    custom_code: Optional pre-generated code (must be enabled on the
        Verify Service). If omitted, Twilio generates one.

Returns:
    The Verify Verification resource (sid, status, to, channel, ...).

tools.name: check_twilio_verification
tools.description:
Check a verification code submitted by a user via Twilio Verify v2.

Args:
    service_sid: Twilio Verify Service SID (starts with "VA"), same one
        used in ``send_twilio_verification``.
    to: Same destination value used to send the verification (E.164 phone
        number or email).
    code: The OTP code the user entered.

Returns:
    The Verify VerificationCheck resource (with ``status`` field — usually
    ``"approved"`` on success or ``"pending"`` on mismatch).

tools.name: get_twilio_account
tools.description:
Fetch the connected Twilio Account resource.

Returns the account sid, friendly name, status (active/suspended/closed),
type (Trial/Full), and date_created/date_updated metadata. Useful for
confirming the account is still active and identifying its type.

Returns:
    The Twilio Account resource.

tools.name: set_creatify_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Creatify API credentials for the current user.

**When to call this tool:**
- When the user wants to connect their Creatify account for AI video generation.
- When the user provides a Creatify API ID and API Key.
- When the user says they want to use Creatify features (URL-to-video, AI avatars, etc.).

The credentials are verified against the live Creatify API before being stored.
If verification fails, an error message is returned and nothing is persisted.

To obtain API credentials, visit: https://app.creatify.ai/settings/organization/api

Args:
    api_id: Creatify API ID (also called x-api-id or client_id).
            Found in the Creatify dashboard under Settings > API.
    api_key: Creatify API Key (also called x-api-key or client_secret).
             Found in the Creatify dashboard under Settings > API.

Returns:
    On success: A confirmation message containing "connected" and a list of
                available Creatify capabilities.
    On failure: A human-readable error message explaining what went wrong.

Example:
    set_creatify_credentials(
        api_id="xxxx",
        api_key="xxx"
    )

tools.name: check_creatify_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the current user's Creatify API credentials.

**When to call this tool:**
- When the user asks if their Creatify account is connected.
- When a Creatify operation fails and you need to verify credential status.
- When the user wants to see their Creatify connection info.

This tool retrieves stored credentials and re-verifies them against the
live Creatify API. It does NOT expose the actual credential values.

Returns:
    Credential status including validity, API ID prefix, and creation time.

Example:
    check_creatify_credentials()

tools.name: delete_creatify_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Creatify API credentials.

**When to call this tool:**
- When the user wants to disconnect their Creatify account.
- When the user wants to remove stored credentials.
- When the user wants to re-link a different Creatify account.

After deletion, the user will need to call `set_creatify_credentials`
again to use Creatify features.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_creatify_credentials()

tools.name: create_url_to_video
tools.description:
Convert any product / landing-page URL into a short-form video ad.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user pastes a product URL (Amazon / Shopify / TikTok Shop / brand site)
  and asks for an ad video, demo video, or social-media video.
- The user wants Creatify to auto-extract title / images / videos from a
  landing page and turn them into a vertical TikTok-style video.

**Pipeline (this tool wraps two API calls):**
1. `POST /api/links/`            — scrape the URL → `link_id`
2. `POST /api/link_to_videos/`   — create an async video job from `link_id`

Args:
    url: Required. The full product/landing page URL to scrape.
    target_platform: Target platform, default ``"tiktok"``. Common values:
        ``"tiktok"``, ``"instagram"``, ``"youtube"``, ``"facebook"``.
    target_audience: Free-text audience description, e.g. ``"young adults
        who care about clean beauty"``. Optional.
    language: BCP-47-ish language code (``en``, ``zh``, ``es``, ``fr``,
        ``de``, ``ja``, ``ko`` …). Default ``"en"``.
    video_length: Duration in seconds. Allowed: ``15`` / ``30`` / ``45`` /
        ``60``. Default ``15``.
    aspect_ratio: Allowed: ``"16x9"`` / ``"9x16"`` / ``"1x1"``. Default ``"9x16"``.
    script_style: Optional script template, e.g. ``"DiscoveryWriter"``,
        ``"BenefitsV2"``, ``"ProblemSolutionV2"``. See Creatify docs for
        the full enum.
    visual_style: Optional visual template, e.g. ``"AvatarBubbleTemplate"``.
    override_avatar: Optional avatar_id (UUID) — fetch from the Creatify
        ``GET /api/personas/`` endpoint. If omitted, Creatify auto-matches.
    override_voice: Optional voice_id (UUID) — fetch from
        ``GET /api/voices/``. If omitted, Creatify uses the avatar's
        default voice.
    name: Optional human-readable name for the resulting video.
    no_background_music: If True, disables the auto background music.
    webhook_url: Optional callback URL — Creatify will POST job results to it.
    extra: Optional dict of additional Creatify fields to pass through
        verbatim (e.g. ``{"caption_setting": {...}}``). Caller wins on
        duplicate keys. Example:
        ``extra={"caption_setting": {"style": "normal-black"}}``.

Returns:
    On success — text summary + JSON containing ``id``, ``status``,
    ``progress`` etc. The ``id`` is the link_to_videos job id; poll with
    ``get_video_status(task_id=..., task_type="url_to_video")``.
    On failure — single-line error code + actionable hint.

Example:
    create_url_to_video(
        url="https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09JZXHJM7",
        target_platform="tiktok",
        language="en",
        video_length=30,
        aspect_ratio="9x16",
        script_style="BenefitsV2",
    )

tools.name: create_avatar_video
tools.description:
Create a single-scene AI Avatar lipsync video (Creatify Lipsync v1).

**When to call this tool:**
- The user wants a "talking avatar" video for a single piece of script.
- Scenarios: explainer videos, product pitches, training intros,
  one-shot social videos.
- For multi-scene / multi-character conversations, use
  ``create_multi_avatar_conversation`` instead.

**API:** ``POST /api/lipsyncs/``

Args:
    text: Required. The script the avatar will speak.
    creator: Required. The avatar_id (UUID). Fetch from
        ``GET /api/personas/`` in the Creatify dashboard or API.
    aspect_ratio: ``"9x16"`` (default) / ``"16x9"`` / ``"1x1"``.
    voice_id: Optional voice UUID; if omitted, the avatar's default voice
        is used.
    accent: Optional accent UUID (each voice has multiple accents — pick
        the ``id`` from the ``accents`` array of ``GET /api/voices/``).
    audio_url: Optional. If provided, Creatify uses this audio file
        instead of synthesizing voice from ``text``.
    name: Optional human-readable video name.
    green_screen: If True, render with a green-screen background.
    no_caption: If True, disable burned-in captions.
    caption_setting: Optional dict for caption styling, e.g.
        ``{"style": "normal-black", "font_family": "Montserrat",
            "offset": {"x": 0, "y": 0.45}}``.
    webhook_url: Optional callback URL.
    extra: Pass-through dict for any other Creatify lipsync fields.

Returns:
    On success — summary + JSON with ``id``, ``status``. Poll with
    ``get_video_status(task_id=..., task_type="lipsync")``.
    On failure — single-line error with actionable hint.

Example:
    create_avatar_video(
        text="Hi! Today I want to show you our new clean beauty cream.",
        creator="7350375b-9a98-51b8-934d-14d46a645dc2",
        aspect_ratio="9x16",
        voice_id="6f8ca7a8-87b9-4f5d-905d-cc4598e79717",
    )

tools.name: create_multi_avatar_conversation
tools.description:
Create a multi-scene / multi-avatar video using Creatify Lipsync v2.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user wants two or more avatars taking turns speaking
  (e.g. a "conversation" or "interview" video).
- The user wants different backgrounds, captions, or voices per scene.
- For a single-shot single-speaker video, use ``create_avatar_video``.

**API:** ``POST /api/lipsyncs_v2/``

Args:
    video_inputs: Required. A non-empty list of segment dicts. Each
        segment represents one scene (one speaker turn) with the
        following structure (only ``character`` and ``voice`` are
        required, every other key is optional):

        ```jsonc
        {
          "character": {                       // REQUIRED
            "type": "avatar",                  // fixed value
            "avatar_id": "<uuid>",             // REQUIRED, from list_personas
            "avatar_style": "normal",          // avatar render style
            "offset": {"x": -0.23, "y": 0.35}, // position offset, -1..1
            "scale": 1.0,                       // 0..N, default 1.0
            "hidden": false                     // hide avatar (audio-only scene)
          },
          "voice": {                            // REQUIRED
            "type": "text",                    // "text" or "audio"
            "input_text": "...",               // required when type=text
            "voice_id": "<uuid>",              // accent id from list_voices
            "volume": 0.8                       // 0..1
          },
          "background": {                       // optional
            "type": "image",                   // "image" or "video"
            "url": "https://...",
            "fit": "crop",                     // crop / contain / cover
            "effect": null
          },
          "caption_setting": {                  // optional
            "style": "normal-black",           // preset style name
            "offset": {"x": 0, "y": 0.45},
            "font_family": "Montserrat",
            "font_size": 70,
            "font_style": null,
            "background_color": null,
            "text_color": null,
            "highlight_text_color": null,
            "max_width": null,
            "line_height": null,
            "text_shadow": null,
            "hidden": false                     // disable burned-in captions
          },
          "transition_effect": {                // optional, scene-to-scene
            "transition_in": null,
            "transition_out": null
          },
          "visual_style": null                  // optional
        }
        ```

        See https://docs.creatify.ai/api-documentation/ai-avatar/lipsync-v2
        for the authoritative spec.
    aspect_ratio: ``"9x16"`` (default) / ``"16x9"`` / ``"1x1"``.
    model_version: ``"standard"`` / ``"aurora_v1"`` / ``"aurora_v1_fast"``
        (default). ``aurora_v1`` gives the highest quality but costs more.
    name: Optional video name.
    webhook_url: Optional callback URL invoked when the job completes.
    extra: Pass-through dict for any other top-level v2 fields not
        modeled above (e.g. future server-side options).

Returns:
    On success — summary + JSON with ``id``. Poll with
    ``get_video_status(task_id=..., task_type="lipsync_v2")``.
    On failure — single-line error reason + actionable hint.

Example:
    create_multi_avatar_conversation(
        video_inputs=[
            {
                "character": {
                    "type": "avatar",
                    "avatar_id": "7350375b-9a98-51b8-934d-14d46a645dc2",
                    "avatar_style": "normal",
                    "offset": {"x": -0.23, "y": 0.35},
                },
                "voice": {
                    "type": "text",
                    "input_text": "Have you tried this?",
                    "voice_id": "6f8ca7a8-87b9-4f5d-905d-cc4598e79717",
                },
                "background": {
                    "type": "image",
                    "url": "https://video.creatify.ai/bg.jpg",
                },
                "caption_setting": {
                    "style": "normal-black",
                    "offset": {"x": 0, "y": 0.45},
                },
            },
            {
                "character": {
                    "type": "avatar",
                    "avatar_id": "18fccce8-86e7-5f31-abc8-18915cb872be",
                },
                "voice": {
                    "type": "text",
                    "input_text": "Yes, I love it!",
                    "voice_id": "360ab221-d951-413b-ba1a-7037dc67da16",
                },
            },
        ],
        aspect_ratio="9x16",
        model_version="aurora_v1_fast",
    )

tools.name: create_ai_shorts
tools.description:
Create a short-form viral video (TikTok / Reels / YouTube Shorts) from a
text script using Creatify AI Shorts.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user already has (or has just generated via ``generate_ai_script``)
  a finished video script and wants to render it into a vertical
  short-form video.
- For URL/link-based input, use ``create_url_to_video`` instead.
- For avatar-driven monologues, use ``create_avatar_video``.

**API:** ``POST /api/ai_shorts/`` — costs 5 credits per 30s.

.. note::
    The official endpoint takes a finished ``script`` (not a creative
    prompt). To turn a topic / brief into a script, first call
    ``generate_ai_script`` and feed its output here.

Args:
    script: Required. Finished video script text to be rendered.
    aspect_ratio: Required. ``"9x16"`` (default) / ``"16x9"`` / ``"1x1"``.
    style: Required. Visual style preset. Allowed values (case-sensitive):
        ``"4K realistic"`` / ``"3D"`` / ``"Cinematic"`` (default) /
        ``"Cartoonish"`` / ``"Line art"`` / ``"Pixel art"`` /
        ``"Mysterious"`` / ``"Steam punk"`` / ``"Collage"`` / ``"Kawaii"``.
    accent: Optional voice accent UUID — use the ``id`` from a voice's
        ``accents`` array in ``list_voices``. Omit to use the default
        voice associated with the chosen ``style``.
    caption_setting: Optional caption styling dict. Recognized keys:
        ``style`` (e.g. ``"normal-black"`` / ``"normal-white"`` / ``"neo"``
        / ``"brick"`` / ``"frenzy"`` / ``"verana"`` / ``"mustard"`` /
        ``"glow"`` / ``"mint"`` / ``"coolers"`` / ``"bilo"`` / ``"toons"``
        / ``"deep-blue"`` / ``"mystique"`` / ``"caution"`` / ``"duality"``
        / ...), plus ``font_family`` / ``font_size`` / ``offset`` etc.
    background_music_url: Optional URL of a custom BGM track. Omit to
        let Creatify pick a random track.
    background_music_volume: Optional float in ``[0.0, 1.0]``.
        Omit to use the style's default BGM volume.
    voiceover_volume: Optional float in ``[0.0, 1.0]``.
        Omit to use the style's default voiceover volume.
    webhook_url: Optional callback URL invoked when the job completes.
    extra: Pass-through dict for any additional fields the official API
        adds in the future.

Returns:
    On success — JSON with job ``id``. Poll with
    ``get_video_status(task_id=..., task_type="ai_shorts")``.
    On failure — single-line error reason + actionable hint.

Example:
    create_ai_shorts(
        script="3 reasons clean-beauty body cream is worth trying...",
        aspect_ratio="9x16",
        style="Cinematic",
        background_music_volume=0.6,
    )

tools.name: generate_ai_script
tools.description:
Generate AI-powered marketing video scripts (1 credit per call).

**When to call this tool:**
- The user wants a "script first, video later" workflow — preview the
  copy before spending credits on video rendering.
- The user provides EITHER a product URL OR a (title, description) pair.

**Input modes (at least one required):**
- ``url`` — let Creatify scrape product info from the URL.
- ``title`` (+ optional ``description``) — caller already has product copy.

**API:** ``POST /api/ai_scripts/``  (schema ``AiScriptJob``)

Args:
    url: Optional. Product / landing-page URL — Creatify will scrape it.
    title: Optional. Product / topic title (used when no URL is given).
    description: Optional. Long-form description for context.
    language: ISO language code (default ``"en"``). Allowed (76 codes):
        ``af`` / ``ar`` / ``as`` / ``az`` / ``be`` / ``bg`` / ``bn`` / ``bs``
        / ``ca`` / ``cb`` / ``cs`` / ``cy`` / ``da`` / ``de`` / ``el`` /
        ``en`` / ``es`` / ``et`` / ``fa`` / ``fi`` / ``fl`` / ``fr`` / ``ga``
        / ``gl`` / ``gu`` / ``ha`` / ``he`` / ``hi`` / ``hr`` / ``hu`` /
        ``hy`` / ``id`` / ``is`` / ``it`` / ``ja`` / ``jv`` / ``ka`` /
        ``kk`` / ``kn`` / ``ko`` / ``ky`` / ``lb`` / ``ln`` / ``lt`` /
        ``lv`` / ``mk`` / ``ml`` / ``mr`` / ``ms`` / ``ne`` / ``nl`` /
        ``no`` / ``ny`` / ``pa`` / ``pl`` / ``ps`` / ``pt`` / ``ro`` /
        ``ru`` / ``sd`` / ``sk`` / ``sl`` / ``so`` / ``sr`` / ``sv`` /
        ``sw`` / ``ta`` / ``te`` / ``th`` / ``tl`` / ``tr`` / ``uk`` /
        ``ur`` / ``vi`` / ``zh``.
    target_audience: Optional audience description (free-text).
    video_length: Length in seconds. Allowed: ``15`` / ``30`` / ``45`` /
        ``60``. Default ``30``.
    script_styles: Optional list of script-style templates to generate
        (max 5 items). If omitted, Creatify generates 4 random styles.
        Allowed (19 case-sensitive enum values, choose any subset):
        ``BenefitsV2`` (Benefits) / ``BrandStoryV2`` (Brand Story) /
        ``CallToActionV2`` (Call To Action) / ``DiscoveryWriter`` (Discovery)
        / ``DontWorryWriter`` (Don't Worry) / ``EmotionalWriter`` (Emotional)
        / ``GenzWriter`` (Gen Z) / ``HowToV2`` (How To) /
        ``LetMeShowYouWriter`` (Let Me Show You) / ``MotivationalWriter``
        (Motivational) / ``ProblemSolutionV2`` (Problem Solution) /
        ``ProblemSolutionWriter`` (Problem-Solution) / ``ProductHighlightsV2``
        (Product Highlights) / ``ProductLifestyleV2`` (Product Lifestyle) /
        ``ResponseBubbleWriter`` (Response Bubble) / ``SpecialOffersV2``
        (Special Offers) / ``StoryTimeWriter`` (Storytime) /
        ``ThreeReasonsWriter`` (3 Reasons Why) / ``TrendingTopicsV2``
        (Trending Topics).
        Note: this enum is **smaller** than the ``script_style`` enum used
        by ``create_url_to_video`` (which also accepts hook variants).
    extra: Optional dict of additional Creatify fields to pass through
        verbatim. Caller wins on duplicate keys.

Returns:
    On success — JSON string of the ``AiScriptJob`` response, including
    ``id`` (UUID), ``status`` (``pending`` / ``in_queue`` / ``running`` /
    ``failed`` / ``done`` / ``rejected``), ``generated_scripts`` (list of
    ``{paragraphs, script_name, script_style, title}``), ``product``,
    ``credits_used``. Use the ``id`` to poll progress via
    ``get_video_status(task_id=..., task_type="ai_script")``.
    On failure — single-line error payload with code + actionable hint.

Example:
    generate_ai_script(
        url="https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09JZXHJM7",
        language="en",
        video_length=30,
        script_styles=["BenefitsV2", "ProblemSolutionV2"],
    )

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description:
List the available Creatify AI voices and their accents.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user / agent needs an ``accent`` UUID to call
  ``create_avatar_video`` (``voice_id`` / ``accent`` field) or
  ``create_multi_avatar_conversation``.
- The user asks "what voices do I have" / "show me available languages".

**API:** ``GET /api/voices/``

Args:
    page: Optional. 1-based page number.
    page_size: Optional. Page size (Creatify default if omitted).
    gender: Optional client-side hint (e.g. ``"male"`` / ``"female"``)
        — passed through as a query param if the API supports it.
    language: Optional language filter (e.g. ``"en"`` / ``"zh"``).

Returns:
    On success: a human-readable summary (count) + the full JSON list.
        Each voice item has an ``id`` and an ``accents`` array; **the
        ``accent`` value used elsewhere is ``accents[*].id``**, not the
        voice id itself.
    On failure: a single-line error reason + an actionable hint.

Example:
    list_voices(language="en", page_size=50)

tools.name: list_personas
tools.description:
List available Creatify avatars (personas), including built-ins and BYOA.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user / agent needs a ``creator`` UUID to call
  ``create_avatar_video`` or ``create_multi_avatar_conversation``.
- The user asks "what avatars do I have" / "show me my custom avatars" /
  "are there any female presenter avatars I can use".

**API:** ``GET /api/personas/``

All filter params accept a single value or a comma-separated multi-value
string (e.g. ``gender="f,nb"``). To filter only BYOA-trained avatars,
fetch the full list and filter client-side by each item's ``type`` field
(the official API does NOT expose an ``is_custom`` query param).

Args:
    page: Optional. 1-based page number.
    page_size: Optional. Page size (Creatify default if omitted).
    gender: Optional. Comma-separated. Allowed values:
        ``m`` (Male) / ``f`` (Female) / ``nb`` (Non-Binary).
    style: Optional. Comma-separated. Allowed values:
        ``selfie`` / ``presenter`` / ``other``.
    age_range: Optional. Comma-separated. Allowed values:
        ``child`` / ``teen`` / ``adult`` / ``senior``.
    location: Optional. Comma-separated. Allowed values:
        ``outdoor`` / ``fantasy`` / ``indoor`` / ``other``.
    suitable_industries: Optional. Comma-separated industry names
        (e.g. ``"Beauty & Personal Care,E-Commerce,Tech & Electronics"``).
        Full list: Apparel & Accessories, Appliances, Apps,
        Baby Kids & Maternity, Beauty & Personal Care, Business Services,
        E-Commerce, Education, Financial Services, Food & Beverage, Games,
        Health, Home Improvement, Household Products, Life Services,
        News & Entertainment, Pets, Sports & Outdoors, Tech & Electronics,
        Travel, Vehicle & Transportation, Others.

Returns:
    On success: a human-readable summary (count) + the full JSON list.
        Each persona item exposes an ``id`` — use it as the ``creator``
        param of ``create_avatar_video`` /
        ``create_multi_avatar_conversation``.
    On failure: a single-line error reason + an actionable hint.

Example:
    list_personas(gender="f", style="presenter", age_range="adult")

tools.name: get_video_status
tools.description:
Poll the status of any Creatify asynchronous job.

**When to call this tool:**
- After any of the ``create_*`` / ``generate_*`` tools returned a
  ``job_id`` / ``task_id`` and you need to know whether the job is
  ``pending`` / ``in_progress`` / ``done`` / ``failed``.
- To retrieve the final ``output`` / ``media_url`` / ``audio_url`` for
  a finished job.

**Routing:** ``task_type`` is mapped to the matching Creatify resource:
- ``url_to_video``       → ``GET /api/link_to_videos/{id}/``
- ``lipsync`` / ``avatar_video``
                          → ``GET /api/lipsyncs/{id}/``
- ``lipsync_v2`` / ``multi_avatar``
                          → ``GET /api/lipsyncs_v2/{id}/``
- ``ai_shorts``          → ``GET /api/ai_shorts/{id}/``
- ``ai_editing`` / ``ai_edited``
                          → ``GET /api/ai_editing/{id}/``
- ``custom_template``    → ``GET /api/custom_template_jobs/{id}/``
- ``aurora``             → ``GET /api/aurora/{id}/``
- ``ai_script``          → ``GET /api/ai_scripts/{id}/``
- ``tts`` / ``text_to_speech``
                          → ``GET /api/text-to-speech/{id}/``
- ``custom_avatar``      → ``GET /api/custom_avatars/{id}/``

Args:
    task_id: Required. The id returned by the corresponding ``create_*``
        tool (Creatify usually formats this as a UUID).
    task_type: Required. One of the keys listed above.

Returns:
    On success: a human-readable summary (status / progress / output URL /
    failed_reason) + a JSON snippet of the full response.
    On failure: a single-line error reason + an actionable hint
    (e.g. unknown task_type / not connected / not found).

Example:
    get_video_status(task_id="6f4f1f4b-...-abcd", task_type="url_to_video")

tools.name: get_remaining_credits
tools.description:
Get the remaining Creatify credits for the current user's workspace.

**When to call this tool:**
- The user asks "how many Creatify credits do I have left?" /
  "am I going to run out of credits?".
- Before launching an expensive batch of video generations, to check
  whether the workspace has enough credits.
- When a previous generation tool returned a quota / payment error and
  you want to confirm the balance.

**API:** ``GET /api/remaining_credits/``

Args: (none)

Returns:
    On success: a human-readable summary (credits balance) + the full
    JSON snippet from Creatify.
    On failure: a single-line error reason + an actionable hint
    (e.g. reconnect / retry / check input).

Example:
    get_remaining_credits()

tools.name: set_semrush_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Semrush API credentials for a user.

The credentials are stored securely under the current user_id and used for all Semrush tools.
Different user_ids can use the same API Key - each user_id has its own credential storage.
To get your API Key, visit: https://www.semrush.com/kb/92-api-key

Args:
    api_key: Semrush API Key

Returns:
    Success or error message

Example:
    set_semrush_credentials(
        api_key="se_xxxxx"
    )

tools.name: check_semrush_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of a user's Semrush API credentials.

This tool checks if credentials exist and verifies their validity against the Semrush API.
It does NOT expose the actual credential values.

Returns:
    Credential status information

Example:
    check_semrush_credentials()

tools.name: delete_semrush_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current accio_id's Semrush API credentials.

This tool removes the stored credentials for a user. After deletion,
the user will need to set new credentials to use Semrush tools.

Returns:
    Success or error message

Example:
    delete_semrush_credentials()

tools.name: get_domain_organic_keywords
tools.description:
Get organic search keywords that bring traffic to a domain.

**When to use this tool:**
- Analyze a competitor's organic search strategy
- Discover which keywords drive organic traffic to any domain
- Research keyword rankings and traffic estimates

**Parameters:**
- domain: Domain name to analyze (e.g., "example.com")
- database: Regional database code (default: "us")
  Common values: "us" (United States), "uk" (United Kingdom), "de" (Germany), 
  "fr" (France), "es" (Spain), "it" (Italy), "ca" (Canada), "au" (Australia)
- display_limit: Number of results to return (default: 100, max: 100000)

**Returns:**
- Success: List of organic keywords with position, volume, and traffic data
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
get_domain_organic_keywords(
    domain="example.com",
    database="us",
    display_limit=50
)
```

tools.name: get_domain_paid_keywords
tools.description:
Get paid search keywords (Google Ads) for a domain.

**When to use this tool:**
- Analyze a competitor's paid search advertising strategy
- Discover which keywords a domain is bidding on in Google Ads
- Research competitor ad spend and keyword targeting

**Parameters:**
- domain: Domain name to analyze (e.g., "example.com")
- database: Regional database code (default: "us")
  Common values: "us", "uk", "de", "fr", "es", "it", "ca", "au"
- display_limit: Number of results to return (default: 100, max: 100000)

**Returns:**
- Success: List of paid keywords with position, volume, and CPC data
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
get_domain_paid_keywords(
    domain="example.com",
    database="us",
    display_limit=50
)
```

tools.name: get_domain_overview
tools.description:
Get comprehensive SEO overview for a domain.

**When to use this tool:**
- Get a quick snapshot of a domain's SEO performance
- Analyze key metrics like organic traffic, paid traffic, and backlinks
- Compare SEO performance across different time periods

**Parameters:**
- domain: Domain name to analyze (e.g., "example.com")
- database: Regional database code (default: "us")
  Common values: "us", "uk", "de", "fr", "es", "it", "ca", "au"
- display_date: Optional historical date (format: "YYYYMM", e.g., "202401")
  If not specified, returns the latest available data

**Returns:**
- Success: Domain overview with key SEO metrics
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
get_domain_overview(
    domain="example.com",
    database="us"
)

# Get historical data
get_domain_overview(
    domain="example.com",
    database="us",
    display_date="202401"
)
```

tools.name: get_keyword_overview
tools.description:
Get keyword overview data including volume, CPC, and competition.

**When to use this tool:**
- Research keyword search volume and competition levels
- Analyze keyword value for SEO and PPC campaigns
- Compare keyword performance across different regional databases

**Parameters:**
- phrase: Keyword or phrase to analyze (e.g., "seo services")
- database: Optional regional database code (e.g., "us", "uk", "de")
  If not specified, returns data for all available databases

**Returns:**
- Success: Keyword data with volume, CPC, competition across databases
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
# Get data for all databases
get_keyword_overview(phrase="seo services")

# Get data for specific database
get_keyword_overview(phrase="seo services", database="us")
```

tools.name: get_domain_ranks_all
tools.description:
Get domain overview across all regional databases.

**When to use this tool:**
- Analyze domain performance across all global databases
- Compare domain visibility in different regions and countries
- Get comprehensive domain metrics from multiple sources

**Parameters:**
- domain: Domain to analyze (e.g., "apple.com")
- database: Optional regional database code (e.g., "us", "uk")
  If not specified, returns data for all available databases
- display_limit: Number of results to return (max 100,000)
- display_date: Date for historical data in YYYYMM15 format

**Returns:**
- Success: Domain rankings across databases with organic/paid metrics
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
# Get data for all databases
get_domain_ranks_all(domain="apple.com")

# Get data for specific database with historical data
get_domain_ranks_all(domain="apple.com", database="us", display_date="20231215")
```

tools.name: get_domain_rank_history
tools.description:
Get domain ranking history over time (monthly or daily).

**When to use this tool:**
- Track domain ranking changes over time
- Analyze historical performance trends
- Monitor the impact of SEO campaigns and strategies

**Parameters:**
- domain: Domain to analyze (e.g., "apple.com")
- database: Regional database code (e.g., "us", "uk", "de")
- display_limit: Number of historical records to return (max 100,000)
- display_daily: Get daily updates for last 30+ days (true/false)
  If not specified, returns monthly data

**Returns:**
- Success: Historical ranking data with dates and metrics
- Error: Error message with actionable guidance

**Example:**
```python
# Get monthly history
get_domain_rank_history(domain="apple.com", database="us", display_limit=12)

# Get daily history for last 30 days
get_domain_rank_history(domain="apple.com", database="us", display_daily=True, display_limit=30)
```

tools.name: get_domain_ranks_all_json
tools.description:
Get domain rankings across all databases in JSON format.

Returns the domain's ranking metrics (organic/paid keywords and traffic)
across all supported databases in a structured JSON format for programmatic use.

Args:
    domain: The domain to analyze (e.g., "apple.com")
    display_limit: Maximum number of database results to return (default: 20)
    
Returns:
    JSON string containing domain rankings across all databases
    
Example:
    {
        "domain": "apple.com",

tools.name: set_cloudinary_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Cloudinary API credentials for the current user.

Trigger scenarios:
  - User connects Cloudinary connector for the first time (called by desktop client).
  - User updates / rotates API Key (re-invoked to overwrite stored credentials).

Args:
    cloud_name: The 'Cloud name' shown in Cloudinary Console Dashboard
                (e.g. "dxyz1abc2").
    api_key:    Numeric API Key (typically 15 digits) from Console → API Keys.
    api_secret: API Secret from Console → API Keys (sensitive, never logged).

Behavior:
  1. Validates all three fields are non-empty.
  2. Calls GET https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/{cloud_name}/usage with Basic Auth
     to verify credentials against the real Cloudinary service.
     - 200: credentials valid.
     - 401: credentials rejected (bad api_key or api_secret).
     - 404: cloud_name not found.
     - Other 4xx/5xx: service error.
  3. On success, persists to credential_store (isolated by accio_id) and updates
     the auth index so it appears in /auth/authorizations.

Returns:
  - Success: human-readable text containing 'connected'.
  - Failure: single-line human-readable error (no stack trace).

Example:
    set_cloudinary_credentials(
        cloud_name="demo",
        api_key="123456789012345",
        api_secret="abcDEF..."
    )

tools.name: check_cloudinary_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the current user's Cloudinary API credentials.

This tool checks if credentials exist and optionally re-verifies them
against the Cloudinary API. It does NOT expose the actual API Secret.

Returns:
    Credential status information including cloud_name, validity, and creation time.

Example:

tools.name: cloudinary_upload
tools.description:
Upload an image, video, or raw file to Cloudinary.

When to call:
  - User wants to upload a local file or remote URL to Cloudinary.
  - User wants to save media assets to their Cloudinary cloud with folder/tag organization.
  - User needs to upload and simultaneously apply an eager transformation.

Args:
    file: Source of the file to upload. Must be one of:
          - Remote URL (e.g. "https://example.com/image.png")
          - Base64 data URI (e.g. "data:image/png;base64,...")
          Note: Local file paths are NOT supported because the service runs remotely
          and cannot access files on your local machine.
    public_id: Custom resource identifier. If omitted, Cloudinary generates one.
               Example: "marketing/banner_2026"
    folder: Destination folder prefix. Example: "marketing/banners"
            If omitted and no public_id with path, goes to root.
    tags: List of string tags to attach. Example: ["campaign-2026", "hero"]
    resource_type: "auto" (default, auto-detect), "image", "video", or "raw".
    asset_type: Delivery type — "upload" (public), "authenticated" (signed URL needed),
                or "private". Default: "upload".
    overwrite: Whether to overwrite an existing resource with same public_id.
               Default: False.
    transformation: Eager transformations to generate on upload. Each item is a dict
                   of transformation parameters.
                   Example: [{"width": 300, "height": 200, "crop": "fill"}]

Returns:
    On success: JSON with public_id, secure_url, format, width, height, bytes, version.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_upload(
        file="https://example.com/banner.jpg",
        folder="marketing",
        tags=["campaign-2026"],
    )

tools.name: cloudinary_list_resources
tools.description:

When to call:

  - User wants to browse resources before performing operations.

Args:
    resource_type: "image" (default), "video", or "raw".
    delivery_type: Delivery type filter — "upload" (default), "authenticated", "private".
    prefix: Folder prefix filter. Example: "marketing/" lists all in marketing folder.
    tag: Filter by tag. Example: "campaign-2026" shows only tagged resources.
    max_results: Number of results to return, 1-500 (default: 30).
    next_cursor: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass to get next page.

Returns:
    On success: JSON with resources array (public_id, format, url, bytes, created_at)
                and next_cursor for pagination.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_list_resources(prefix="marketing/", max_results=10)

tools.name: cloudinary_search
tools.description:
Advanced search for resources using Cloudinary search expressions.

When to call:
  - User needs to find resources with complex filters (date range, size, format, etc.).
  - User asks "find all PNGs larger than 1MB" or "images uploaded this week".
  - More powerful than cloudinary_list_resources for complex queries.

Args:
    expression: Cloudinary search expression. Examples:
                - "folder:marketing/*" — all in marketing folder
                - "tags=campaign-2026" — by tag
                - "format=png AND bytes>1000000" — PNGs > 1MB
                - "created_at>[2026-05-01]" — uploaded after date
                - "resource_type:video" — only videos
                See: https://cloudinary.com/documentation/search_api#expressions
    sort_by: Field to sort by. Options: "created_at", "public_id", "bytes", "width".
             Default: relevance.
    sort_order: "asc" or "desc" (default: "desc").
    max_results: Number of results, 1-500 (default: 30).
    next_cursor: Pagination cursor from previous response.

Returns:
    On success: JSON with resources array and pagination info.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_search(expression="folder:marketing/* AND format=jpg", max_results=10)
