    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_add_tag(tag="approved", public_ids=["marketing/banner_v2"])

tools.name: cloudinary_remove_tag
tools.description:
Remove a tag from one or more resources.

When to call:
  - User wants to remove a tag/label from specific resources.
  - User says "untag X from these images" or "remove label Y from resource Z".

Args:
    tag: Tag string to remove. Example: "draft"
    public_ids: List of public_ids to untag. Example: ["marketing/banner_old"]
    resource_type: "image" (default), "video", or "raw".

Returns:
    On success: JSON confirming untagged public_ids.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_remove_tag(tag="draft", public_ids=["marketing/banner_old"])

tools.name: cloudinary_build_url
tools.description:
Build a Cloudinary transformation/delivery URL without making any API call.

When to call:
  - User wants to generate a CDN URL for an existing Cloudinary resource.
  - User needs a URL with specific transformations (resize, crop, format, quality).
  - User asks for thumbnail URLs or optimized versions of an image/video.
  - This tool does NOT upload or modify resources — it only constructs URLs.

Args:
    public_id: The public_id of the resource (e.g. "marketing/banner").
    transformation: List of transformation step dicts. Each dict maps parameter
                   names to values. Common parameters:
                   - width/height: pixel dimensions
                   - crop: "fill", "fit", "limit", "scale", "thumb", "pad"
                   - gravity: "auto", "face", "center", "north", etc.
                   - quality: "auto", "auto:good", "auto:best", or 1-100
                   - fetch_format: "auto", "webp", "avif", "jpg", "png"
                   - effect: "blur:300", "grayscale", "sepia", etc.
                   - overlay: text or image overlay identifier

                   Example — 300x200 center crop with auto quality:
                   [{"width": 300, "height": 200, "crop": "fill", "gravity": "auto",
                     "quality": "auto", "fetch_format": "auto"}]

                   Example — chain two steps (resize then overlay):
                   [
                     {"width": 800, "crop": "limit"},
                     {"overlay": "watermark", "gravity": "south_east", "x": 10, "y": 10}
                   ]
    resource_type: "image" (default), "video", or "raw".
    delivery_type: "upload" (default, public) or "fetch" (remote URL proxy).
    format: Force output format extension (e.g. "webp", "jpg", "png", "mp4").
            If omitted, uses original format.
    secure: Use HTTPS (default: True).

Returns:
    On success: The constructed Cloudinary delivery URL string.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_build_url(
        public_id="marketing/banner",
        transformation=[{"width": 300, "height": 200, "crop": "fill", "quality": "auto", "fetch_format": "auto"}],
        format="webp"
    )
    → "https://res.cloudinary.com/my-cloud/image/upload/c_fill,f_auto,h_200,q_auto,w_300/marketing/banner.webp"

tools.name: cloudinary_signed_url
tools.description:
Generate a signed delivery URL for authenticated or private resources.

When to call:
  - User needs to access a resource that was uploaded with type="authenticated" or "private".
  - User wants to share a time-limited access link for a protected asset.
  - Regular (unsigned) URLs will return 401 for authenticated/private resources.

Args:
    public_id: The public_id of the protected resource. Example: "private/confidential_doc"
    transformation: Optional transformation steps (same format as cloudinary_build_url).
                   Example: [{"width": 400, "crop": "limit"}]
    resource_type: "image" (default), "video", or "raw".
    delivery_type: "authenticated" (default) or "private".
    format: Force output format extension. Example: "jpg"
    expires_in: URL expiry time in seconds from now. Example: 3600 (1 hour).
               If omitted, the signed URL is permanent (still protected by signature).
               Note: Expired URLs will return 401.

Returns:
    On success: The signed Cloudinary delivery URL string.
                If expires_in is set, includes a note about expiry time.
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example:
    cloudinary_signed_url(
        public_id="private/contract_scan",
        expires_in=86400
    )
    → "https://res.cloudinary.com/my-cloud/image/authenticated/s--abc12345--/private/contract_scan"

tools.name: cloudinary_get_usage
tools.description:
Query the current month's Cloudinary account usage and credit balance.

When to call:
  - User asks about remaining Cloudinary credits or quota.
  - User wants to check storage/bandwidth usage before a bulk operation.
  - Before batch uploads/transforms, to verify sufficient credit remains.
  - User asks "how much Cloudinary quota do I have left" or "show my usage".

Args:
    None (credentials are resolved automatically from the connected account).

Returns:
    On success: JSON with plan name, credit usage, storage usage, bandwidth usage,
                transformation counts, and object counts.
                Key fields:
                - plan: account plan name (e.g. "free")
                - credits.usage: credits used this period (out of credits.limit)
                - storage.usage: bytes stored
                - bandwidth.usage: bytes transferred this period
                - transformations.usage: transformation count this period
                - objects.usage: total stored objects count
    On failure: Human-readable error with action guidance.

Example output:
    {
      "plan": "free",
      "credits": {"usage": 3.2, "limit": 25.0, "used_percent": "12.8%"},
      "storage": {"usage_bytes": 52428800, "usage_display": "50.0 MB"},
      "bandwidth": {"usage_bytes": 104857600, "usage_display": "100.0 MB"},
      "transformations": {"usage": 1234, "limit": 25000},
      "objects": {"usage": 89}
    }

tools.name: set_yuque_credentials
tools.description:
Set, update, or disconnect Yuque personal access token for the current user.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Yuque (语雀) account,
or when a Yuque API call returns 401/403 indicating the token is missing or expired.

**How to obtain a token:**
The user should visit https://www.yuque.com/settings/tokens to generate a
personal access token with the required scopes.

**Team space support:**
If the user wants to access a team/organization space, they should provide
the ``space_domain`` parameter. This is the subdomain of the team space
(found in Space Management > Settings > Space Info). For example, if the
team's URL is https://myteam.yuque.com, then space_domain is "myteam".
When space_domain is set, all subsequent Yuque API calls will be routed to
the team space endpoint automatically.

**Disconnect:**
Passing an empty string for token is the connector-level disconnect contract.
The stored credential is removed idempotently and no Yuque API verification is performed.

**Verification:**
Before storing, the token is verified against the Yuque API (GET /api/v2/user).
If space_domain is provided, verification uses the team space endpoint.
If verification fails, the token is NOT stored and a human-readable error is returned.

Args:
    token: Yuque personal access token. Empty string means disconnect.
    space_domain: Optional team space subdomain (e.g. "myteam").
        Set this when the user needs to access a team/organization's knowledge bases.
        Leave empty or None for personal space (default).

Returns:
    - On success: a message containing "connected" along with the Yuque username.
    - On empty token: a message containing "disconnected".
    - On failure: a structured JSON error with code and message.

Example:
    set_yuque_credentials(token="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx")
    set_yuque_credentials(token="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", space_domain="myteam")
    set_yuque_credentials(token="")

tools.name: check_yuque_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of the current user's Yuque credentials.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user asks whether Yuque is connected,
or before performing a Yuque operation to confirm auth status.

This tool checks if credentials exist and re-verifies the token against the Yuque API.
It does NOT expose the actual token value.

Returns:
    Credential status information including validity, login, and creation time.

Example:
    check_yuque_credentials()

tools.name: delete_yuque_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Yuque credentials.

**When to trigger:**
Call this tool when the user wants to disconnect their Yuque account
or revoke access.

After deletion, the user will need to set new credentials to use Yuque tools.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_yuque_credentials()

tools.name: yuque_get_user
tools.description:
Get the current authenticated Yuque user's profile information.

**When to call:**
- The user asks "who am I on Yuque" or wants to verify their connected Yuque account.
- Before performing operations that need the user's login or id (e.g. creating a book
  under the user's namespace).

**No parameters required.** The credential is resolved from the current session.

Returns:
    On success — human-readable summary plus JSON:
    ```json
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "login": "zhangsan",
      "name": "张三",
      "avatar_url": "https://...",
      "description": "...",
      "books_count": 10,
      "followers_count": 5
    }
    ```
    On failure — single-line error with actionable guidance, e.g.:
    "**Error (YUQUE_NOT_CONNECTED):** Yuque account is not connected. Please use …"

tools.name: yuque_list_user_groups
tools.description:
List all teams/groups that a user belongs to.

**When to call:**
- The user asks "what teams am I in on Yuque" or wants to see their team list.
- Before performing team-level operations (e.g. listing a team's knowledge bases),
  you need to find the team's login name.
- Typical flow: call ``yuque_get_user`` to get the user's login, then call this tool.

Args:
    login: The user's login name or ID (required). Get it from ``yuque_get_user``.
    role: Optional role filter. 0 = admin only, 1 = member only.
        If not provided, returns all groups regardless of role.
    offset: Pagination offset (default 0). PageSize is fixed at 100.
        Use offset=100 for the second page, offset=200 for the third, etc.

Returns:
    On success — human-readable list of teams plus JSON array:
    ```json
    [
      {
        "id": 123,
        "login": "my-team",
        "name": "我的团队",
        "books_count": 10,
        "members_count": 5,
        "description": "..."
      }
    ]
    ```
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

Example:
    yuque_list_user_groups(login="zhangsan")
    yuque_list_user_groups(login="zhangsan", role=0)  # only teams where user is admin

tools.name: yuque_search
tools.description:
Search for documents or knowledge bases in the user's Yuque workspace.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to find a document or knowledge base by keyword.
- The user asks "search Yuque for …" or "find my doc about …".

Args:
    q: Search keyword (required, max 200 characters). E.g. "项目设计文档".
    type: Resource type to search (required). Options: "doc" (documents, default), "repo" (knowledge bases).
    page: Page number for pagination (default 1, range 1-100). PageSize is fixed at 20.
        Increment by 1 to load next page.
    scope: Optional search scope to limit results.
        E.g. "group_a" (search within a group), "group_a/book_x" (search within a specific repo).
        If not provided, searches the current user/team.
    creator: Optional filter by author login. Only return results authored by this user.

Returns:
    On success — human-readable summary plus JSON with search hits:
    ```json
    {
      "total": 42,
      "page": 1,
      "hits": [
        {"id": 1, "title": "...", "slug": "...", "book_id": 2, "summary": "..."}
      ]
    }
    ```
    On failure — single-line error with actionable guidance.

Example:
    yuque_search(q="API设计", type="doc", page=1)

tools.name: yuque_list_books
tools.description:
List all knowledge bases (repos) owned by a user or group.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to see all their knowledge bases or a team's knowledge bases.
- You need to find a specific knowledge base by name before performing operations on it.
- Typical flow: call ``yuque_get_user`` first to obtain the user's ``login``,
  then call this tool to list their knowledge bases.

Args:
    login: Owner's login name (required). Use user login for personal books,
        or group login for team books. Get it from ``yuque_get_user``.
    owner_type: Owner type. "user" (default) for personal books,
        "group" for team/organization books.
    type: Filter by repo type. "Book" (default) for standard knowledge bases,
        "Design" for design repos. Leave as "Book" in most cases.
    offset: Pagination offset (default 0). Use to paginate through large lists.

Returns:
    On success — human-readable list of knowledge bases plus JSON array:
    ```json
    [{"id": 12345, "slug": "my-book", "name": "我的知识库", "items_count": 30}, ...]
    ```
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

Example:
    yuque_list_books(login="zhangsan")
    yuque_list_books(login="my-team", owner_type="group")

tools.name: yuque_get_book
tools.description:
Get detailed information of a single Yuque knowledge base (repo).

**When to call:**
- The user asks about a specific knowledge base's metadata (name, description, doc count, etc.).
- You need to verify whether a knowledge base exists before listing its docs.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        Can be a numeric id (e.g. "12345") or a namespace string (e.g. "zhangsan/my-book").

Returns:
    On success — human-readable summary plus JSON with book details:
    ```json
    {"id": 12345, "slug": "my-book", "name": "我的知识库", "items_count": 30, ...}
    ```
    On failure — error with actionable guidance.

Example:
    yuque_get_book(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book")

tools.name: yuque_create_book
tools.description:
Create a new Yuque knowledge base under the given user or group.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to create a new knowledge base / repo.
- Typical flow: call ``yuque_get_user`` first to obtain the user's ``login``,
  then call this tool with that login.

Args:
    login: Owner's login name (required). Use user login for personal books,
        or group login for team books. Get it from ``yuque_get_user``.
    name: Display name of the knowledge base (required). E.g. "产品需求文档".
    slug: URL slug (required, alphanumeric + hyphen). E.g. "product-requirements".
    description: Optional description text.
    public: Visibility. 0 = private (default), 1 = public on the internet,
        2 = visible within the team space.
    type: Repo type. "Book" (default) for standard knowledge base.
    owner_type: Owner type. "user" (default) for personal books,
        "group" for team/organization books.
    enhanced_privacy: Optional. When True, enables enhanced privacy mode for the repo.

Returns:
    On success — summary plus JSON of the created book.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_create_book(login="zhangsan", name="项目文档", slug="project-docs")
    yuque_create_book(login="my-team", name="团队文档", slug="team-docs", owner_type="group")

tools.name: yuque_update_book
tools.description:
Update an existing Yuque knowledge base's metadata.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to rename, change visibility, or update the description of a knowledge base.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    name: New display name (optional, only updated if provided).
    slug: New URL slug (optional).
    description: New description (optional).
    public: New visibility (optional). 0 = private, 1 = public, 2 = team-visible.
    toc: New table of contents in Markdown format (optional).
        Use this to reorder the entire TOC at once.

Returns:
    On success — updated book details as JSON.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_update_book(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book", name="新名称", public=1)

tools.name: yuque_list_docs
tools.description:
List all documents in a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user asks "what docs are in this book" or wants to browse a knowledge base.
- You need to find a specific document's slug or id before reading it.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    limit: Number of docs to return per page (default 100, max 100).
    optional_properties: Comma-separated list of extra fields to include in the response.
        Supported values: "hits", "tags", "latest_version_id".
        E.g. "hits,tags" to include read counts and tags.

Returns:
    On success — list of documents with id, title, slug, updated_at:
    ```json
    {
      "count": 30,
      "docs": [
        {"id": 1, "slug": "intro", "title": "简介", "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
      ]
    }
    ```
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_list_docs(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book")

tools.name: yuque_get_doc
tools.description:
Get the full content of a single document in a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to read a specific document.
- You need the body/content of a doc (e.g. for summarization or editing).

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    slug_or_id: The document slug or numeric id (required).
        E.g. "getting-started" or "67890".
    raw: Whether to return raw Markdown body. 1 = yes (default), 0 = rendered HTML body.
    page: Page number for data-table type documents (default 1, min 1).
        Only used when the document is a Yuque data table (sheet).

Returns:
    On success — document title, body (Markdown or HTML), and metadata JSON.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_get_doc(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book", slug_or_id="getting-started")

tools.name: yuque_create_doc
tools.description:
Create a new document in a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to write / publish a new document.
- **Important:** After creating, you MUST call **yuque_update_toc** with
  `action="appendNode"`, `action_mode="child"`, `type="DOC"`, and `doc_ids=[<doc_id>]`
  to add the new doc to the book's table of contents.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    title: Document title (required). E.g. "API 设计规范".
    body: Document content (default empty string).
        For Markdown format, write standard Markdown.
        For HTML format, write standard HTML.
        For Lake format, use Yuque Lake AST JSON.
    slug: URL-friendly slug (optional, auto-generated from title if omitted).
    format: Content format. "markdown" (default), "html", or "lake" (Yuque rich text).
    public: Visibility. 0 = follow book setting (default), 1 = public.

Returns:
    On success — created document summary plus JSON.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_create_doc(
        namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book",
        title="快速入门",
        body="# 快速入门\n\n本文档介绍如何开始使用…",
        format="markdown"
    )

tools.name: yuque_update_doc
tools.description:
Update an existing document in a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to edit the title, content, or visibility of an existing doc.
- Use ``yuque_list_docs`` or ``yuque_search`` first to find the doc_id.

**IMPORTANT — Confirmation required before calling:**
Before invoking this tool, you MUST present the full updated content (title and/or body)
to the user and explicitly ask for their confirmation. Only call this tool after the user
confirms the changes are correct. This prevents accidental overwrites of document content.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
    doc_id: Numeric document id (required, integer). Get from list_docs or search.
    title: New title (optional, only updated if provided).
    body: New body content in the document's format (optional).
    slug: New URL slug (optional).
    public: New visibility (optional). 0 = follow book setting, 1 = public.

Returns:
    On success — updated document summary plus JSON.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_update_doc(
        namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book",
        doc_id=67890,
        title="更新后的标题",
        body="# 更新后的内容\n\n…"
    )

tools.name: yuque_get_toc
tools.description:
Get the table of contents (TOC) tree of a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to see the structure / outline of a knowledge base.
- You need to understand the hierarchy of documents before rearranging them.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".

Returns:
    On success — JSON array of TOC nodes. Each node has:
    ```json
    [
      {"id": "abc", "type": "DOC", "title": "简介", "slug": "intro",
       "doc_id": 123, "level": 0, "parent_uuid": "", "uuid": "abc"}
    ]
    ```
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_get_toc(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book")

tools.name: yuque_update_toc
tools.description:
Update the table of contents of a Yuque knowledge base (add / move / edit / remove nodes).

**When to call:**
- After creating a new document, to add it to the TOC.
- The user wants to reorganise the TOC: move a doc, add a group/link node, or remove a node.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    action: The TOC mutation action (required). Supported values:
        "appendNode"  — append a node at the tail (under target or root).
        "prependNode" — prepend a node at the head (under target or root).
            Note: prependNode is NOT supported for sibling creation.
        "editNode"    — edit an existing node's properties.
        "removeNode"  — remove a node from the TOC (does NOT delete the doc itself).
            When action_mode="sibling": delete current node only.
            When action_mode="child": delete current node and all its children.
    action_mode: Operation mode (required). Supported values:
        "child"   — operate as a child of the target node (or root if target_uuid is empty).
        "sibling" — operate as a sibling after the target node.
    target_uuid: Target node UUID (optional). Defaults to root if not provided.
        Get this from yuque_get_toc. Used for positioning in create/move scenarios.
    node_uuid: The node UUID to operate on (required for move/edit/remove).
        Get this from yuque_get_toc.
    doc_ids: Array of document IDs (required when creating DOC nodes).
        E.g. [12345] or [111, 222] for batch insertion.
    type: Node type (required when creating). Values:
        "DOC"   — document node (requires doc_ids).
        "TITLE" — group/section node (requires title).
        "LINK"  — external link node (requires title + url + open_window).
    title: Node title (required for creating TITLE/LINK nodes; optional for editNode).
    url: External URL (required for creating LINK nodes; optional for editNode).
    open_window: Whether to open in new window (required for LINK creation).
        0 = open in current page (default), 1 = open in new window.
    visible: Node visibility (optional). 0 = hidden, 1 = visible (default).

Returns:
    On success — updated TOC JSON.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example — Add a new doc to TOC:
    yuque_update_toc(
        namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book",
        action="appendNode",
        action_mode="child",
        doc_ids=[99999],
        type="DOC"
    )

Example — Remove a node:
    yuque_update_toc(
        namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book",
        action="removeNode",
        action_mode="child",
        node_uuid="abc-def-ghi"
    )

tools.name: yuque_delete_doc
tools.description:
Delete a document from a Yuque knowledge base.

**When to call:**
- The user wants to permanently delete a document.
- Use ``yuque_list_docs`` or ``yuque_search`` first to find the doc_id.

**⚠️ IMPORTANT — User confirmation required:**
This operation is **irreversible**. Before calling this tool, you MUST:
1. Clearly inform the user that the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.
2. Show the document information (title, id, knowledge base) to be deleted.
3. Explicitly ask the user to confirm the deletion.
4. Only after the user gives an affirmative reply (e.g. "确认删除", "是", "yes"),
   call this tool with ``confirm=True``.
If the user does not confirm, do NOT call this tool.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".
    doc_id: Numeric document id (required, integer). Get from list_docs or search.
    confirm: Safety flag. Must be True to execute the deletion.
        Set to True only after the user explicitly confirms.

Returns:
    On success — confirmation message.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_delete_doc(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/my-book", doc_id=67890, confirm=True)

tools.name: yuque_delete_book
tools.description:
Delete a Yuque knowledge base (repo) permanently.

**When to call:**
- The user explicitly wants to delete an entire knowledge base.
- **Warning:** This is a destructive operation. All documents within the knowledge base
  will also be deleted and CANNOT be recovered.

**IMPORTANT — Confirmation required before calling:**
Before invoking this tool, you MUST clearly inform the user that this operation is
irreversible and will permanently delete all documents in the knowledge base. List the
knowledge base name/id and explicitly ask the user to confirm the deletion. Only call
this tool after the user confirms.

Args:
    namespace_or_id: The knowledge base identifier (required).
        E.g. "zhangsan/my-book" or "12345".

Returns:
    On success — confirmation message.
    On failure — error with guidance.

Example:
    yuque_delete_book(namespace_or_id="zhangsan/old-book")

tools.name: start_cj_auth
tools.description: Start CJ authorization flow.

tools.name: get_cj_access_token
tools.description: Get the current workspace CJ access token.

tools.name: start_square_auth
tools.description:
Manually initiate Square POS OAuth authentication flow.

NOTE: This tool should typically NOT be called directly. The authentication system
automatically handles credential checks and prompts for authentication when needed.
Only use this tool if:
1. You need to re-authenticate with different credentials
2. You want to proactively authenticate before using other tools
3. The automatic authentication flow failed and you need to retry

In most cases, simply try calling the Square POS tool you need - it will
automatically handle authentication if required.

Args:
    merchant_label: Optional label to identify the merchant (for display purposes only).

Returns:
    A formatted message with authentication instructions and URL.

tools.name: start_alibaba_com_auth
tools.description:
Generate an Alibaba second-party authorization login URL.

This tool generates a login URL that users can visit to authorize their
Alibaba account. After successful authentication, the user will be
redirected to the configured callback URL with an access token.

The authorization flow:
1. User visits the generated login URL
2. User authenticates with Alibaba
3. User is redirected to callback with access_token
4. Backend validates token via RLAB two-step exchange and stores credential

Args:
    lang: Language preference for the callback page ('en' or 'zh').
          Defaults to 'en'.

Returns:
    JSON string containing:
    - login_url: The complete login URL for user to visit
    - callback_url: The callback URL that will receive the access token
    - note: Instructions or notes about the login process

tools.name: exchange_alibaba_connector_token
tools.description:
Exchange and store Alibaba OAuth access_token from local callback via MCP.

This tool is used by Phoenix PC SDK when the OAuth callback is handled locally
(instead of by MCP server). The MCP server will:
  1. Exchange access_token via RLAB two-step (accessToken → token → aliId)
  2. Store the resulting token + aliId in Redis

Args:
    access_token: OAuth access_token from Alibaba callback.
    state: Optional opaque state passed through from the login flow.

Returns:
    JSON string containing:
    - ok: Whether the exchange succeeded
    - provider: Always "alibaba"
    - accio_id: The accio_id this credential belongs to
    - ali_id: The Alibaba user ID
    - email: The Alibaba account email when returned by RLAB
    - error_message: Error message if failed

tools.name: start_ali1688_auth
tools.description: Generate a 1688 OAuth authorization URL.

tools.name: exchange_ali1688_connector_code
tools.description: Exchange and store a 1688 OAuth code from the Phoenix PC local callback.

tools.name: start_taobao_auth
tools.description:
Generate a Taobao OAuth authorization URL.

This tool generates a login URL that users can visit to authorize their
Taobao account. After successful authentication, the user will be
redirected to the configured callback URL with an authorization code.

The authorization flow:
1. User visits the generated login URL
2. User authenticates with Taobao
3. User is redirected to callback with authorization code
4. Backend exchanges code for access_token and stores credential

Args:
    lang: Language preference for the callback page ('en' or 'zh').
          Defaults to 'en'.

Returns:
    JSON string containing:
    - login_url: The complete authorization URL for user to visit
    - callback_url: The callback URL that will receive the code
    - note: Instructions about the login process

tools.name: start_shopline_auth
tools.description: Start Shopline authorization for a store.

tools.name: get_shopline_access_token
tools.description: Get Shopline token metadata only; this does not return the raw access token value.

tools.name: get_shopline_access_token_raw
tools.description: Get the raw Shopline access token when you explicitly need the token value itself.

tools.name: claim_shopline_store
tools.description:
Claim a pending Shopline store installation to the current workspace.

Use this tool when a Shopline store was installed from the marketplace
and needs to be linked to the current Accio workspace. The binding_code
is displayed on the Shopline app page after installation.

Args:
    handle: The Shopline store handle (e.g., 'my-store')
    binding_code: The binding code shown on the Shopline app page (e.g., 'XXXXX-XXXXX')

tools.name: start_okki_auth
tools.description:
Start Okki OAuth authorization flow (PKCE mode).

Generates an authorization URL for the user to connect their Okki account.

tools.name: start_visable_auth
tools.description:
Start Visable OAuth authorization flow (PKCE mode).

Generates an authorization URL for the user to connect their Visable account.
Visable is a B2B supplier discovery platform (wlw.de / europages.com).

tools.name: start_asana_auth
tools.description:
Start Asana OAuth 2.0 authorization flow.

When to call:
    - When a user clicks "Connect Asana" in Accio Settings -> Connectors.
    - When a skill needs Asana access but no valid credential exists for the current workspace.
    - When the existing Asana token has expired and re-authorization is required.

Returns:
    A human-readable Markdown message containing the Asana authorization URL.
    The user must open this URL in a browser to complete the OAuth consent.
    After successful authorization, the callback route automatically persists
    the access token and the connection becomes active.

Raises:
    No exceptions are raised to the caller; errors are returned as formatted strings.

Example:
    ```
    result = await start_asana_auth()
    # Returns: "**Complete Asana authorization**\n\nShare this link with the user..."
    ```

tools.name: disconnect_asana
tools.description:
Disconnect (remove) a linked Asana account.

When to call:
    - When a user clicks "Disconnect Asana" in Accio Settings -> Connectors.
    - When a user explicitly asks to remove their Asana connection.

If multiple Asana accounts are connected, pass the user_id of the one
to remove.  If only one account is connected, user_id can be omitted and
it will be removed automatically.

Args:
    user_id: Asana user gid to disconnect (optional when only one exists).

Returns:
    A human-readable message indicating success or failure.
    Success text always contains "disconnected".

tools.name: get_asana_me
tools.description:
Get the currently authenticated Asana user's profile and workspaces.

When to call:
    - First thing after connecting Asana — to obtain workspace_gid.
    - When the user asks "who am I on Asana?" or "show my Asana profile".

Returns:
    JSON with user gid, name, email, and workspaces list.

tools.name: list_asana_tasks
tools.description:
List tasks from a project, or tasks assigned to a user in a workspace.

When to call:
    - "Show me all tasks in project X"
    - "What tasks are assigned to me?"

You MUST provide either ``project_gid`` OR (``workspace_gid`` + ``assignee``).

Args:
    project_gid: Filter by project GID (from ``list_asana_projects``).
    workspace_gid: Filter by workspace GID (requires ``assignee``).
    assignee: Assignee user GID or "me" (requires ``workspace_gid``).
    completed_since: Use "now" for only incomplete tasks (optional).
    limit: Max results per page (1-100, default 20).

Returns:
    JSON with tasks array.

tools.name: get_asana_task
tools.description:
Get full details of a single Asana task.

Args:
    task_gid: The task GID (from ``list_asana_tasks``).

Returns:
    JSON with task details including name, notes, assignee, due_on, status.

tools.name: create_asana_task
tools.description:
Create a new task in Asana.

You must provide at least ``workspace_gid`` OR ``project_gid``.

Args:
    name: Task title (required).
    workspace_gid: Workspace GID — required if ``project_gid`` is not given.
    project_gid: Add the task to this project (optional).
    assignee: Assignee user GID or "me" (optional).
    notes: Task description (optional).
    due_on: Due date in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional).

Returns:
    JSON of the created task including its new GID.

tools.name: update_asana_task
tools.description:
Update an existing Asana task.

When to call:
    - "Mark task X as complete"
    - "Rename task X to Y"
    - "Assign task X to user Z"

Only the fields you provide will be updated.

Args:
    task_gid: The task GID to update (required).
    name: New task title (optional).
    completed: Set to true to mark complete, false to reopen (optional).
    assignee: New assignee user GID or "me" (optional).
    notes: New description (optional).
    due_on: New due date YYYY-MM-DD, or empty string to clear (optional).

Returns:
    JSON of the updated task.

tools.name: list_asana_projects
tools.description:
List projects in a workspace.

When to call:
    - "Show me all projects"
    - When you need a project_gid for task listing or creation.

Args:
    workspace_gid: Workspace GID (from ``get_asana_me``). Required.
    archived: Filter by archive status. ``false`` = active only (optional).
    limit: Max results per page (1-100, default 20).

Returns:
    JSON with projects array.

tools.name: list_asana_teams
tools.description:
List teams in a workspace (Organization workspaces only).

When to call:
    - "Show me all teams"
    - "Which teams are in this workspace?"

Args:
    workspace_gid: Workspace GID (from ``get_asana_me``). Required.

Returns:
    JSON array of team objects (gid, name).

tools.name: start_figma_auth
tools.description:
Start Figma OAuth 2.0 authorization flow with PKCE.

    When to call:
        - When a user clicks "Connect Figma" in Accio Settings -> Connectors.
        - When a skill needs Figma access but no valid credential exists for the current workspace.
        - When the existing Figma token has expired and re-authorization is required.

    Returns:
        A human-readable Markdown message containing the Figma authorization URL.
        The user must open this URL in a browser to complete the OAuth consent.
        After successful authorization, the callback route automatically persists
        the access token and the connection becomes active.

    Raises:
        No exceptions are raised to the caller; errors are returned as formatted strings.

    Example:
        ```
        result = await start_figma_auth()
        # Returns: "**Complete Figma authorization**

Share this link with the user..."
        ```

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description:
Get the authenticated Figma user's profile and approximate plan level.

When to call:
    - Immediately after connecting Figma to verify the OAuth token works.
    - When you need to know the user's Figma handle, email, or avatar URL.
    - Before calling plan-restricted features to check if the user has access.

Returns:
    On success: Human-readable profile summary including handle, email, avatar URL,
                and approximate plan level inferred from granted scopes.
    On failure: Single-line reason + reconnection instruction.

tools.name: check_user_plan
tools.description:
Check the current Figma user's plan level and available feature scopes.

When to call:
    - Before attempting Enterprise-only features (variables, library analytics).
    - Before Dev Mode features (Code Connect) to verify Organization plan.
    - When troubleshooting "403 Forbidden" errors from Figma API.

Returns:
    On success: Structured summary of inferred plan and granted scopes.
    On failure: Single-line reason + reconnection instruction.

tools.name: validate_scope_access
tools.description:
Validate whether the current Figma credential has a specific OAuth scope.

When to call:
    - Before attempting an operation that requires a specific scope.
    - When troubleshooting "403 Forbidden" errors.
    - As a preflight check in multi-step workflows.

Args:
    required_scope: The scope to check for (required).
        Example: "file_comments:write", "webhooks:write", "team_library_content:read"

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation that the scope is granted, or warning if missing.
    On failure: Single-line reason + reconnection instruction.

tools.name: read_file_content
tools.description:
Read the content and node tree of a Figma file (use this for nodes, layers, or any detail beyond basic metadata).

**Do NOT confuse with read_file_metadata** — this tool returns the full node tree and supports
node_ids, depth, and version_id. read_file_metadata only returns file name, pages, and timestamps.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "Show me the structure of Figma file X".
    - When you need to extract layer names, text content, colors, or component instances.
    - When you need specific nodes by ID (use node_ids parameter).
    - After getting a file key from a Figma URL (e.g., https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123/...).

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key, found in the URL after /file/ (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456" from https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123def456/MyFile
    version_id: Optional specific version to retrieve. If omitted, returns the latest.
        Example: "v1234"
    depth: Optional max depth of the node tree (1-3 recommended for large files).
        Example: 1 returns only top-level pages, 2 includes page children.
    node_ids: Optional list of specific node IDs to fetch instead of the full file.
        Example: ["1:2", "3:45"]. Use this when you only need specific frames or layers.

Returns:
    On success: File name, version, last modified, top-level node count, and JSON content.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: read_file_metadata
tools.description:
Read metadata of a Figma file without fetching the full node tree.

**Do NOT confuse with read_file_content** — this tool only returns lightweight metadata
(file name, pages list, timestamps). It does NOT support ids, depth, node_ids, or geometry.
If you need node details, layers, or any content beyond basic metadata, use read_file_content instead.

When to call:
    - When you only need the file name, pages list, last modified time, or thumbnail.
    - As a quick check before reading the full file content.
    - When the user asks "What is the name of this Figma file?" or "When was it last updated?".

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key, found in the URL after /file/ (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"

Returns:
    On success: File name, pages list, author info, creation time, last modified time, and thumbnail URL.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: read_file_versions
tools.description:
Read the version history of a Figma file.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "What are the previous versions of this file?" or "Show version history".
    - Before restoring or comparing an older design version.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"

Returns:
    On success: Version count, labels, creators, and timestamps.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: read_file_comments
tools.description:
Read all comments on a Figma file, including replies, positions, and authors.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "What feedback does this design have?" or "Show me the comments".
    - When compiling review notes or action items from stakeholders.
    - Before creating a new comment to avoid duplicates.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"

Returns:
    On success: Comment count, author list, and truncated JSON of all comments.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: create_comment
tools.description:
Create a new comment on a Figma file or a specific node.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "Leave a comment on this design saying ...".
    - When an AI review skill needs to publish feedback directly into Figma.
    - When adding annotations or action items to a specific layer or frame.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"
    message: The comment text (required).
        Example: "Great work on the color palette! Consider increasing contrast."
    node_id: Optional node ID to attach the comment to. If provided, the comment is
        pinned to that specific layer/frame.
        Example: "1:2"
    client_meta: Optional dict with canvas coordinates. If both node_id and client_meta
        are omitted, defaults to {"x": 50, "y": 50}.
        Example: {"x": 100, "y": 200}

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation with the new comment ID and created_at timestamp.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description:
Delete a comment from a Figma file.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "Delete comment X from this file".
    - When cleaning up resolved or outdated feedback.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"
    comment_id: The ID of the comment to delete (required).
        You can get this from read_file_comments.

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation that the comment was deleted.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: read_library_assets
tools.description:
Read components and styles published from a personal Figma file.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "What components are in this file?".
    - When inspecting reusable assets before using them in another file.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"

Returns:
    On success: Component and style lists with keys and descriptions.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: read_dev_resources
tools.description:
Read development resources (design tokens, annotations, spacing systems) from a Figma file.

When to call:
    - When the user asks "Show me the design tokens for this file".
    - When extracting spacing, color, or typography tokens for handoff to developers.
    - Before creating or updating dev resources.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"
    node_id: Optional node ID to filter resources to a specific layer.
        Example: "1:2"

Returns:
    On success: Dev resource count, names, URLs, and associated nodes.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: create_dev_resource
tools.description:
Create a new development resource (design token, annotation, or link) on a Figma node.

When to call:
    - When adding a design token reference to a layer.
    - When linking a Figma component to a code repository or documentation page.
    - When documenting spacing or color values for developer handoff.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"
    node_id: The node ID to attach the resource to (required).
        Example: "1:2"
    name: Human-readable name of the resource (required).
        Example: "Primary Button Token"
    url: URL or value of the resource (required).
        Example: "https://tokens.example.com/primary-button" or "#007AFF"

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation with the new resource ID.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: update_dev_resource
tools.description:
Update an existing development resource on a Figma file.

When to call:
    - When correcting a design token value or URL.
    - When renaming a resource for better clarity.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
    resource_id: The ID of the dev resource to update (required).
        Get this from read_dev_resources.
    name: New name for the resource (required).
    url: New URL or value for the resource (required).

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation that the resource was updated.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: list_figma_team_projects
tools.description:
List projects within a Figma team.

When to call:
    - A user asks "What projects do we have in Figma team X?".
    - Before listing files to understand the project structure.

Args:
    team_id: The Figma team ID. Found in the URL:
        https://www.figma.com/files/team/{team_id}/... (required).

Returns:
    On success: Project names and IDs.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: list_figma_project_files
tools.description:
List files within a Figma project.

When to call:
    - A user asks "What files are in Figma project X?".
    - After list_figma_team_projects to drill into a specific project.

Args:
    project_id: The Figma project ID (required).
    branch_data: Whether to include branch information for each file. Default False.

Returns:
    On success: File names, keys, and last-modified times.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: delete_dev_resource
tools.description:
Delete a development resource from a Figma file.

When to call:
    - When removing an outdated design token or annotation.
    - When cleaning up dev resources that are no longer relevant.

Args:
    file_key: The Figma file key (required).
        Example: "ABC123def456"
    resource_id: The ID of the dev resource to delete (required).
        Get this from read_dev_resources.

Returns:
    On success: Confirmation that the resource was deleted.
    On failure: Single-line reason + action suggestion.

tools.name: list_figma_connections
tools.description:
List all Figma accounts currently connected to this workspace.

When to call:
    - When checking which Figma accounts are authorized.
    - Before running Figma tools to verify a connection exists.
    - When troubleshooting "not connected" errors.

Returns:
    On success: A list of connected accounts with user names and emails.
    On failure: Message indicating no connections found.

tools.name: start_pipedrive_auth
tools.description:
Start Pipedrive OAuth 2.0 authorization flow.

When to call:
    - When a user clicks "Connect Pipedrive" in Accio Settings -> Connectors.
    - When a skill needs Pipedrive CRM access but no valid credential exists
      for the current workspace.
    - When the existing Pipedrive token has expired and automatic refresh failed,
      requiring re-authorization.

Parameters:
    None. The accio_id and locale are resolved from the request context.

Returns:
    A human-readable Markdown message containing the Pipedrive authorization URL
    (authUrl). The user must open this URL in a browser to complete the OAuth
    consent on Pipedrive. After successful authorization, the callback route
    automatically persists the access token and refresh token, and the connection
    becomes active.

    Structure:
        - On success: Markdown with clickable authorization link
        - On failure: Markdown error message describing the configuration issue

Raises:
    No exceptions are raised to the caller; errors are returned as formatted strings.

tools.name: list_pipedrive_deals
tools.description:
List deals from Pipedrive CRM with optional filters.

Use this tool when the user wants to see their sales pipeline, open deals,
won/lost deals, or deals in a specific stage or pipeline.

Args:
    status: Filter by deal status. One of: "open", "won", "lost". Default: all open.
    stage_id: Filter by specific pipeline stage ID.
    pipeline_id: Filter by pipeline ID.
    owner_id: Filter by deal owner (Pipedrive user ID).
    sort_by: Sort field: "id", "add_time", "update_time", "title", "value". Default: "id".
    sort_direction: "asc" or "desc". Default: "asc".
    limit: Max number of deals to return (1-500). Default: 50.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup (internal).

Returns:
    JSON list of deals with id, title, value, currency, status, stage_id,
    pipeline_id, person_id, org_id, owner_id, expected_close_date, etc.

tools.name: get_pipedrive_deal
tools.description:
Get details of a specific Pipedrive deal by ID.

Use this tool when the user asks about a specific deal, wants to check deal details,
value, stage, associated contacts, or activities.

Args:
    deal_id: The numeric ID of the deal in Pipedrive (required).
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    Full deal object including title, value, currency, status, stage_id, pipeline_id,
    person_id, org_id, owner_id, expected_close_date, custom_fields, timestamps.

tools.name: create_pipedrive_deal
tools.description:
Create a new deal in Pipedrive.

Use this tool when the user wants to add a new sales opportunity to their pipeline.

Args:
    title: Deal title (required). E.g., "Enterprise Plan - Acme Corp".
    value: Monetary value of the deal.
    currency: 3-letter currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR"). Uses account default if omitted.
    pipeline_id: Pipeline to place the deal in. Uses default pipeline if omitted.
    stage_id: Stage within the pipeline. Uses first stage if omitted.
    person_id: Link to an existing person (contact) by ID.
    org_id: Link to an existing organization by ID.
    owner_id: Assign deal to a specific Pipedrive user by ID.
    expected_close_date: Expected close date in "YYYY-MM-DD" format.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    The created deal object with its new ID and all fields.

tools.name: update_pipedrive_deal
tools.description:
Update an existing Pipedrive deal (v2 uses PATCH).

Use this tool when the user wants to modify deal properties like value, stage,
status (mark as won/lost), or move it to a different pipeline.

Args:
    deal_id: The numeric ID of the deal to update (required).
    title: New deal title.
    value: New monetary value.
    currency: New currency code (e.g., "USD").
    status: New status: "open", "won", or "lost".
    stage_id: Move deal to this stage.
    pipeline_id: Move deal to this pipeline.
    owner_id: Reassign deal to another Pipedrive user.
    person_id: Link to a different person.
    org_id: Link to a different organization.
    expected_close_date: New expected close date ("YYYY-MM-DD").
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    The updated deal object.

tools.name: delete_pipedrive_deal
tools.description:
Delete a deal from Pipedrive.

Use this tool when the user wants to permanently remove a deal.
In v2 API, deleted deals are soft-deleted and fully removed after 30 days.

Args:
    deal_id: The numeric ID of the deal to delete (required).
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    Confirmation of deletion.

tools.name: search_pipedrive_deals
tools.description:
Search deals in Pipedrive by keyword.

Use this tool when the user wants to find specific deals by name/title keyword.

Args:
    term: Search keyword (searches deal titles and custom fields). Required.
    status: Optional filter: "open", "won", "lost".
    limit: Max results to return (1-100). Default: 20.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    List of matching deals with id, title, value, status, etc.

tools.name: list_pipedrive_persons
tools.description:
List persons (contacts) from Pipedrive CRM.

Use this tool when the user wants to see their contacts, leads, or people.

Args:
    owner_id: Filter by owner (Pipedrive user ID).
    org_id: Filter persons by organization ID.
    sort_by: Sort field: "id", "add_time", "update_time", "name". Default: "id".
    sort_direction: "asc" or "desc". Default: "asc".
    limit: Max persons to return (1-500). Default: 50.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    JSON list of persons with id, name, emails, phones, org_id, owner_id, etc.

tools.name: get_pipedrive_person
tools.description:
Get details of a specific person (contact) by ID.

Use this tool when the user asks about a specific contact's details.

Args:
    person_id: The numeric ID of the person (required).
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    Full person object including name, emails, phones, org_id, owner_id, custom_fields.

tools.name: create_pipedrive_person
tools.description:
Create a new person (contact) in Pipedrive.

Use this tool when the user wants to add a new contact to their CRM.

Args:
    name: Full name of the person (required). E.g., "John Smith".
    email: Primary email address.
    phone: Primary phone number.
    org_id: Link to an existing organization by ID.
    owner_id: Assign to a specific Pipedrive user.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

Returns:
    The created person object with its new ID.

tools.name: update_pipedrive_person
tools.description:
Update an existing person (contact) in Pipedrive (v2 uses PATCH).

Use this tool when the user wants to modify a contact's name, email, phone,
organization link, or owner.

Args:
    person_id: The numeric ID of the person to update (required).
    name: New name.
    email: New primary email.
    phone: New primary phone.
    org_id: Link to a different organization.
    owner_id: Reassign to another user.
    user_id: Pipedrive user_id for credential lookup.

tools.name: start_atlassian_rovo_auth
tools.description:
Start the Atlassian Rovo OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authorization flow.

触发场景 (when to call):
    - 用户在 Accio Settings → Connectors 中点击 "Connect Atlassian"。
    - Agent 需要访问 Jira / Confluence / Rovo，但当前 workspace 还没有有效凭证。
    - 之前的 Atlassian access token 过期且 refresh 失败，需要重新走授权。

参数 (args):
    无；scope / redirect_uri 等由服务端配置决定。
    accio_id / locale 从请求 context 自动注入到 OAuth state，callback 时还原。

返回结构 (returns):
    Markdown 文本，包含给最终用户点击的授权链接；不会返回 access token。
    授权成功后，由 GET /atlassian-rovo/callback 在服务端完成 token 交换并落库，
    当前工作区 (accio_id) 下即可通过 /auth/authorizations 查询到对应授权账号。

错误处理:
    - 当 ATLASSIAN_ROVO_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / SECRET 缺失时，返回中文/英文双语提示；
    - state、code 等校验失败均不会污染凭证存储（落库只在 callback 成功后执行）。

tools.name: check_atlassian_rovo_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of Atlassian Rovo credentials for the current workspace.

触发场景 (when to call):
    - 用户问"Atlassian 连接还好吗 / 是否需要重新授权"。
    - 调用 Jira / Confluence 系列 tool 之前希望先确认凭证可用。
    - 用户怀疑 token 被撤销，需要主动验真。

校验机制:
    检查 access_token 过期时间 + refresh_token 是否存在。Atlassian 使用
    rotating refresh token，过期 token 可通过 refresh 续期；无 refresh_token
    的凭证视为失效并被清理。

参数 (args):
    account_id: 可选。Atlassian account UUID（/me 接口的 ``account_id`` 字段）。
        - 留空 (默认)：枚举当前 ``accio_id`` 下所有 Atlassian 凭证逐个校验。
        - 指定值：仅校验该单个凭证。

返回 (returns):
    Markdown 文本，展示每个凭证的 account / site / scope / 过期时间 /
    状态。失效凭证在响应中明确标记为 ``❌ Invalid``，且已被服务端清理。

tools.name: delete_atlassian_rovo_credentials
tools.description:
Disconnect Atlassian Rovo credentials for the current workspace.

触发场景 (when to call):
    - 用户在 Accio 中要求"断开 Atlassian 连接"或"清除 Atlassian 授权"。
    - 上一次授权的账号需要切换，重新走 ``start_atlassian_rovo_auth`` 之前先做清理。
    - 凭证状态异常 (例如 401)，希望强制删掉缓存以重新授权。

参数 (args):
    account_id: 可选。Atlassian account UUID（GET /me 返回的 ``account_id``）。
        - 留空 (默认)：删除当前 ``accio_id`` 下所有 Atlassian 凭证。
        - 指定具体值：仅删除该单个 Atlassian 账号的凭证；其余账号保留。

返回结构 (returns):
    Markdown 文本，说明删除结果与被清理的账号数量。语义幂等：原本不存在
    凭证时仍返回 success，不视为错误。
