tools.name: zendesk_pd_list_triggers
tools.description:
List Zendesk triggers (event-based rules that fire on ticket changes).

**When to call:** When the user wants to see trigger rules.

**Parameters:**
- active_only: Only active triggers (default True).
- page_size: Results per page (1–100, default 25).
- page_cursor: Cursor for next page.

**Returns:** JSON with `triggers` array.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_get_trigger
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Zendesk trigger.

**When to call:** When the user wants to inspect trigger conditions/actions.

**Parameters:**
- trigger_id: (required) The trigger ID.

**Returns:** JSON with `trigger` object including conditions and actions.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_create_trigger
tools.description:
Create a new Zendesk trigger (event-based rule).

**When to call:** When the user wants to create an automation rule.

**Parameters:**
- title: (required) Trigger title.
- conditions_all: JSON array of ALL conditions.
  '[{"field":"status","operator":"is","value":"open"}]'
- conditions_any: JSON array of ANY conditions.
- actions: (required) JSON array of actions.
  '[{"field":"priority","value":"high"}]'

**Returns:** JSON with the created `trigger` object.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_update_trigger
tools.description:
Update an existing Zendesk trigger.

**When to call:** When the user wants to modify a trigger.

**Parameters:**
- trigger_id: (required) The trigger ID.
- title: New title (optional).
- conditions_all: JSON array of ALL conditions (optional, replaces).
- conditions_any: JSON array of ANY conditions (optional, replaces).
- actions: JSON array of actions (optional, replaces).
- active: "true" or "false" to enable/disable (optional).

**Returns:** JSON with the updated `trigger` object.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_delete_trigger
tools.description:
Delete a Zendesk trigger.

**When to call:** When the user explicitly asks to delete a trigger.

**Parameters:**
- trigger_id: (required) The trigger ID.

**Returns:** JSON confirmation.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_list_automations
tools.description:
List Zendesk automations (time-based rules that run periodically).

**When to call:** When the user wants to see automation rules.

**Parameters:**
- active_only: Only active automations (default True).
- page_size: Results per page (1–100, default 25).
- page_cursor: Cursor for next page.

**Returns:** JSON with `automations` array.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_get_automation
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Zendesk automation.

**When to call:** When the user wants to inspect an automation's
conditions and actions.

**Parameters:**
- automation_id: (required) The automation ID.

**Returns:** JSON with `automation` object.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_list_macros
tools.description:
List Zendesk macros (predefined ticket action sets / reply templates).

**When to call:** When the user wants to see available macros.

**Parameters:**
- active_only: Only active macros (default True).
- page_size: Results per page (1–100, default 25).
- page_cursor: Cursor for next page.

**Returns:** JSON with `macros` array.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_get_macro
tools.description:
Get details of a single Zendesk macro.

**When to call:** When the user wants to inspect a macro's actions.

**Parameters:**
- macro_id: (required) The macro ID.

**Returns:** JSON with `macro` object including title, actions, description.

tools.name: zendesk_pd_apply_macro
tools.description:
Apply a macro to a Zendesk ticket.

Fetches the macro preview first, then applies changes to the ticket.

**When to call:** When the user wants to apply a predefined action set.

**Parameters:**
- ticket_id: (required) Target ticket ID.
- macro_id: (required) Macro ID to apply.

**Returns:** JSON with the updated `ticket` object after macro application.

tools.name: start_typeform_auth
tools.description:
Start Typeform OAuth2 authorization flow.

Returns the authorization URL for the user to visit in their browser.
After authorization, the callback will store the token automatically.

tools.name: check_typeform_credentials
tools.description:
Check if Typeform OAuth credentials are valid and connected.

Re-verifies the stored token against the Typeform API (GET /me).
If the token is expired but a refresh_token exists, auto-refreshes.
Does NOT expose the actual token value.

Returns:
    Credential status information (connected/expired/not found).

tools.name: get_typeform_account_info
tools.description:
Get current Typeform account information including user ID, email, and alias.

Returns:
    JSON string with account details.

tools.name: list_typeform_forms
tools.description:
List forms in the user's Typeform account.

Args:
    search: Filter forms by title keyword.
    page: Page number (starts at 1).
    page_size: Number of forms per page (max 200).
    workspace_id: Filter by workspace ID.

Returns:
    JSON with total_items, page_count, and items array.

tools.name: get_typeform_form
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Typeform form including all fields, logic, and settings.

Args:
    form_id: The unique form ID (found in form URL).

Returns:
    JSON with complete form definition.

tools.name: create_typeform_form
tools.description:
Create a new Typeform form.

Args:
    title: Form title.
    fields: JSON string of fields array. Each field needs at minimum 'type' and 'title'.
        Supported types: short_text, long_text, multiple_choice, dropdown, yes_no,
        email, number, date, rating, opinion_scale, nps, website, phone_number,
        file_upload, statement, ranking, picture_choice, legal, payment.
    workspace_id: Optional workspace ID to place the form in.

Returns:
    JSON with created form details including the generated form_id.

tools.name: update_typeform_form
tools.description:
Update an existing Typeform form (partial patch).

Args:
    form_id: The form ID to update.
    updates: JSON string with fields to update (e.g., title, fields, settings).

Returns:
    JSON with updated form.

tools.name: delete_typeform_form
tools.description:
Delete a Typeform form permanently.

Args:
    form_id: The form ID to delete.

Returns:
    Confirmation message.

tools.name: get_typeform_responses
tools.description:
Get responses/submissions for a specific Typeform form.

Args:
    form_id: The form ID to get responses for.
    page_size: Number of responses to return (max 1000, default 25).
    since: ISO 8601 date to filter responses from (inclusive).
    until: ISO 8601 date to filter responses until (inclusive).
    completed: If True, only completed responses; if False, only started.
    query: Full-text search across answer values.

Returns:
    JSON with total_items and items array containing response data.

Note:
    Very recent responses (within ~30 min) may not appear yet due to Typeform platform indexing delay.

tools.name: list_typeform_workspaces
tools.description:
List all workspaces in the Typeform account.

Returns:
    JSON with workspace list.

tools.name: set_apollo_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Apollo.io API credentials for the current user.

The credentials are stored securely and used for all Apollo.io tools
(people search, enrichment, organization lookup).
To get your API Key, visit https://developer.apollo.io/#/keys and click "Create New Key".

Args:
    api_key: Apollo.io API Key

Returns:
    Success or error message

tools.name: check_apollo_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of Apollo.io API credentials for the current user.

Returns:
    Credential status information

tools.name: delete_apollo_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Apollo.io API credentials.

After deletion, the user will need to set new credentials to use Apollo tools.

Returns:
    Success or error message

tools.name: enrich_apollo_organization
tools.description:
Enrich a company/organization profile on Apollo.io by its domain.

Use this tool when the user wants detailed information about a specific company,
including employee count, funding, tech stack, industry, and key contacts.

Args:
    domain: Company domain (e.g., "google.com", "stripe.com")

Returns:
    JSON with the enriched organization profile. The top-level `result.id` is
    the Apollo public-database organization id — pass it to
    `get_apollo_organization_job_postings(organization_id=...)` to chain.
    Includes industry, size, funding, tech stack, etc.

tools.name: create_apollo_contact
tools.description:
Create a new contact in your Apollo.io CRM (saves a prospect WITHOUT contacting them).

Use this tool when the user wants to SAVE a person to their Apollo CRM after finding
or enriching them — e.g., "save this prospect", "add John to my contacts/list".
This is an internal CRM write only: it does NOT send any email or start any outreach
sequence. To actually reach out, a separate explicit action would be required.

Provide at least one of: email, or (first_name + last_name).

Args:
    first_name: Contact's first name
    last_name: Contact's last name
    email: Contact's email address
    title: Job title (e.g., "VP of Sales")
    organization_name: Company name the contact works at
    website_url: Company website/domain (e.g., "https://stripe.com")
    present_raw_address: Contact's location (e.g., "San Francisco, CA")
    direct_phone: Direct phone number
    mobile_phone: Mobile phone number
    label_names: Lists/labels to add this contact to (e.g., ["High Intent", "Q2 Outbound"]).
        Apollo only attaches labels that ALREADY exist in your workspace; unknown
        labels are silently dropped. When any requested label is dropped, the
        response will include a `warning` field listing the missing labels.

Returns:
    JSON with the created contact's id and saved fields. If any requested
    `label_names` were not applied, includes a `warning` field.

tools.name: get_apollo_organization_job_postings
tools.description:
Get current job postings for an organization on Apollo.io.

A common B2B sales signal: companies actively hiring often indicate growth,
new initiatives, or budget availability — making them better prospects.

Typical chain: call `enrich_apollo_organization(domain=...)` first to get
the Apollo `organization.id`, then pass that id here.

Args:
    organization_id: Apollo **public-database** organization id (e.g.,
        "5d0a0fbff6512580bf33a120"). Get it from `enrich_apollo_organization(domain=...)`'s
        top-level `result.id`. **NOT** a CRM `account_id` — those are a different
        namespace. If you have a CRM account object, use its `organization_id`
        field (which we surface), not its `id`.
    page: Page number (default: 1)
    per_page: Results per page, max 100 (default: 10)

Returns:
    JSON with job postings (title, location, posted date, url) and total count

tools.name: search_apollo_contacts
tools.description:
Search contacts already saved in YOUR Apollo CRM (not Apollo's prospect database).

Use this when the user asks about contacts they already have in Apollo, not
when they want to find brand-new prospects.

Args:
    q_keywords: Free-text search across name/email/title (e.g., "John CTO")
    contact_stage_ids: Filter by contact stage ids
    label_ids: Filter by label/list ids
    page: Page number (default: 1)
    per_page: Results per page, max 100 (default: 25)

Returns:
    JSON with contacts (id, name, title, email, organization_name) and pagination

tools.name: search_apollo_accounts
tools.description:
Search companies/accounts already saved in YOUR Apollo CRM.

Use this for "what companies are already in my CRM"; use enrich/search prospect
tools instead when the user wants to discover new companies.

Args:
    q_organization_name: Filter by organization name (e.g., "Stripe")
    account_stage_ids: Filter by account stage ids
    page: Page number (default: 1)
    per_page: Results per page, max 100 (default: 25)

Returns:
    JSON with accounts (id, name, domain, industry, employee count) and pagination

tools.name: create_apollo_account
tools.description:
Create a new account (company) in your Apollo.io CRM.

Use this to save a company into the user's CRM. Like create_apollo_contact,
this is an internal-only CRM write — no email or outreach is sent.

Args:
    name: Company name (required, e.g., "Stripe")
    domain: Company website domain (e.g., "stripe.com")
    phone: Main company phone number
    raw_address: HQ address (e.g., "San Francisco, CA")
    account_stage_id: Apollo account stage id

Returns:
    JSON with the created account's id and saved fields

tools.name: list_apollo_sequences
tools.description:
List email sequences (a.k.a. emailer campaigns) defined in your Apollo workspace.

READ-ONLY: returns sequence metadata only (id, name, status). Does not enroll
any contacts and does not send any emails.

Args:
    q_name: Filter by sequence name substring (optional)
    page: Page number (default: 1)
    per_page: Results per page, max 100 (default: 25)

Returns:
    JSON with sequences (id, name, active, num_steps, archived) and pagination

tools.name: set_fireflies_credentials
tools.description:
Set or update Fireflies.ai API credentials for the current user.

The credential is verified against Fireflies' user query before being
stored. To get your API key, sign in at https://app.fireflies.ai and visit
https://app.fireflies.ai/integrations/custom/fireflies — both Free and
paid plans support API access.

Args:
    api_key: Fireflies.ai API Key (a UUID-shaped token from the Integrations page)

Returns:
    Success or error message. The success message contains the substring
    "connected" so the desktop client can detect a successful connection.

tools.name: check_fireflies_credentials
tools.description:
Check the status of Fireflies.ai API credentials for the current user.

Re-verifies the stored API key against Fireflies — a key revoked on the
Fireflies side will be reported as Invalid here even if it is still
present in the local store.

Returns:
    A human-readable credential status block (no secrets).

tools.name: delete_fireflies_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current user's Fireflies.ai API credentials.

After deletion, you'll need to call `set_fireflies_credentials` again with
a valid API key before any Fireflies tool will succeed.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

tools.name: list_fireflies_transcripts
tools.description:
List or search meeting transcripts from Fireflies.ai.

Use this to find meetings — by keyword, date range, organizer / participant
email(s), Fireflies user id, or channel. Returns lightweight metadata
(no sentences, no summary) so the result fits comfortably in context.
Call ``get_fireflies_transcript(id=...)`` afterwards to drill into one
meeting.

Args:
    keyword: Free-text search; ``scope`` controls whether it matches title
        only (default), sentences (spoken content), or both.
    scope: One of "title", "sentences", "all". When ``scope`` is provided,
        ``keyword`` becomes required by Fireflies.
    from_date: ISO 8601 lower bound, e.g. ``"2024-07-08T00:00:00.000Z"``.
    to_date: ISO 8601 upper bound (same format).
    host_email: Filter by host email.
    organizers: List of organizer emails (preferred for organizer filtering).
    participants: List of participant emails (preferred for participant
        filtering).
    organizer_email: Single-organizer filter, kept for backward
        compatibility. Cannot be combined with ``organizers`` /
        ``participants``.
    participant_email: Single-participant filter, kept for backward
        compatibility. Cannot be combined with ``organizers`` /
        ``participants``.
    user_id: Filter meetings where this Fireflies user id was the organizer
        or a participant.
    channel_id: Filter meetings that belong to a Fireflies channel.
    mine: When True, only return transcripts owned by the API key's user.
    limit: Max results to return (Fireflies caps this at 50; default 25).
    skip: Pagination offset (default 0).

Returns:
    JSON with the matching transcripts. Each entry includes id, title,
    date, duration, attendees, speakers, transcript_url, and a
    ``meeting_info`` block (``fred_joined`` / ``silent_meeting`` /
    ``summary_status``) that signals whether the bot actually joined and
    whether the AI summary has finished processing.

tools.name: get_fireflies_transcript
tools.description:
Fetch the full content of a single Fireflies meeting transcript.

Returns metadata + summary (overview, action items, keywords, topics) +
speakers + the full sentence-by-sentence transcript. Long meetings
produce large responses; call ``list_fireflies_transcripts`` first when
the user only needs to identify a meeting.

Args:
    id: Transcript id (from ``list_fireflies_transcripts``).

Returns:
    JSON with the full transcript payload.

tools.name: get_fireflies_user_info
tools.description:
Fetch the connected Fireflies account's profile and usage signals.

Useful before quota-sensitive operations: ``minutes_consumed`` and
``num_transcripts`` give a coarse read on how close the account is to
its plan limits, and ``is_admin`` / ``integrations`` reveal what the
key can do (e.g. team-scoped queries or which calendar/CRM is linked).

Returns:
    JSON with the current user's id, email, name, transcript count,
    consumed minutes, recent meeting / transcript ids, admin flag, and
    the list of connected integrations. Fields the account does not
    expose (e.g. some signals on Free plans) are omitted.

tools.name: add_fireflies_to_live_meeting
tools.description:
Invite the Fireflies.ai notetaker (Fred) to an in-progress meeting.

SIDE EFFECT: this actually joins a real meeting — confirm the user wants
to proceed before chaining it to other tools. Rate limit: 3 requests per
20 minutes (a tight, separate bucket from the daily quota).

Args:
    meeting_link: HTTPS URL for the live meeting (Zoom / Google Meet / Teams /
        Webex). Must be the exact join link.
    title: Optional title for the resulting transcript (max 256 chars).
    duration: How long Fred should stay (minutes). Min 15, max 120,
        default 60 if omitted.
    language: Language code (e.g. "en", "es", "de"). Max 5 characters.
        Defaults to English. See Fireflies' Language Codes page for the
        full list.
    meeting_password: Password if the meeting requires one (max 32 chars).
    attendees: Optional list of expected meeting participants. Each item is
        a dict with optional ``displayName`` / ``email`` / ``phoneNumber``
        fields, e.g. ``[{"email": "alice@x.com", "displayName": "Alice"}]``.
        Helps Fred match transcript speakers to known people.

Returns:
    JSON with ``success: true`` if Fred was dispatched.

tools.name: list_fireflies_channels
tools.description:
List the Fireflies meeting channels (folders) visible to the connected
account.

Use this before calling ``list_fireflies_transcripts(channel_id=...)`` —
that filter needs a Fireflies channel id which is not visible elsewhere.

Returns:
    JSON with each channel's ``id``, ``title``, ``is_private``,
    ``created_at`` / ``updated_at``, and ``created_by``.

tools.name: list_fireflies_users
tools.description:
List the Fireflies users visible to the connected account.

Use this before calling ``list_fireflies_transcripts`` with ``user_id`` /
``organizers`` / ``participants`` filters — those filters need Fireflies
user ids or emails which this tool surfaces.

Note: on personal plans this typically returns only the connected user.
Full team listings require admin-level credentials on a paid plan.

Returns:
    JSON with each user's ``user_id``, ``email``, ``name``,
    ``num_transcripts``, ``is_admin``, ``is_calendar_in_sync`` and
    connected ``integrations``.

tools.name: get_fireflies_active_meetings
tools.description:
List meetings that are currently in progress for the connected account.

Useful before calling ``add_fireflies_to_live_meeting`` to avoid inviting
Fred to a meeting he is already in, or to check which meetings Fred is
actively recording right now.

Args:
    email: Optional — restrict to meetings for a specific user (by email).
        Defaults to the connected account.
    states: Optional — filter by meeting state. Valid values:
        ``["active", "paused"]``. Defaults to both.

Returns:
    JSON with each in-progress meeting's ``id``, ``title``,
    ``organizer_email``, ``meeting_link``, ``start_time`` / ``end_time``,
    ``privacy``, and ``state``.

tools.name: list_fireflies_soundbites
tools.description:
List Fireflies soundbites (short highlight clips cut from meetings).

Fireflies requires exactly one scope — at least one of ``mine`` /
``my_team`` / ``transcript_id`` must be set. When all three are omitted
this tool defaults to ``mine=True``.

Args:
    mine: When True, only soundbites created by the connected user.
    my_team: When True, only soundbites created by the user's team.
    transcript_id: When set, only soundbites cut from that specific
        meeting transcript.
    limit: Page size (1-50, default 25).
    skip: Pagination offset (>= 0, default 0).

Returns:
    JSON with each soundbite's ``id``, ``name``, ``transcript_id``,
    ``summary``, ``status`` / ``summary_status``, ``start_time`` /
    ``end_time``, ``media_type``, ``created_at``, ``thumbnail`` /
    ``preview`` URLs, ``user`` (creator), and ``created_from`` (source
    meeting). Call ``get_fireflies_soundbite(id=...)`` for full detail.

tools.name: get_fireflies_soundbite
tools.description:
Fetch a single Fireflies soundbite with full metadata.

Args:
    id: Soundbite id (from ``list_fireflies_soundbites``).

Returns:
    JSON with the soundbite's full metadata: ``id``, ``name``,
    ``transcript_id``, ``summary``, ``status`` / ``summary_status``,
    ``start_time`` / ``end_time``, ``media_type``, ``created_at``,
    ``thumbnail`` / ``preview`` URLs, ``privacies``, ``user`` (creator),
    and ``created_from`` (source meeting).

tools.name: start_facebook_auth
tools.description:
Authorize a user's Facebook account for the current workspace.

Each workspace (accio_id) can bind exactly one Facebook account. After authorization,
Facebook tools in this workspace will run as that Facebook account.

**WHEN TO CALL**

Only call this tool in these cases:
  1. First time the user wants to use Facebook tools and this workspace has no
     Facebook credential yet.
  2. A Facebook tool **explicitly** returned `unauthorized` / `token_invalid` /
     a `401 Unauthorized` error AND the user agreed to re-authorize.
  3. The user explicitly asked to switch to a different Facebook account
     (re-authorization).

**WHEN NOT TO CALL — IMPORTANT**

Do NOT call this tool when a Facebook tool returns `403 Forbidden` or
a permissions error (e.g. #200 OAuthException "requires ... permission").
A permission error ≠ token expired. Re-authorizing **will not fix it** —
the new token will have the same scope and the next call will fail again,
creating a frustrating loop for the user. Instead, tell the user the
action is restricted and stop.

**IDEMPOTENT**

If the workspace already has a healthy Facebook credential, this tool will detect
that and return an `already connected` message *without* generating a new
OAuth link, so accidentally calling it does not force the user to re-authorize.

Returns:
    Either a markdown message containing the authorization link to share
    with the user, or a markdown message saying the workspace is already
    connected (so you can proceed directly with other Facebook tools).

tools.name: get_facebook_user_profile
tools.description:
Get the authenticated user's Facebook profile information.

**WHEN TO CALL**
- User asks "who am I on Facebook", "show my Facebook profile", or similar
- Need to confirm which Facebook account is connected to this workspace
- Before performing other Facebook operations, to verify the connection is healthy

**PARAMETERS**
None. Uses the workspace's connected Facebook account.

**RETURNS**
- Success: JSON with id, name, email, picture URL
- Failure: structured error with reason_code and actionable hint

**ERROR CASES**
- `auth_required=true`: token expired → call `start_facebook_auth`
- `permission_denied`: scope insufficient (should NOT re-authorize)

tools.name: list_facebook_pages
tools.description:
List all Facebook Pages managed by the authenticated user.

**WHEN TO CALL**
- User asks "show my Facebook pages" or "which pages do I manage"
- Before performing page-specific operations (to get the page_id)
- User wants to post on a page but hasn't specified which one

**PARAMETERS**
None.

**RETURNS**
- Success: JSON array of pages with id, name, category, access_token, fan_count
- Failure: structured error

**IMPORTANT**
Each page has its own page_access_token. When you need to post on a page or
read page-specific data, use the page_id returned here.

tools.name: get_facebook_page_posts
tools.description:
Get recent posts from a Facebook Page.

**WHEN TO CALL**
- User asks "show recent posts on my page" or "what did I post on [page name]"
- Need to check published content for a specific page
- Reviewing page activity before creating new content

**PARAMETERS**
- page_id (str, required): The Page ID. Get from `list_facebook_pages`.
- limit (int, default=10): Number of posts to return (max 100)
- after (str, optional): Pagination cursor

**RETURNS**
- Success: JSON array of posts with id, message, created_time, type, permalink
- Failure: structured error

**EXAMPLE**
get_facebook_page_posts(page_id="123456789", limit=5)

tools.name: create_facebook_page_post
tools.description:
Create a new post on a Facebook Page.

**WHEN TO CALL**
- User asks to "post on my Facebook page" or "publish content to my page"
- User provides text/link to share on their page

**PARAMETERS**
- page_id (str, required): The Page ID to post on. Get from `list_facebook_pages`.
- message (str, optional): The text content of the post.
- link (str, optional): A URL to share. Facebook will auto-generate a link preview.
- published (bool, default=True): Whether to publish immediately.
  Set False to create as draft (scheduled post).

**RETURNS**
- Success: JSON with post id and confirmation
- Failure: structured error

**IMPORTANT**
At least one of `message` or `link` must be provided.
Requires `pages_manage_posts` permission.

**EXAMPLE**
create_facebook_page_post(page_id="123456", message="Hello from our page!")
create_facebook_page_post(page_id="123456", message="Check this out", link="https://example.com")

tools.name: delete_facebook_page_post
tools.description:
Delete a post from a Facebook Page.

**WHEN TO CALL**
- User asks to delete a specific post from their page
- User wants to remove published content

**PARAMETERS**
- post_id (str, required): The post ID to delete.
  Format is typically "page_id_post_id" (e.g., "123456789_987654321").

**RETURNS**
- Success: confirmation message
- Failure: structured error

**IMPORTANT**
This action is irreversible. The post_id must belong to a page managed by
the authenticated user.

tools.name: start_ebay_auth
tools.description:
Initiate the eBay OAuth 2.0 authorization flow and return the authorization URL.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when the user wants to connect
their eBay seller account, or when any eBay tool returns an authentication error
indicating the credential is missing or invalid.

The tool generates an authorization URL that the user must open in a browser to
grant access. After the user completes authorization, eBay redirects back to the
server callback, which automatically stores the credentials.

**No credentials are stored** by this tool -- storage happens in the callback.

Returns:
    A message containing the eBay authorization URL for the user to click.
    The URL is formatted as a clickable hyperlink.

Example:
    start_ebay_auth()

tools.name: set_ebay_credentials
tools.description:
Set eBay credentials using a refresh token, or disconnect by passing an empty string.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when:
1. The user provides an eBay refresh token directly (e.g. from another system).
2. The user wants to disconnect eBay (pass empty string).
3. The OAuth callback flow is unavailable and the user has a valid refresh token.

The tool verifies the refresh token against the eBay Identity API by exchanging
it for a new access token. If verification fails, no credential is stored and a
human-readable error is returned.

**Single-credential contract**: each workspace (accio_id) binds at most ONE eBay
account. Setting a new token replaces the previous one.

**Disconnect contract**: passing an empty string for ``refresh_token`` disconnects
the current eBay binding idempotently.

Args:
    refresh_token: eBay OAuth refresh token. Empty string means disconnect.

Returns:
    On success: a message containing "connected" with the verified account info.
    On disconnect: a message containing "disconnected".
    On failure: a human-readable error message.

Example:
    set_ebay_credentials(refresh_token="v^1.1#i^1#...")
    set_ebay_credentials(refresh_token="")

tools.name: delete_ebay_credentials
tools.description:
Delete the current workspace's eBay credentials and disconnect the account.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when the user wants to
disconnect their eBay account or revoke access.

Each workspace (accio_id) binds at most one eBay account, so this tool
takes no parameters. The operation is idempotent.

After deletion, the user will need to re-authorize via ``start_ebay_auth``
or ``set_ebay_credentials`` to reconnect.

Returns:
    Success or error message.

Example:
    delete_ebay_credentials()

tools.name: get_ebay_token
tools.description:
Retrieve the current user's eBay OAuth access token.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool when it needs to obtain
the current valid eBay access token for the authorized user, e.g. for
debugging, displaying connection status, or passing to external systems.

If the stored access token has expired (eBay access tokens are valid for
2 hours), this tool will automatically refresh it using the stored refresh
token and update the credential store.

Returns:
    A message containing the current valid access token, token type,
    environment, and expiration info.
    If no credential is found, returns an error prompting re-authorization.

Example:
    get_ebay_token()

tools.name: check_ebay_connection
tools.description:
Check whether the current workspace has a valid eBay connection.

**When to call**: The agent should call this tool to quickly determine if the
user's eBay account is connected and whether the stored credentials are still
valid, without exposing the actual access token.

The tool checks:
1. Whether credentials exist for the current workspace (accio_id).
2. Whether the stored access token is still valid (not expired).
3. If the access token is expired, whether the refresh token can renew it.

Returns:
    A status message indicating connected/disconnected and token validity.

Example:
    check_ebay_connection()

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Get the current RPA publishing Spec for a platform category.

categoryId.description: Platform category identifier. Always pass it as a string.

tools.name: get_rpa_assets
tools.description: Return a version-consistent protected Converter and Locator bundle.

pluginVersion.description: Installed Plugin version bound to the protected asset bundle.

sceneCode.description: Business scene, for example product_publish or merchant_data_analysis.

assetVersion.description: Optional current asset version assertion. Omit it to resolve the current platform/scene bundle; an outdated version returns not found.

tools.name: get_platform_login_dsls
tools.description: Return encrypted check/logout/login DSL entries for one platform.

tools.name: get_multi_platform_dsls
tools.description: Return encrypted RPA DSL items for one platform and business type.

tools.name: start_microsoft365_auth
tools.description:
Start Microsoft 365 OAuth 2.0 authorization.

When to call:
  Use this tool whenever the user asks to "connect Microsoft 365",
  "connect Outlook", "authorize Microsoft 365 mail", or any other
  Microsoft 365-related capability and there is no existing valid
  credential. Do NOT call it just to double-check existing connections —
  other tools will trigger the auth flow automatically when needed.

What it does:
  Builds the Microsoft Identity Platform v2.0 authorization URL for the
  current ``accio_id`` (multi-tenant isolation) and returns it inside a
  human-friendly instruction message. The URL is what the end user must
  open in their browser to grant the requested scopes
  (``offline_access``, ``User.Read``, ``Mail.ReadWrite``,
  ``Calendars.ReadWrite``, ``Files.ReadWrite.All``,
  ``Chat.ReadWrite``, ``Notes.ReadWrite.All``, etc.).

Args:
  user_email: Optional Microsoft account email. When provided it is sent
    as ``login_hint`` so Microsoft prefills the account picker. Leaving
    it empty lets the user pick any account they have access to.

Returns:
  A Markdown-formatted instruction message. The relevant fields are:
    - ``authUrl``: the authorization URL string
    - guidance text in the user's locale (zh/en)
  No credential is persisted at this stage; persistence happens in the
  ``GET /microsoft365/callback`` route after the browser completes the flow.

tools.name: set_microsoft365_credentials
tools.description:
Manually register a Microsoft Graph access token.

When to call:
  Use this tool only when the user has obtained a Microsoft Graph access
  token outside the in-app OAuth flow (e.g. from Azure Postman, a
  pre-existing service principal token exchange, or another integration)
  and wants the MCP server to use it directly. For first-time end-user
  authorization, prefer ``start_microsoft365_auth`` instead.

Validation:
  The token is verified by calling ``GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me``
  BEFORE persistence. If the call fails (network error, 401, missing
  ``mail`` / ``userPrincipalName``), nothing is written to the credential
  store and the function returns a human-readable error message.

Storage:
  On success the credential is stored under the current ``accio_id`` and
  keyed by the email returned from ``/me``. Multiple Microsoft 365 accounts
  under the same workspace are kept independent.

Args:
  access_token: A non-empty Microsoft Graph delegated access token.
  refresh_token: Optional refresh token. Without it, the credential cannot
    be auto-refreshed and tools may need to re-prompt the user when the
    access token expires.
  expires_in_seconds: Optional remaining lifetime of the access token, in
    seconds. When provided, future requests will refresh the token a few
    minutes before this deadline.
  scope: Optional space-separated list of granted scopes (e.g.
    ``"User.Read Mail.ReadWrite"``). Used to drive future refresh calls
    when set.

Returns:
  Markdown text. On success the message contains the literal word
  ``connected`` and shows the email of the connected account. On failure
  the message starts with ``Error:`` and includes the underlying reason.

tools.name: search_microsoft365_emails
tools.description:
Search messages in the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this tool whenever the user wants to LIST or FIND emails —
  e.g. "show my unread mail from Bob this week", "find the invoice from
  Stripe", "what's in my Sent Items?". Prefer this over
  ``get_microsoft365_email_detail`` when the message id is unknown.

Authentication:
  Requires a previously connected Microsoft 365 account with the
  ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope. If the credential is missing or revoked, the
  tool returns an actionable error string asking the user to call
  ``start_microsoft365_auth`` (no exception is raised to the Agent).

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email address of the
    authenticated user (e.g. ``"alice@contoso.com"``). When omitted /
    empty string, the tool auto-locates the credential as long as the
    current accio has **exactly one** connected Microsoft 365 account.
  query: OPTIONAL Microsoft Graph ``$search`` expression (KQL-style).
    Examples:
      - ``"from:bob@contoso.com"``
      - ``"subject:invoice received:>=2024-01-01"``
      - ``"hasAttachment:true"``
    Empty string → list recent messages in ``folder``.
  folder: OPTIONAL well-known folder name. Default ``"inbox"``. Other
    common values: ``"sentitems"``, ``"drafts"``, ``"deleteditems"``,
    ``"archive"``. Pass an empty string to search across all folders.
  top: OPTIONAL page size (1-999). Default ``20``.
  next_link: OPTIONAL pagination URL returned by a previous call as
    ``nextLink``. When provided, all other paging params are ignored.

Returns:
  On success — a Markdown text containing:
    * a one-line count summary
    * a numbered list of messages (subject / from / id)
    * a fenced ```json``` block with the messages array and optional nextLink

  On failure — a single-line failure reason followed by an action hint.

tools.name: get_microsoft365_email_detail
tools.description:
Fetch a single message by id, including full body and recipients.

When to call:
  Call this AFTER ``search_microsoft365_emails`` returns a message id and
  the user wants to read the full content / quote it / reply to it.

Authentication:
  Requires the ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id (the ``id`` field returned
    by ``search_microsoft365_emails``).
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Same semantic as in ``search_microsoft365_emails``.
  body_format: OPTIONAL. ``"text"`` (default) or ``"html"``.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text with key headers plus a fenced json block.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: send_microsoft365_email
tools.description:
Send a new email on behalf of the authenticated Microsoft 365 user.

When to call:
  Use this whenever the user asks to "send an email", "reply via Outlook",
  "email Bob the report", etc. This sends immediately — there is no
  draft tool yet.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.Send`` scope for the ``/me/sendMail`` endpoint of
  Microsoft Graph. ``Mail.ReadWrite`` covers read/write operations
  on mailbox content but does **not** cover sending.

Args:
  to: REQUIRED non-empty list of recipient email addresses.
  subject: REQUIRED. Subject line.
  body: REQUIRED. Mail body content.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox that will appear as sender.
  cc: OPTIONAL list of CC addresses.
  bcc: OPTIONAL list of BCC addresses.
  body_format: OPTIONAL ``"text"`` (default) or ``"html"``.
  save_to_sent_items: OPTIONAL bool, default ``True``.

Returns:
  On success — a one-line confirmation + fenced json block.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: reply_microsoft365_email
tools.description:
Reply to an existing email message.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "reply to this email", "respond to Bob's
  message", "reply all", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.Send`` scope.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id to reply to
    (from search_microsoft365_emails or get_microsoft365_email_detail).
  comment: REQUIRED. The reply body text.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.
  reply_all: OPTIONAL. If True, replies to all recipients. Default False.

Returns:
  Confirmation text on success; error message on failure.

tools.name: forward_microsoft365_email
tools.description:
Forward an existing email message to new recipients.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "forward this email to Alice", "send this
  message to the team", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.Send`` scope.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id to forward.
  to: REQUIRED. Non-empty list of recipient email addresses.
  comment: OPTIONAL. Additional text to include above the forwarded content.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.

Returns:
  Confirmation text on success; error message on failure.

tools.name: list_microsoft365_email_attachments
tools.description:
List attachments on an email message.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks "show attachments", "what files are attached
  to that email?", "does this message have attachments?", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id
    (from search_microsoft365_emails or get_microsoft365_email_detail).
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.

Returns:
  Markdown text with attachment metadata listing (id, name, size,
  contentType, isInline) + fenced json. Does NOT include attachment
  file content; to download content, a separate Graph API call to
  ``GET /me/messages/{id}/attachments/{attachmentId}`` is needed.

tools.name: create_microsoft365_draft
tools.description:
Create a draft email in the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "create a draft", "save an email as draft",
  "prepare an email but don't send it yet", etc. The draft is saved in the
  Drafts folder and can be retrieved/updated later.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  subject: OPTIONAL. Subject line of the draft.
  body: OPTIONAL. Body content of the draft.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.
  to: OPTIONAL list of recipient email addresses.
  cc: OPTIONAL list of CC addresses.
  bcc: OPTIONAL list of BCC addresses.
  body_format: OPTIONAL ``"text"`` (default) or ``"html"``.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text confirming draft creation with draft id.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: delete_microsoft365_message
tools.description:
Delete an email message from the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "delete this email", "remove that message",
  "trash this email", etc. The message is moved to the Deleted Items folder.
  To permanently delete, call this on a message already in Deleted Items.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id to delete.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: download_microsoft365_attachment
tools.description:
Download the content of an email attachment.

When to call:
  Use this after ``list_microsoft365_email_attachments`` returns an
  attachment id and the user wants to retrieve the actual file content.

Behavior:
  - **Text-based attachments** (txt, csv, json, xml, html, md, yaml, log,
    etc.) are base64-decoded and the plain text content is returned directly
    so you can display it, process it, or write it to a file.
  - **Binary attachments** (pdf, docx, xlsx, images, zip, etc.) are returned
    as raw base64 content. You should write this base64 string to a local
    file using the appropriate tool (e.g. create a file with decoded bytes).

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id containing the attachment.
  attachment_id: REQUIRED. The Graph attachment id to download.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.

Returns:
  On success — attachment metadata + actual content (decoded text or base64).
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: move_microsoft365_message
tools.description:
Move an email message to a different folder in the mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "move this email to Archive", "move
  that message to the Projects folder", "organize my inbox", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id to move.
  destination_folder: REQUIRED. Either a well-known folder name
    (``"archive"``, ``"inbox"``, ``"drafts"``, ``"sentitems"``,
    ``"deleteditems"``, ``"junkemail"``, ``"outbox"``, ``"clutter"``)
    OR a Graph folder id (from ``list_microsoft365_mail_folders``).
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message with moved message info.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: update_microsoft365_draft
tools.description:
Update an existing draft email in the mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "edit the draft", "update the draft
  subject", "add recipients to the draft", etc. Only works on messages
  in the Drafts folder.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id of the draft to update.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
  subject: OPTIONAL. New subject line.
  body: OPTIONAL. New body content.
  body_format: OPTIONAL. "text" or "html". Default "text".
  to: OPTIONAL. New list of recipient emails (replaces existing).
  cc: OPTIONAL. New list of CC emails (replaces existing).
  bcc: OPTIONAL. New list of BCC emails (replaces existing).

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message with updated draft info.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: copy_microsoft365_message
tools.description:
Copy an email message to a different folder in the mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "copy this email to Archive", "duplicate
  that message to another folder", etc. Unlike move, the original message
  remains in its current location.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id to copy.
  destination_folder: REQUIRED. Either a well-known folder name
    (``"archive"``, ``"inbox"``, ``"drafts"``, ``"sentitems"``,
    ``"deleteditems"``, ``"junkemail"``, ``"outbox"``, ``"clutter"``)
    OR a Graph folder id (from ``list_microsoft365_mail_folders``).
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message with copied message info.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: list_microsoft365_mail_folders
tools.description:
List all mail folders in the user's mailbox.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks "what folders do I have?", "show my mail
  folders", or when you need a folder id for ``move_microsoft365_message``
  or ``copy_microsoft365_message`` and the target is a custom folder
  (not a well-known name like archive/inbox/drafts).

Authentication:
  Requires ``Mail.Read`` or ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
  include_children: OPTIONAL. If True, also fetches child folders
    (one level deep). Default False.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text with folder listing (id + displayName).
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: search_microsoft365_contacts
tools.description:
Search the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 personal contacts.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "find a contact", "look up Bob's email",
  "who do I know at Contoso?", or any address-book lookup on the user's
  PERSONAL contacts (NOT the org-wide directory).

Authentication:
  Requires the ``Contacts.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365
  account.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email of the authenticated user.
  query: OPTIONAL Microsoft Graph ``$search`` term.
  top: OPTIONAL page size (1-999). Default ``25``.
  next_link: OPTIONAL pagination URL returned by a previous call.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text with count summary, numbered list, and json block.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: get_microsoft365_contact
tools.description:
Get details of a specific Microsoft 365 personal contact by ID.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "get details of a contact", "show me the
  full info for contact <id>", or after searching contacts and wanting to
  fetch complete information for a specific contact.

Authentication:
  Requires the ``Contacts.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365
  account.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email of the authenticated user.
  contact_id: REQUIRED. The unique ID of the contact to retrieve.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text with contact details and json block.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: create_microsoft365_contact
tools.description:
Create a new contact in the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 personal contacts.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "add a new contact", "create a contact for
  John Doe", "save Bob's contact info", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires the ``Contacts.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365
  account.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email of the authenticated user.
  given_name: OPTIONAL. First name of the contact.
  surname: OPTIONAL. Last name of the contact.
  display_name: OPTIONAL. Full display name. Auto-generated if not provided.
  email_address: OPTIONAL. Primary email address.
  company_name: OPTIONAL. Company name.
  job_title: OPTIONAL. Job title.
  business_phones: OPTIONAL. List of business phone numbers.
  mobile_phone: OPTIONAL. Mobile phone number.
  home_phones: OPTIONAL. List of home phone numbers.
  business_address: OPTIONAL. Business address object with keys like
    ``street``, ``city``, ``state``, ``postalCode``, ``countryOrRegion``.
  home_address: OPTIONAL. Home address object with same structure.
  birthday: OPTIONAL. Birthday in ISO 8601 format (e.g. ``"1990-01-15"``).
  department: OPTIONAL. Department name.
  profession: OPTIONAL. Profession or occupation.
  personal_notes: OPTIONAL. Personal notes about the contact.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text confirming creation with contact summary.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: update_microsoft365_contact
tools.description:
Update an existing contact in Microsoft 365 personal contacts.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "update that contact's phone number",
  "change the email for John", "edit the contact info", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Contacts.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  contact_id: REQUIRED. The Graph contact id to update.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
  given_name: OPTIONAL. New first name.
  surname: OPTIONAL. New last name.
  display_name: OPTIONAL. New display name.
  email_address: OPTIONAL. New primary email address.
  company_name: OPTIONAL. New company name.
  job_title: OPTIONAL. New job title.
  business_phones: OPTIONAL. New business phone numbers.
  mobile_phone: OPTIONAL. New mobile phone.
  home_phones: OPTIONAL. New home phone numbers.
  department: OPTIONAL. New department.
  personal_notes: OPTIONAL. New personal notes.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation with updated contact summary.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: delete_microsoft365_contact
tools.description:
Delete a contact from Microsoft 365 personal contacts.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "delete that contact", "remove John
  from my contacts", "clean up old contact entries", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Contacts.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  contact_id: REQUIRED. The Graph contact id to delete.
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: get_microsoft365_user_profile
tools.description:
Return the connected Microsoft 365 user's profile (verifies credential).

When to call:
  Two main scenarios:
    1) After ``start_microsoft365_auth`` / ``set_microsoft365_credentials``
       — to confirm the credential actually works against Microsoft Graph.
    2) Before a multi-step workflow when you want a cheap pre-flight check
       (this hits ``GET /me``, the lightest Graph endpoint that requires
       ``User.Read``).
  Do NOT call it on every mail/contacts request — those tools already
  perform their own auth check.

Authentication:
  Requires ``User.Read`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email of the authenticated user.
    When omitted, the tool auto-locates the credential if exactly one
    account is connected.

Returns:
  On success — Markdown text starting with ``✅ Microsoft 365 profile verified``
  followed by a fenced json block.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: list_microsoft365_events
tools.description:
List upcoming calendar events for the authenticated Microsoft 365 user.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks "what's on my calendar?", "show my meetings
  this week", "do I have anything scheduled tomorrow?", etc.

Args:
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email. Auto-locates if one account.
  start_date: OPTIONAL. ISO 8601 datetime string for range start
    (e.g. ``"2024-06-01T00:00:00"``). Defaults to now.
  end_date: OPTIONAL. ISO 8601 datetime string for range end
    (e.g. ``"2024-06-07T23:59:59"``). Defaults to 7 days from now.
  top: OPTIONAL. Page size (1-999). Default 20.
  next_link: OPTIONAL. Pagination URL from a previous call.

Returns:
  Markdown text with event summaries + fenced json block.

tools.name: get_microsoft365_event
tools.description:
Fetch a single calendar event by id.

When to call:
  After ``list_microsoft365_events`` returns an event id and the user
  wants full details (body, attendees, online meeting link, etc.).

Args:
  event_id: REQUIRED. The Graph event id.
  user_email: OPTIONAL.

Returns:
  Markdown text with event details + fenced json.

tools.name: create_microsoft365_event
tools.description:
Create a new calendar event.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "schedule a meeting", "create a calendar
  event", "book time for...", etc.

Args:
  subject: REQUIRED. Event title.
  start_datetime: REQUIRED. ISO 8601 start (e.g. "2024-06-15T10:00:00").
  end_datetime: REQUIRED. ISO 8601 end (e.g. "2024-06-15T11:00:00").
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated account.
  time_zone: OPTIONAL. IANA time zone (default "UTC").
  location: OPTIONAL. Display name of the location.
  body: OPTIONAL. Event body/description.
  body_format: OPTIONAL. "text" (default) or "html".
  attendees: OPTIONAL. List of attendee email addresses.
  is_online_meeting: OPTIONAL. Create a Teams meeting link. Note: this
    uses the ``teamsForBusiness`` provider and requires a **work or school**
    account; personal Microsoft accounts do not support Teams online
    meetings and the request will fail.

Returns:
  Confirmation text + fenced json with created event summary.

tools.name: update_microsoft365_event
tools.description:
Update an existing calendar event (partial update / PATCH).

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "reschedule", "change the meeting title",
  "update the event description", etc.

Args:
  event_id: REQUIRED. Graph event id.
  user_email: OPTIONAL.
  subject: OPTIONAL. New subject.
  start_datetime: OPTIONAL. New start ISO 8601 datetime.
  end_datetime: OPTIONAL. New end ISO 8601 datetime.
  time_zone: OPTIONAL. IANA time zone for start/end.
  location: OPTIONAL. New location display name.
  body: OPTIONAL. New body content.
  body_format: OPTIONAL. "text" or "html".

Returns:
  Confirmation text + updated event summary json.

tools.name: delete_microsoft365_event
tools.description:
Delete a calendar event by id.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "cancel the meeting", "delete the event",
  "remove from my calendar", etc.

Args:
  event_id: REQUIRED. Graph event id.
  user_email: OPTIONAL.

Returns:
  Confirmation text on success, or error message on failure.

tools.name: accept_microsoft365_event
tools.description:
Accept a meeting invitation / calendar event.

When to call:
  Use this when the user asks to "accept the meeting", "confirm attendance",
  "say yes to this invite", etc. This sends an acceptance response to the
  organizer and updates the event status.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Calendars.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  event_id: REQUIRED. The Graph event id to accept.

tools.name: list_microsoft365_drive_items

List files and folders in the user's OneDrive.

  Documents folder?", "list files in /Reports", etc.

Args:

tools.name: search_microsoft365_drive

Search across the user's OneDrive for files and folders.

Returns:
  Markdown text with matched items + fenced json.

tools.name: get_microsoft365_drive_item
tools.description:
Get metadata (name, size, type, timestamps) for a specific OneDrive item.

IMPORTANT: This tool only returns metadata and a URL. It does NOT return
the actual file content. If the user wants to read, view, or download
the file content, use ``download_microsoft365_drive_file`` instead.

When to call:
  Use when you need file properties (size, MIME type, last modified date)
  or want to check if an item exists before performing operations.
  Do NOT use this for downloading — use ``download_microsoft365_drive_file``.

Args:
  item_id: The Graph driveItem id. One of item_id or path is required.
  path: Path relative to root (e.g. "/Documents/report.xlsx").
  user_email: OPTIONAL.

Returns:
  Markdown text with item metadata + fenced json (no file content).

tools.name: upload_microsoft365_drive_file
tools.description:
Upload a file (up to 250 MB) to OneDrive.

When to call:
  Use when the user asks to "save this to OneDrive", "upload a file",
  "put this document in my drive", etc. Supports both text and binary
  files.

Behavior:
  - **Text files** (default): pass the file content directly as a string
    in ``content`` with ``content_encoding="text"``.
  - **Binary files** (images, PDF, docx, etc.): pass base64-encoded file
    content in ``content`` with ``content_encoding="base64"``. The tool
    will decode it before uploading.

Args:
  file_name: REQUIRED. Target file name (e.g. "report.pdf", "photo.png").
  content: REQUIRED. File content — plain text string when
    content_encoding="text", or base64-encoded string when
    content_encoding="base64".
  user_email: OPTIONAL.
  parent_path: OPTIONAL. Parent folder path (e.g. "/Documents").
    Empty = root.
  content_type: OPTIONAL. MIME type (e.g. "application/pdf",
    "image/png"). If empty, auto-detected from file extension.
  content_encoding: OPTIONAL. How ``content`` is encoded:
    - ``"text"`` (default) — content is plain text, uploaded as-is.
    - ``"base64"`` — content is base64-encoded binary, decoded before upload.

Returns:
  Confirmation text + created item metadata json.

tools.name: create_microsoft365_drive_folder
tools.description:
Create a new folder in OneDrive.

When to call:

Args:
  folder_name: REQUIRED. Name of the new folder.

  parent_path: OPTIONAL. Parent folder path (e.g. "/Documents").

  parent_id: OPTIONAL. Graph driveItem id of parent folder.

Returns:
  Confirmation text + created folder metadata json.

tools.name: delete_microsoft365_drive_item

Delete a file or folder from OneDrive.

When to call:

  from OneDrive", "trash the old report", etc.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Files.ReadWrite.All`` scope.

Args:
  item_id: The Graph driveItem id. One of item_id or path is required.
  path: Path relative to root (e.g. "/Documents/old-report.xlsx").
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.

Returns:
  Confirmation text on success; error message on failure.

tools.name: download_microsoft365_drive_file
tools.description:
Download and return the actual content of a file from OneDrive.

When to call:
  Use this whenever the user wants to download, read, view, open, or get
  the content of a file from OneDrive. This is the ONLY tool that returns
  actual file content.

  Typical workflow:
    1. ``search_microsoft365_drive`` or ``list_microsoft365_drive_items``
       → find the file (get item_id)
    2. ``download_microsoft365_drive_file`` (this tool) → get file content

  Do NOT use ``get_microsoft365_drive_item`` for downloading — that tool
  only returns metadata, not content.

Behavior:
  - **Text-based files** (txt, csv, json, xml, html, md, yaml, py, etc.)
    are returned as decoded plain text, ready to display or write locally.
  - **Binary files** (pdf, docx, xlsx, images, zip, etc.) are returned as
    base64-encoded content. You should decode and write to a local file.

Authentication:
  Requires ``Files.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.

Args:
  item_id: The Graph driveItem id. One of item_id or path is required.
  path: Path relative to root (e.g. "/Documents/report.xlsx").
  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.

Returns:
  On success — file metadata + actual content (decoded text or base64).
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: move_rename_microsoft365_drive_item
tools.description:
Move or rename a file or folder in OneDrive.

Authentication:

Args:

  user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
  new_name: OPTIONAL. New name for the item. If not provided, name remains unchanged.
  new_parent_path: OPTIONAL. New parent folder path (e.g. "/Archive").
    Ignored if new_parent_id is provided.
  new_parent_id: OPTIONAL. Graph driveItem id of new parent folder.

Returns:
  On success — confirmation message with updated item info.
  On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.

tools.name: create_github_repo
tools.description:
Create a new GitHub repository, either under the authenticated user
or under a GitHub organization.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Create a new repo called my-project"
- "Help me set up a new private GitHub repository"
- "Initialize a new project on GitHub"
- "Create a repo named foo under the my-org organization"

Args:
    name: Repository name (required). Must be unique under the chosen
          owner (user or org). Example: "my-awesome-project".
    description: Short description of the repository.
    private: If True, create a private repo. Default False (public).
    auto_init: If True, initialize with a README. Default True.
    org: If provided, create the repo under this GitHub organization
         instead of the authenticated user's account. The authenticated
         user must have permission to create repositories in that org
         (org "Repository creation" policy + sufficient role). When
         omitted (default), the repo is created under the user's
         account — backward compatible.
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON with the created repo: full_name, html_url, private,
    description, default_branch, created_at.

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion. Common org
    failures: 403 (insufficient permission / org policy forbids creation),
    404 (org not found or not visible to the token), 422 (name already
    taken in the org).

tools.name: fork_github_repo
tools.description:
Fork an existing GitHub repository to the authenticated user's account.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Fork facebook/react to my account"
- "I want my own copy of this repo"
- "Fork this project to my org"

Args:
    owner: Owner of the repository to fork, e.g. "facebook".
    repo: Repository name to fork, e.g. "react".
    organization: If provided, fork to this org instead of the user's account.
                  The user must be a member of the org.
    name: Custom name for the forked repo. Default is the original repo name.
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON with the forked repo: full_name, html_url, private,
    description, parent (source repo full_name).

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

tools.name: list_github_repos
tools.description:
List GitHub repositories accessible to the authenticated user,
including **private repos** that are invisible without login.

By default, lists repos owned by / accessible to the authenticated user
(``GET /user/repos``). When ``organization`` is supplied, the tool
switches to listing repos under that organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``);
private repos the authenticated user has access to within the org are
included.

Note: this tool intentionally does NOT accept a ``username`` filter.
GitHub's ``GET /users/{username}/repos`` endpoint only ever returns
public repositories — even when authenticated and even when the
username matches the caller — so exposing it here would mislead users
into thinking private repos can be listed by username. To see your
own private repos, simply omit ``organization``.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "What repos do I have?"
- "Show me my private repositories"
- "List my recently updated projects"
- "Show all repositories under the alibaba organization"

Args:
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    visibility: Filter — "all" (default), "public", or "private".
        Only applies when listing the authenticated user's own repos
        (i.e. ``organization`` is not provided).
    sort: Sort field — "created", "updated" (default), "pushed", or "full_name".
    per_page: Results per page, 1–100. Default 20.
    page: Page number starting at 1.
    organization: If provided, list repositories under this GitHub
        organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``).

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ repos: [...], pagination: {...}, user_login,
    scope: {...} }``. ``scope`` describes which listing was performed:
    ``{"type": "self" | "org", "target": <name or null>}``.
    Each repo: full_name, description, html_url, private, language,
    stargazers_count, forks_count, updated_at, default_branch.

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

tools.name: star_github_repo
tools.description:
Star a GitHub repository as the authenticated user.

Call this tool when the user asks:

Args:

    repo: Repository name, e.g. "react".

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ starred: true, repo: "owner/repo" }``

tools.name: unstar_github_repo
tools.description:
Unstar a GitHub repository as the authenticated user.

Call this tool when the user asks:

Args:
    owner: Repository owner, e.g. "facebook".
    repo: Repository name, e.g. "react".

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ unstarred: true, repo: "owner/repo" }``

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

tools.name: list_github_starred
tools.description:
List repositories that the authenticated user has starred.

This is the user's personal bookmark / collection list on GitHub.

Call this tool when the user asks:

- "Show my GitHub stars"
- "What projects did I bookmark?"

Args:
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    sort: Sort field — "created" (default, when you starred it) or "updated".
    direction: Sort direction — "desc" (default, newest first) or "asc".
    per_page: Results per page, 1–100. Default 20.
    page: Page number starting at 1.

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ starred_repos: [...], pagination: {...}, user_login }``
