tools.name: compare_asin_keywords
tools.description:
Helium 10 Keyword Research (Cerebro). Multi-ASIN keyword comparison for one main ASIN vs 1–10 competitors: returns the compare scope (union of organic phrases from the main ASIN and each competitor — not intersection only) with each phrase's CPS, search volume, main organic rank, competitor coverage, and competitive average rank; the scope includes main-only keywords (cps = 0), gap/opportunity keywords, and shared competitive keywords.

When to use: call when the user's question — across multiple ASINs — involves keyword competition, shared keywords, competitor organic ranking, competitive pressure, CPS, or gap/opportunity keywords, even if they never say "CPS". Complement with get_keywords_by_asin as needed for richer per-ASIN metrics.

Not for: single-ASIN questions with no compare intent.

Edge case: the main ASIN may return no Cerebro rows — still call; results are then driven by the competitor side (rows where the main ASIN does not rank organically omit main_organic_rank).

main_asin.description: Primary ASIN under analysis (the user's product), 10-char alphanumeric (e.g. B09F9C3KFS).
main_asin.title: Main Asin

competitor_asins.description: 1 to 10 competitor ASINs (must NOT include main_asin). Each ASIN is 10-char alphanumeric.
competitor_asins.title: Competitor Asins

marketplace.description: Marketplace code: US, UK, DE, JP, etc. Must be in the Cerebro allowlist.
marketplace.title: Marketplace

data.description: Multi-ASIN CPS compare payload when the call succeeds. May be omitted or empty on failure—check for an ``error`` payload.

keywords.description: One row per phrase in the CPS compare scope (main ASIN plus competitors — organic union). Sorted by ``cps`` descending. Optional fields with no value are omitted (not sent as null).

phrase.description: Keyword Phrase — search term in the CPS compare scope (main + competitor organic union).

search_volume.description: Search Volume — estimated monthly Amazon searches for this phrase.

main_organic_rank.description: Your Rank — main ASIN organic rank for this phrase. Absent = main ASIN does not rank organically (gap word); treat a missing field the same as null.

ranking_competitors.description: Competitors Ranking (numerator) — number of competitor ASINs that rank organically for this phrase (excludes the main ASIN).

total_competitors.description: Competitors Ranking (denominator) — total de-duplicated competitor ASINs supplied in the request (excludes the main ASIN).

competitive_avg.description: Competitive Avg — arithmetic mean organic rank of the competitors that rank for this phrase. Absent when no competitor ranks organically.

cps.description: CPS (Competitor Performance Score), 0–10. Higher = more competitive pressure (competitors rank well and broadly). 0 = main-only word (no competitor ranks organically) or formula 0.

error.description: Structured error response from io-api for MCP endpoints.

details.description: Optional structured error details.

remediation.description: Optional human-readable remediation guidance (may be omitted).

tools.name: compare_listings
tools.description: Helium 10 Listing Comparison. Returns the field set from Compare Key Metrics for every ASIN in the session — the main ASIN plus all competitor ASINs — as an array of objects under asins. The main ASIN is always first, flagged with is_main: true. Maps to the Compare Key Metrics Across ASINs table in the LA UI. Use to benchmark your listing against multiple competitors at once, see where you're ahead or behind on content and sales, and build a prioritized improvement list. Competitor ASINs that are valid 10-char codes but can't be resolved upstream are not returned as empty rows — they are split out into failed_asins as {asin, error} so the asins rows always carry real data. Not for: a single-ASIN lookup (use get_listing_details); keyword comparison (use get_top_keywords); the LQS checklist (use get_listing_score).

main_asin.description: Main Amazon ASIN (10 characters). Always emitted as the first row of ``asins`` with ``is_main: true``.
main_asin.title: Main Asin

competitor_asins.description: Up to 10 competitor ASINs (each 10 characters). Required: ``compare_listings`` only returns rows in multi-ASIN mode. Empty / blank entries are dropped before the upstream call.
competitor_asins.title: Competitor Asins

marketplace.description: Optional marketplace short code where the ASINs are listed. Supported: US, CA, MX, DE, ES, IT, FR, UK, IN, NL, AE, BR, AU. Defaults to US when omitted. Case-insensitive; whitespace is trimmed.
marketplace.title: Marketplace

data.description: Multi-mode only — same field set as ``get_listing_details.seed_data`` for every ASIN in the session (main ASIN plus all competitor ASINs). The main ASIN is always first, flagged with ``is_main: true``. Maps to the ``Compare Key Metrics Across ASINs`` table in the Listing Analyzer UI. Rows are returned under ``asins``. Partial-failure handling: a competitor ASIN that is a valid 10-char code but could not be resolved upstream (not found / no data) is NOT emitted as an empty ``asins`` row — it is split out into ``failed_asins`` with an error code, so every row in ``asins`` carries real data.

asins.description: Per-ASIN listing rows that resolved successfully. Main ASIN first (``is_main: true``); the remaining rows are the caller-supplied competitor ASINs in the order returned by upstream. ASINs that could not be resolved are excluded here and listed in ``failed_asins`` instead.

is_main.description: True for the main ASIN (always emitted as the first array entry); false for competitor ASINs.

asin.description: ASIN this row describes.

lqs.description: Listing Quality Score (LQS) — 0–10 score; an analysis of this product's copy, media and reviews.

top10_keywords.description: Top 10 Keywords — Number of keywords in which this product ranks in the top 10.

top10_search_volumes.description: Top 10 Search Volume — Total search volume for the keywords in which this product ranks in the top 10.

is_coupon_exists.description: Coupon Status — whether this listing currently advertises a coupon.

coupon_value.description: Coupon Value — raw coupon-value payload, most often a nested object such as ``{amount: 5}``; occasionally a scalar. Treat it as an opaque blob. Null when no coupon is active or the value was not reported.

coupon_type.description: Coupon Type — discount kind (e.g. ``percentage``, ``absolute``). Null when no coupon is active.

sales_rank.description: Category BSR — Best Seller Rank; Amazon-awarded rank for the main category.

price.description: Price — Price at which the product is sold (already converted to major currency units, e.g. dollars).

price_change.description: Price change indicator vs. recent baseline (upstream-defined direction code).

review_count.description: Review — Total number of customer reviews.

reviews_rating.description: Rating — Amazon customer reviews rating from poor (1.0) to outstanding (5.0).

monthly_revenue.description: Parent Level Revenue — Estimated revenue for all child ASINs under this parent over the past 30 days (major currency units).

monthly_sales.description: Parent Level Sales — Estimated sales for all child ASINs under this parent over the past 30 days.

sales_change.description: Parent Level Sales change indicator vs. recent baseline.

seller_type.description: Fulfillment — Method of storage and shipping. FBA = Fulfilled by Amazon, FBM = Fulfilled by Merchant, Amazon = Sold by Amazon (encoded as integer code).

age.description: Age (Month) — Listing age in full calendar months from original list date through today (UTC). Null when upstream age is missing or invalid.

seller_country.description: Seller Region — Seller's country/region of origin.

category_title.description: Top-level Amazon category name for this ASIN.

best_sellers_url.description: Amazon Best Sellers list URL for this product's category.

number_of_sellers.description: Number of active sellers competing on this listing.

subcategories.description: Subcategory entries for this ASIN. Each item carries node_id / node_name / subcategory_url / subcategory_bsr (subcategory BSR rank).

subcategory_url.description: Amazon Best Sellers URL scoped to this subcategory.

subcategory_bsr.description: Subcategory Best Seller Rank for this ASIN.

subcategories_bsr.description: Per-subcategory BSR rows (alternate shape to ``subcategories``); each item has ``node_id`` and ``bsr``. ``node_id`` is the same string form as ``subcategories[*].node_id`` so consumers can join the two lists by plain string equality.

node_id.description: Subcategory browse node id. String form (aligned with ``subcategories[*].node_id``) so the two lists can be joined with string equality.

bsr.description: Best Seller Rank within this subcategory.

year_sales.description: Last Year Sales — Sales over the trailing 12 months.

sales_year_over_year.description: Parent-level YoY sales delta indicator vs. last year (e.g. -13 means 13% lower than last year). Same shape as ``child_sales_year_over_year``.

size_tier.description: Amazon size tier classification (encoded id; e.g. small standard / oversize).

storage_fee.description: Storage Fee — FBA storage fee per 1,000 units / month, split into ``jan_sept`` (Jan–Sept rate, USD) and ``oct_dec`` (Oct–Dec rate, USD). Only populated for US-marketplace, Fulfilled-by-Amazon listings whose size tier is in the supported FBA bucket (small/large standard, large bulky, or any of the four extra-large tiers). Null in every other case (non-US marketplace, non-FBA seller, unsupported size tier, or missing package dimensions).

best_month.description: Best Sales Period — Calendar month in which a product sees its highest sales volume.

number_of_images.description: Number of Images on the product listing.

variation_count.description: Variation Count — Number of product variations.

sales_to_reviews.description: Sales to Reviews — Monthly Sales / Total Reviews Count (float).

stock.description: Stock — Estimated number of units left in inventory.

stock_has_limit.description: Whether upstream reports an inventory cap on this listing. Null when upstream did not report it.

child_monthly_sales.description: ASIN Sales — Estimated sales for this specific ASIN over the past 30 days.

child_sales_change.description: ASIN-level sales change indicator vs. recent baseline.

child_monthly_revenue.description: ASIN Revenue — Estimated revenue for this specific ASIN over the past 30 days (major currency units).

failed_asins.description: Competitor ASINs that were syntactically valid but could not be resolved upstream (not found or no analyzable data returned — an otherwise-empty row). Each entry is ``{asin, error}``. Null / omitted when every requested ASIN resolved. The main ASIN never appears here (an unresolved main ASIN fails the whole call upstream).

asin.description: The competitor ASIN that could not be resolved.

error.description: Machine-readable failure reason. ``ASIN_NOT_FOUND`` when upstream returned no analyzable data for this ASIN.
Always null — Listing Analyzer surfaces failures as an MCP error result (isError=true), not as an inline error payload.

tools.name: execute_ads_query
tools.description: Helium 10 Run Ads Query (Data Query, step 5 of 5, terminal). Given a platform key, level, dimensions, measures, filters, date range, and optional profile_ids, runs the query and returns columns + rows (no middleware translation, truncation, or pagination). Use to retrieve advertising performance — spend, ROAS, ACoS, impressions, clicks, conversions, and more — across any supported dimension and time range. profile_ids is RECOMMENDED, not required — pass an explicit list when the user named a specific profile (resolve via get_ads_query_materials); leaving it empty / omitted is accepted by upstream and treated as 'every profile the user has access to' (tenant isolation stays enforced via the inbound bearer token). State filtering is supported: the state field and its enum are in get_ads_query_schema — add a not_in/in/eq filter to exclude or include archived/deleted/removed states per the user's intent. No default; leave state unconstrained unless the request implies a status scope. Prerequisites: steps 1–3 for a valid spec; step 4 to resolve profile/campaign ids the user named.

mode.description: Comparison mode. **Only ``pop`` (Period over Period) is supported today**; any other value will be rejected by the backend with a structured 400. Kept as a plain string rather than a StrEnum so future expansion (yoy / qoq / mom / ...) does not force a wrapper release. Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required when ``compare`` is set. Default null -- the wrapper drops the ``mode`` key from the wire when it is null or empty (and, if every child of ``compare`` is null / empty, drops the whole block).
mode.title: Mode

current.description: Current-period date range as a 2-element ``[start, end]`` array. Format: ``yyyy-MM-dd`` or ``yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss`` (no timezone offset). The upstream rejects zero-length lists outright (``compare.current and compare.previous must each be a 2-element [start, end] range``); when the LLM leaves the field null or passes an empty list, the wrapper drops the ``current`` key from the wire (and, if every child of ``compare`` is null / empty, drops the whole block) so the validator never fires. Default null.
current.title: Current

previous.description: Previous-period date range as a 2-element ``[start, end]`` array. Same format, validation and wrapper-drop-on-empty semantics as ``current``.
previous.title: Previous

Dimension.description: A single GROUP BY dimension. Time-typed dimensions also need ``granularity``.

field.description: Dimension field name as declared in the schema returned by get_ads_query_schema (dimensions[].field), e.g. campaign_name, ad_group_id, date. Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful dimension entry.
field.title: Field

granularity.description: Time bucket granularity (typical values: day / week / month / quarter / year). Required for date/time dimensions; ignored for non-time dimensions. Free-form string -- the authoritative set is platform-specific and surfaced by get_ads_query_schema. Default null.
granularity.title: Granularity

Dimension.title: Dimension

Filter.description: A single WHERE-clause condition. Combine via AND across the filters array.

field.description: Field name to filter on, as declared in the schema (filters[].field or dimensions[].field). Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful filter entry.
field.title: Field

op.description: Comparison operator. Valid ops are advertised per-field by get_ads_query_schema (filters[].ops); typical values: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, not_in, like, not_like, between. Use not_in to exclude delete-like enum values when filtering state-like fields (archived, deleted, removed, ...). Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful filter entry.
op.title: Op

value.description: Comparison value. Type follows the field's declared schema type: scalar for eq / ne / gt / lt, array for in / not_in, two-element array for between. Nullable on the upstream contract.
value.title: Value

field.description: Field name to filter on, as declared in the schema (filters[].field or dimensions[].field). Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful filter entry.

op.description: Comparison operator. Valid ops are advertised per-field by get_ads_query_schema (filters[].ops); typical values: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, not_in, like, not_like, between. Use not_in to exclude delete-like enum values when filtering state-like fields (archived, deleted, removed, ...). Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful filter entry.
op.title: Op

value.description: Comparison value. Type follows the field's declared schema type: scalar for eq / ne / gt / lt, array for in / not_in, two-element array for between. Nullable on the upstream contract.
value.title: Value

HavingFilter.title: HavingFilter

Options.description:
Query-level options passed through to the backend.

Field naming mirrors the swagger ``QueryOptions`` schema but uses
snake_case on the input surface; the tool's body builder renames each
key to its camelCase wire form (``attribution_window`` ->
``attributionWindow``, ``to_currency`` -> ``toCurrency``).

attribution_window.description: Attribution window for ad-conversion measures (e.g. 7d, 14d, 30d). Default ``14d``; pass an explicit ``null`` to opt out and let the backend choose. Wire field: ``attributionWindow``.
attribution_window.title: Attribution Window

to_currency.description: Target currency code (ISO 4217, e.g. USD, EUR, GBP). When set to a non-empty value, the backend converts monetary measures (spend / sales / ...) into this currency before returning rows. Default ``""`` (empty string) -- the backend treats empty as 'no currency conversion' and returns each profile's native currency. Pass an explicit ``null`` to omit the field entirely. Wire field: ``toCurrency``.
to_currency.title: To Currency

Options.title: Options

field.description: Field or measure name to sort by. Must appear in the chosen dimensions or measures. Nullable on the upstream contract; semantically required for a meaningful order-by entry.
field.title: Field

direction.description: Sort direction (typical values: ``asc`` / ``desc``). Free-form string. Default null -- the backend treats absent direction as ``desc``.
direction.title: Direction

platform.description: Platform key (e.g. amazon, walmart). Same value used in get_ads_query_list and get_ads_query_schema.
platform.title: Platform

level.description: Level name (e.g. profile, campaign, target). Same value used in get_ads_query_schema.
level.title: Level

profile_ids.description: Tenant-isolation profile ids (string[]). Optional on the input surface; the upstream swagger marks ``profileIds`` as nullable and accepts an empty list as 'every profile the user has access to' (tenant isolation is still enforced via the inbound bearer token). Forward an explicit list when the user named a specific profile (resolve via get_ads_query_materials(level=profile); each returned row carries the profile id as a number, so stringify it before forwarding -- e.g. ``["100001", "100002"]``). When omitted, the wrapper emits ``profileIds: []`` on the wire, which the backend interprets as the user's full accessible set. Wire field: ``profileIds``.
profile_ids.title: Profile Ids

dimensions.description: Group-by dimensions. Each item picks a field from the schema (dimensions[]) and an optional time granularity. Default null (no grouping; one aggregate row).
dimensions.title: Dimensions

measures.description: Measure (aggregated metric) field names from the schema (measures[]). Default null (no measures; dimension-only query).
measures.title: Measures

filters.description: WHERE-clause conditions, AND-combined. State filtering is supported — add a not_in/in/eq filter on the state field (enum from schema) only when the request implies it; no exclude-by-default.
filters.title: Filters

having.description: HAVING-clause conditions on aggregated measures, AND-combined. Default null.
having.title: Having

compare.description: Period-over-period comparison config. Default null (no comparison).

order_by.description: Sort order. Multi-key sort applies items in array order. Default null (backend-default ordering).
order_by.title: Order By

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default null (backend default).
limit.title: Limit

offset.description: Row offset for pagination. Default null (no offset).
offset.title: Offset

options.description: Query-level options. Default null -- when omitted, the ``options`` field is not sent on the wire at all. When you pass an object (even ``{}``), the per-field defaults apply: ``attribution_window="14d"`` and ``to_currency=""`` (empty string, which the backend interprets as 'no currency conversion'). Pass an explicit ``null`` on a sub-field to opt out of that default.

tools.name: get_ads_query_platforms
tools.description:
Helium 10 Available Ad Platforms (Data Query, step 1 of 5). Returns the advertising platforms available to query in your account (e.g. amazon, walmart). No inputs required — platforms are derived from your account credentials (the inbound bearer token). The entry point: use it to get valid platform keys before steps 2–5. Not for: actual performance numbers (use execute_ads_query after the intermediate steps). Next: get_ads_query_list(platform).

### Data Query pipeline

① get_ads_query_platforms → ② get_ads_query_list → ③ get_ads_query_schema → ④ get_ads_query_materials → ⑤ user selects specific profile(s) → ⑥ execute_ads_query

### Required profile selection

Before calling execute_ads_query, the user must choose specific profiles from the profile/material results.

1. Call get_ads_query_materials for the relevant scope (profile, advertiser, vendor_account, or seller_account).
2. Build a concise selection list from the returned materials. Each option should include the display name plus the id that will be sent to execute_ads_query.
3. Use Cursor's AskQuestion tool with multi-select enabled when available so the user gets a real choice list. Do not proceed from a plain text assumption.
4. Continue only after the user selects at least one option. Send only the selected ids in profile_ids or the matching scope id field.
5. Never call execute_ads_query with all profiles by default, a guessed default profile, or profiles inferred only from prior context.

If the returned material list is too large, show the most relevant profiles first and include an 'Other profile id' option. If there is only one returned profile, still ask the user to confirm that profile before executing.

tools.name: get_listing_details

Not for: comparing multiple ASINs (use compare_listings); the LQS pass/fail checklist (use get_listing_score); keyword strategy (use get_top_keywords).

tools.name: get_listing_score
tools.description: Helium 10 Listing Quality Audit. For an ASIN group (main + up to 10 competitors), returns the session-average LQS (0–10) with aggregate pass/fail counts per criterion, plus individual LQS scores and pass/fail results for all 13 criteria per ASIN — across Copy, Media, and Review (title symbols/length, ≥5 bullets, bullet length, image resolution & count, white-background main image, video presence, description ≥1000 chars or A+, ≥20 reviews, ≥4-star rating). All ASINs returned in one call; the agent surfaces whichever ASIN the user asks about. Use to understand content-compliance scores, pinpoint which elements drag LQS down, and compare listing quality across competitors. Not for: full attribute lookup (use get_listing_details); a quick LQS number alongside other metrics (use compare_listings).

data.description: Listing Quality Score (LQS) analysis per ASIN: ``score_data`` keys each ASIN to its ``lqs`` plus a per-metric pass / fail breakdown (single mode carries just the main ASIN; multi mode carries every session ASIN). ``summary_data`` (multi mode only) adds the cross-ASIN ``average_lqs`` and per-metric passed / failed ASIN lists. Use when the user asks about listing quality, content compliance, or what specifically needs improvement.

lqs.description: 0–10 Listing Quality Score for this ASIN (a perfect score is emitted as the integer ``10``).

Single mode carries exactly one entry (the main ASIN); multi mode carries one entry per session ASIN (main ASIN plus competitors). Expenditure metrics (refund, promo, advertising_cost, amazon_fees, cost_of_goods, expenses, indirect_cost) are returned as NEGATIVE values (cash outflows). Income metrics (sales, reimbursements, estimated_payout, gross_revenue, gross_profit, net_profit) are positive when the period is profitable. Per-metric notes: sales — gross sales revenue before any deductions; refund — total refund/return amount (negative, expenditure); promo — promotional discounts (negative, expenditure); advertising_cost — total ad spend across Sponsored Products, Brands, Display (negative, expenditure); amazon_fees — all Amazon platform fees: FBA, referral, etc. (negative, expenditure); reimbursements — Amazon reimbursement credits; estimated_payout — estimated settlement payout from Amazon; cost_of_goods — seller-defined cost of goods sold / COGS (negative, expenditure); gross_revenue — top-line revenue (sales minus refunds); gross_profit — gross_revenue minus amazon_fees and cost_of_goods; expenses — total operating expenses (negative, expenditure); indirect_cost — overhead / indirect costs allocated to this period (negative, expenditure); net_profit — bottom-line profit after all deductions. Rate/percentage values (float, rounded to 2 decimal places, expressed as a percentage, e.g. 21.01 means 21.01%): margin — net profit margin (net_profit / gross_revenue × 100); roi — return on investment (net_profit / cost_of_goods × 100); tacos — TACoS (attr 1 day): ad spend / total sales, using Profits 1-day attribution for ad spend alignment; measures ad spend impact on total sales and profitability (advertising_cost / gross_revenue × 100); ads_acos — ACoS (attr 1 day): ACOS based on Profits ad sales (1-day attribution, SKU-level SP/SD only); use mainly for profit, same-day, or organic sales analysis — for general advertising performance prefer Ads ACOS (advertising_cost / ad-attributed sales × 100); refunds_percentage — refund rate (refund / gross_revenue × 100). Count metrics (integer, e.g. 6): units_sold — total units ordered; units_returned — total units returned/refunded; sessions — unique visitor sessions on product detail pages. A key is omitted when its value is null for the period.

tools.name: get_top_keywords
tools.description: Helium 10 Top Keywords for Listing. For an ASIN group, returns keyword data in two layers — an aggregate summary and a per-keyword detail table (search volume, keyword sales, CPR, organic rank, per-ASIN ranks) — plus a side-by-side view of which keywords competitors rank for that you don't. Summary is always returned. Field names differ by mode: single ASIN mode (no competitors) returns total_keywords, top10_keywords, total_search_volume, top10_search_volume; multi ASIN mode (with competitors) returns total_shared_keywords, shared_top10_keywords, total_shared_search_volume, shared_top10_search_volume. The response includes a mode field ("single" or "multi") so the caller knows which field set to expect. Keyword details are conditionally returned. In multi-ASIN mode, a keyword qualifies when: at least 2 ASINs share it, average competitor rank is between 1–40, at least 4 ranking competitors, and search volume > 500. In single-ASIN mode, a keyword qualifies when: word count ≥ 2, search volume > 500, and organic rank ≤ 10. When no keywords qualify, keyword_details returns an empty array [] and no_ranking_keywords is set to true. Use to see which keywords drive the most traffic, find coverage gaps versus competitors. Organic ranking signals only — paid keyword data is out of scope. Not for: general attribute comparison (use compare_listings); LQS or sales data (use get_listing_score).

marketplace.description: Optional marketplace short code where the ASIN is listed. Supported: US, CA, MX, DE, ES, IT, FR, UK, IN, NL, AE, BR, AU. Defaults to US when omitted. Case-insensitive; whitespace is trimmed.
marketplace.title: Marketplace

competitor_asins.description: Optional list of up to 10 competitor ASINs (each 10 characters). When non-empty the response switches to multi mode: per-phrase rows gain shared-rank metrics and the aggregates move to summary_multi (Shared* variants). When omitted or empty the call runs in single mode.
competitor_asins.title: Competitor Asins

data.description: Keyword data for the session ASIN group, split into two layers (single vs multi). Aggregate field names differ by mode (see ``mode``); ``keyword_details`` is the per-phrase passthrough.

mode.description: ``single`` when the session has only the main ASIN; ``multi`` when competitor ASINs are present.

no_ranking_keywords.description: True when ``keyword_details`` is empty (no top-ranking keywords found).

keyword_details.description:
Top keyword phrases for the session. Element shape differs by mode:
* single mode — phrase + organic_position + search_volume + monthly_sales (Keyword Sales) + new_cpr_exact / new_cpr_broad (CPR, rounded integers) + search_volume_trend30 + iq + cpc / high_cpc / low_cpc + amazon_choice + results_number + match-type fields.
* multi mode — phrase + organic_position + search_volume + monthly_sales (Keyword Sales) + competitive_avg (Organic Rank Avg) + ranking_competitors + position_range + new_cpr_exact / new_cpr_broad (CPR, rounded integers) + search_volume_trend30 + competitor_performance_score (Performance Score Avg) + amazon_choice + match_type.

new_cpr_exact.description: CPR (Exact) — Estimated number of units that need to be sold over 8 days, resulting from a search for this keyword in order for the product to rank on top half page one. Rounded to an integer (the raw value is a float, e.g. 355.85).

new_cpr_broad.description: CPR (Broad) — same definition as ``new_cpr_exact`` but computed against the broad-title-match competitor pool. Also rounded to an integer.

summary_single.description: Single-mode keyword aggregates. Populated when ``mode == 'single'``; omitted (key absent) when ``mode == 'multi'``.

total_keywords.description: Total Keywords — Number of keywords this ASIN organically ranks in the top 306.

top10_keywords.description: Number of keywords for which this ASIN organically ranks in the top 10 (rank ≤ 10).

total_search_volume.description: Total Search Volume — Combined Search Volume generated by Total Keywords.

top10_search_volume.description: Top 10 Search Volume — Combined Search Volume generated by Top 10 Keywords.

summary_multi.description: Multi-mode keyword aggregates. Populated when ``mode == 'multi'``; omitted (key absent) when ``mode == 'single'``.

total_shared_keywords.description: Total Shared Keywords — Number of keywords where at least 2 ASINs are organically in the top 306.

shared_top10_keywords.description: Number of keywords that at least 2 ASINs organically rank on with average rank ≤ 10.

total_shared_search_volume.description: Total Shared Search Volume — Combined Search Volume generated by Total Shared Keywords.

shared_top10_search_volume.description: Shared Top 10 Search Volume — Combined Search Volume generated by Shared Top 10 Keywords.

tools.name: list_my_products
tools.description: Return a paginated list of the caller's OWN Amazon product rows (one row per SKU x marketplace x seller). Each row carries product identity only: product_name, asin, sku, brand, image_url, product_page_url, seller_id, marketplace, fulfillment_type. No P&L, inventory, or listing-analysis metrics. No required input — default scope is all sellers authorised by the Pacvue token; call with no arguments to page through the full authorised catalog. Use when the user asks to list, browse, or find their own products/SKUs/ASINs across linked seller accounts, needs product metadata (title, image, Amazon listing URL) before calling P&L or inventory tools, or wants to resolve which SKUs match a name/brand within their catalog. Narrow with seller_ids, marketplace, asins, skus, fulfillment_type (FBA | FBM), product_name (case-insensitive LIKE on title), or brand_name (case-insensitive LIKE on brand). Not for: market-wide product or competitor research (use search_products / search_inactive_products); profit & loss metrics (use get_product_profit_and_loss_summary); inventory on-hand / inbound quantities (use get_inventory_values); deep single-ASIN listing profile / BSR / scores (use get_listing_details). Does not distinguish active vs inactive listing status; rows reflect whatever Profits has ingested. No sort parameters — order is backend-defined.

seller_ids.description: Optional. SQL IN filter on seller account IDs (array of strings). Profits intersects with sellers from Pacvue token; no intersection → empty result. Default null (all authorised sellers).
seller_ids.title: Seller Ids

marketplace.description: Optional marketplace filter as an array of region short codes (e.g. ['US', 'CA', 'MX']). Allowed: AE, AU, BE, BR, CA, CN, DE, EG, ES, FR, IE, IN, IT, JP, MX, NL, PL, SA, SE, SG, TR, UK, US, ZA. Default null (all authorised marketplaces).
marketplace.title: Marketplace

asins.description: Optional. SQL IN filter by ASIN list (array of strings, e.g. ['B001234567']). Default null (all ASINs).
asins.title: Asins

skus.description: Optional. SQL IN filter by seller SKU list (array of strings). Default null (all SKUs).
skus.title: Skus

fulfillment_type.description: Optional fulfillment channel filter: FBA | FBM. Omit to query both FBA and FBM inventory.
fulfillment_type.title: Fulfillment Type

product_name.description: Optional. Case-insensitive substring match (SQL LIKE '%keyword%') against the product listing title. Omit or null = no title filter (rows with any title, including empty, may be returned).
product_name.title: Product Name

brand_name.description: Optional. Case-insensitive substring match (SQL LIKE '%keyword%') against the brand name. Omit or null = no brand filter (rows with brand: null may still be returned).
brand_name.title: Brand Name

page_index.description: Optional. Page number (integer), starts from 1. Default 1.
page_index.title: Page Index

page_size.description: Optional. Rows per page (integer). Min 5, max 1000. Default 50.

tools.name: list_tracked_competitor_keywords
tools.description: Helium 10 Competitor Keyword Rank Tracker. For a main ASIN with competitor ASINs configured in Keyword Tracker, returns the tracked keywords with your rank, each competitor's rank, relative_rank, rank_avg, and Competitor Performance Score (CPS) side-by-side. Use to find rank gaps on shared keywords, prioritize which keywords deserve PPC or listing investment, and monitor whether competitor moves are eroding your visibility. Not for: a single-ASIN view (use list_tracked_keywords); discovering new keywords (use get_keywords_new_suggestion); competitors not yet in Keyword Tracker (add them there first). Errors: invalid_input / invalid_asin / no_result / no_data / rate_limited / upstream_timeout. Degradation: reach_limitation (partial results returned).

tools.name: search_alert_events
tools.description: Helium 10 Alerts — query listing-change alert events for a seller. Supports three modes: (1) recent events — omit dates, returns latest `limit` events; (2) date-range — provide start_time + end_time; (3) single-event lookup — provide fired_at timestamp. Optionally filter by ASIN or alert_types. Do NOT use for Buy Box ownership history; use search_buybox_history instead.

tools.name: search_amazon_brand_analytics
tools.description: Helium 10 Top Search Terms & Brand Analytics (formerly Black Box — ABA). Exports Amazon Brand Analytics (ABA) Top Search Terms: per-phrase search frequency rank, exact/broad search volume with trend, CPC range, the top-3 clicked ASINs with click & conversion share, combined clicked-product metrics, and share trend vs the prior period. Use to find which products consumers click for a term, identify click/conversion-share leaders, compare ABA periods week-over-week or month-over-month, and find which keywords a competitor ASIN appears in. REQUIRES Brand Registry — non-Brand accounts get PERMISSION.DENIED. Not for: generic keyword search volume only (use search_amazon_keywords).

Use the bare field for ascending/smallest/lowest/A-to-Z sort, and the same field prefixed with '-' for descending/largest/highest/Z-to-A sort. For search_frequency_rank, ascending means more popular (lower rank) first.

tools.name: search_amazon_keywords
tools.description: Helium 10 Keyword Database Search (formerly Black Box — Search Keywords). Searches the FULL Helium 10 keyword database (not one ASIN's keywords) by filters (search-volume / impression range, word count, competing products, price, monthly revenue, reviews, rating, category, density, broad reach potential, and top-10 competitor distribution buckets). Returns paginated keyword rows with demand metrics, competitive landscape, and aggregated top-10 competitor profile data. Use for market-level keyword discovery, low-competition keyword mining, niche sizing by demand, and category keyword-landscape analysis — no ASIN or seed term needed. Not for: ABA click/conversion share & top clicked products (use search_amazon_brand_analytics); product lists (use search_products / search_inactive_products).

sort_by.description: Keywords sort field. Use default when the user does not request a specific sort. Use the bare field for ascending/smallest/lowest/A-to-Z sort, and the same field prefixed with '-' for descending/largest/highest/Z-to-A sort. Allowed fields: phrase=keyword phrase text; last_30_days_sales=sales in the last 30 days; monthly_revenue=monthly revenue; price=price; reviews_number=review count; reviews_rating=review rating; best_sellers_rank=Best Sellers Rank, where lower rank means better sales rank; sellers_number=seller count; variation_count=variation count; exact_impression_count_last_30_days=exact 30-day impression count; words_count=number of words in the phrase; results_number=number of Amazon search results; broad_reach_potential=broad reach potential.

触发条件：用户输入「商品{ID} 检测商品风险」「{商品URL} 检测商品风险」，或发出「扫描店铺风险」「检测商品风险」等通用指令，且已登录商家账号。
期望产出：返回 ShopRiskDiagnosisResult 对象，包含各类风险商品数量（TRO 风险 troProdCnt、重复投诉 repeatedComplaintProdCnt、高频投诉 highFreqComplaintProdCnt、禁限售描述违规 forbidDescriptionRiskProdCnt、违规待办超时 toRectifyTaskCnt、欺诈订单 fraudOrderCnt）、对应检测时间及后台处理跳转链接 aiAutoRaiseUrl，供生成三段式风险概览报告。
